docs.title: Home
docs.text:
GASPALS is a character template. It starts from the Game Animation Sample (GASP): motion matching locomotion, traversal and the sample's characters. On top of that it adds overlay layering in the style of the Advanced Locomotion System (ALS): the character holds a rifle, a torch or a box while every locomotion animation keeps playing underneath. Around that core sit the systems most third- and first-person games need: a camera system, cover, equipment, first person with aim down sights, ragdoll and takedowns. Every system runs on both movement back ends (Mover and the Character Movement Component) and works in multiplayer.

Everything is a Blueprint inside one content plugin, mounted as /GASPALS. There is no C++ module to compile.

docs.title: GASPALS
docs.text:
Epic's Game Animation Sample, extended with ALS-style overlay layering and a set of modular, networked gameplay systems. Unreal Engine 5.8, Blueprint only.

Get started Tutorials Reference

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Motion matching locomotion

    The Game Animation Sample's motion matching on two pawns: one on Mover with Network Prediction, one on the Character Movement Component. Walk, run, sprint, crouch, strafe, slide, jump and traversal.

    Mover and CMC pawns

  • Overlay layering

    ALS-style overlay poses blended per body part with curves, on top of motion matching. Item and stance poses, three body styles, aim sweeps and hand IK.

    Overlay system

  • Cover

    Soft cover by walking into walls, sticky cover on a button, cover run to the crosshair, corner turns, vault over cover, and aim from cover that picks the least exposed pose.

    Cover system

  • First person

    True first person on the full body, generated at runtime from your third-person meshes. Three modes, aim down sights, first-person overlays, and per-character eye offsets.

    First person system

  • Equipment

    Data-driven items: a data asset per item links the overlay poses, the attach sockets and the actor to spawn. Rifle, pistol, bow, torch, binoculars, box and barrel included. Selection menu and hand IK.

    Equipment system

  • Camera

    Gameplay Cameras with a Blueprint camera director: third person with three distances, first person, top-down and side-scroller, shoulder swap, crouch and cover offsets, crosshair and aim ray.

    Camera system

  • Ragdoll and interactions

    Networked ragdoll with get-up animations, takedowns and shoves between characters, and demo tools to shoot and spawn characters.

    Ragdoll and interactions

  • Retargeted characters

    Manny, Quinn and the MetaHuman Kellan run every system through runtime retargeting from the animation skeleton. Add your own character with an IK Retargeter and a few settings.

    Characters and visual overrides

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.8.
  • No C++. The plugin has no code module; a Blueprint-only project can use it.
  • Engine plugins used by the content are listed in GASPALS.uplugin and are enabled with it.
  • Project settings: a few settings live in the project's config files (collision channels, data-driven console variables, navigation). Installation lists them and gives the lines to copy.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
These pages explain how GASPALS works, so you can change it with confidence.

Page Read it to understand Architecture The pawn, the system components, the interfaces between them, initialization and the per-frame data flow. Mover and CMC pawns The two movement back ends, how they differ, and which to build on. Animation pipeline How motion matching, overlay layering, aim offset, IK and cover lowering combine into the final pose. Characters and visual overrides How one animation skeleton drives Manny, Quinn, a MetaHuman or your own character. Networking What each system replicates and the patterns to follow.

docs.title: Animation pipeline
docs.text:
Each pawn runs one character Anim Blueprint. It is the Game Animation Sample's motion matching Anim Blueprint with GASPALS layering added: overlay poses blended per body part on top of locomotion, an aim offset, procedural IK and cover lowering.

Anim Blueprint Used by /GASPALS/Blueprints/SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP SandboxCharacter_Mover /GASPALS/Blueprints/SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP SandboxCharacter_CMC

Both are animated on the UEFN mannequin skeleton. Other characters (Manny, Quinn, the MetaHuman Kellan, or your own) copy or retarget that pose; see Characters and visual overrides.

docs.title: The pose, step by step
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    MM[Locomotion<br>motion matching or hybrid] --> LB
    OP[Overlay pose layer<br>ALI_OverlayPose] --> LB
    OB[Overlay body layer<br>ALI_OverlayBody] --> LB
    LB[ABP_LayerBlending<br>per-bone blends by curves] --> AO[Additive leans<br>and aim offset]
    AO --> Slot[DefaultSlot<br>montages: traversal, interactions, get-up]
    Slot --> Root[Offset root bone]
    Root --> Proc[Procedural layers<br>foot placement, leg IK, hand IK, full body IK]
    Proc --> Hist[Pose history<br>for motion matching]
    Hist --> Cover[CR_Humanoid_CoverLower<br>cover lowering]
    Cover --> Out((Output pose))

  1. Locomotion. Two locomotion setups exist, selected per pawn by a console variable:

    • Full motion matching: the motion matching node picks frames from the pose search databases to match the character's trajectory.
    • State machine / blend stack hybrid: a state machine (idle, locomotion and in-air loops, transitions, idle breaks, slide) whose states pick animations with choosers and play them through a blend stack.

    DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover (default 1, hybrid) and DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC (default 0, full motion matching) choose the setup. The result is cached as the locomotion pose. 2. Overlays. Two linked anim layers produce the overlay poses: ALI_OverlayPose (what the hands hold: rifle, torch, box...) and ALI_OverlayBody (the body style: default, masculine, feminine). The Blueprints that implement them are linked at runtime by the overlay and equipment systems. Inertialization smooths the switch when a new layer is linked. 3. Layer blending. ABP_LayerBlending (a linked anim graph) blends the overlays onto the locomotion pose bone chain by bone chain: legs, pelvis, spine, head, each arm and hand, in local or mesh space, as additive or override. The weights come from curves on the overlay animations, so each overlay pose decides how much of the body it takes over (see below). 4. Leans and aim offset. Additive leans from the lateral acceleration, then the aim offset layer turns the spine toward the aim direction. 5. Montages. The DefaultSlot plays montages: traversal, takedowns and shoves, ragdoll get-ups. 6. Root and procedural. The offset root bone keeps the feet planted while the capsule turns. The procedural layers run foot placement and leg IK, the hand IK Control Rig (CR_Humanoid_HandIK), and on the Mover pawn a full-body IK pass for character interactions. 7. Pose history records the final pose for motion matching's next search. 8. Cover lowering. CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis in cover. It runs last so it acts on the final pose.

The Mover and CMC Anim Blueprints differ in the procedural part: the Mover one splits it into Procedural_PreLayering, Procedural_Feet (the CR_Biped_FootPlacement Control Rig) and Procedural_FullBody; the CMC one runs a single Procedural layer with the Foot Placement node and leg IK.

docs.title: Layering curves
docs.text:
Overlay animations carry curves that say how strongly each body part follows the overlay. The pose Anim Blueprints write them from a curve map on each pose (see Overlay system), and ABP_LayerBlending reads them:

Curve Effect layering_legs, layering_pelvis How much the overlay drives the legs and pelvis. 0 keeps the locomotion legs. layering_spine, layering_spine_add Spine override and additive weight. layering_head, layering_head_add Head override and additive weight. layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r Arm weight. layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add Additive arm weight (arm swing kept on top). layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls Local-space arm weight. Below 1 the arm blends in mesh space, so it keeps its orientation while the spine moves. layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r Hand (finger) weight. enable_handik_l, enable_handik_r Hand IK weight toward the item's IK sockets. enable_cr_aimoffset, disable_cr_aimoffset_pitch, disable_cr_aimoffset_yaw Aim offset Control Rig on or off, and per axis.

A rifle ready pose, for example, takes the spine, arms and hands fully (layering_* = 1), keeps the head free, and turns the left hand IK on so the support hand stays on the handguard.

docs.title: Aim offset and weapon aim
docs.text:
When the character aims, the upper body follows the aim direction in two steps:

  1. The aim rotation (the control rotation for the local player) is smoothed in the character Anim Blueprint with a critically damped spring. The smoothed value drives the spine aim offset.
  2. In the overlay Anim Blueprint, the aim pitch is mapped to 0..1 and blends the weapon's aim sweep animations, which raise and lower the arms.

The camera has no rotation smoothing of its own, so any body lag shows against the crosshair. The smoothing is therefore short for the player you control and longer for remote copies, where the aim arrives in network steps.

Setting Asset (category GASPALS > Anim > Aim / Overlay > Aim) Default Aim Smoothing Time Local Both character Anim Blueprints 0.04 s Aim Smoothing Time Remote Both character Anim Blueprints 0.2 s Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local ABP_OverlayPose_Base and every ABP_Overlay_<Item> 30 Aim Sweep Interp Speed Remote The same 10

With the defaults the aim offset trails the mouse by about 1.4 degrees on average while turning at a steady rate. A sweep speed of 0 snaps the arm pitch.

New overlay children

Variables added to ABP_OverlayPose_Base do not reach the class defaults of existing children. When you create an ABP_Overlay_<Item> by duplicating an existing one, the values come along; when you add a new setting to the base, set it on every child.

docs.title: Legs and foot placement
docs.text:
The overlay legs are blended in (layering_legs, layering_pelvis), so carry and ready stances such as the rifle's bent-knee stance show in the legs. Foot placement then plants the feet:

  • Mover pawn: CR_Biped_FootPlacement (Control Rig). Its leg IK measures the leg bone lengths from the posed skeleton every frame, so skeletons with scaled leg bones (the UEFN mannequin's thighs and calves carry a 1.12 scale) keep their real leg length.
  • CMC pawn: the engine's Foot Placement node, then leg IK.

On the Mover pawn, DDCvar.FootPlacementMode selects the foot placement method (0 off, 1 foot placement node, 2 biped Control Rig). To keep the locomotion legs for an overlay, lower its layering_legs and layering_pelvis curves.

docs.title: Threads and update order
docs.text: The Anim Blueprints use the thread-safe update (BlueprintThreadSafeUpdateAnimation): the game thread only copies the pawn's state (Update_PropertiesFromCharacter, which reads Get_PropertiesForAnimation from the pawn through BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn), and the worker thread computes the rest. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable (default on) selects the path; GASPALS' overlay Anim Blueprints read it once at start and run their update on exactly one of the two paths.

docs.title: Console variables that change the animation
docs.text:
Variable Default Effect DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover 1 Mover Anim Blueprint: 0 full motion matching, 1 state machine / blend stack hybrid. DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC 0 CMC Anim Blueprint: 0 full motion matching (work in progress), 1 hybrid. DDCVar.ExperimentalStateMachine.Enable false Experimental state machine path of the CMC Anim Blueprint. DDCvar.MMDatabaseLOD 0 Pose search databases: 0 dense, 1 sparse, 2 extreme sparse (cheaper, less precise). DDCvar.FootPlacementMode 1 Mover Anim Blueprint: 0 off, 1 foot placement node, 2 biped Control Rig. DDCvar.OffsetRootBone.TranslationRadius 0 How far the root bone may drift from the capsule. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable true Thread-safe animation update.

The full list, with what reads each one, is in Console variables.

docs.title: First person
docs.text: First person uses its own Anim Blueprint (ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN) on generated first-person meshes. It copies the third-person pose and adds camera, aim down sights and arm aim Control Rigs. See First person system.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
GASPALS is built from three layers:

  1. The pawn owns movement, input and the meshes, and exposes its state through an interface.
  2. System components (camera, cover, equipment, first person, overlay, ragdoll, traversal, debug tools) sit on the pawn. Each one is self-contained: it reads what it needs from the pawn and its own settings, and handles its own input actions.
  3. Anim Blueprints pull the pawn's state every frame and turn it into a pose, with layers linked in by the systems.
flowchart TB
    subgraph Framework
        GM[GM_Sandbox<br>pawn and character lists] --- PC[PC_Sandbox<br>pawn switch, teleport]
    end
    subgraph PawnBox[Pawn: SandboxCharacter_Mover / _CMC]
        Move[Movement<br>CharacterMover or CMC]
        Meshes[UEFN mesh, first-person logic mesh,<br>VisualOverride child actor]
        Systems[System components<br>Camera, Cover, Equipment, FirstPerson,<br>Overlay, Traversal, Ragdoll, VisualOverride]
        Iface[BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn<br>Get_PropertiesForAnimation / Camera / Traversal]
    end
    ABP[Character Anim Blueprint] -->|pull every frame| Iface
    Director[Camera director] -->|pull every frame| Iface
    Systems -->|link anim layers,<br>attach items| ABP
    Systems -->|read state| Iface
    GM -->|spawns| PawnBox

docs.title: The pawns
docs.text:
Pawn Base class Movement SandboxCharacter_Mover Pawn Mover (CharacterMoverComponent) with Network Prediction; physics-based ragdoll (Physics Control), takedowns and shoves, debug tools SandboxCharacter_CMC Character Character Movement Component; ragdoll through AC_RagdollSystem

The pawns offer the same features; they differ in how movement, prediction and replication work. See Mover and CMC pawns.

Each pawn has:

  • a UEFN mannequin mesh running the character Anim Blueprint (the animation source for every character);
  • a hidden first-person logic mesh (SkeletalMesh_FP) running the first-person Anim Blueprint;
  • a VisualOverride Child Actor component for retargeted characters;
  • a Gameplay Camera component (and a legacy spring arm camera used only when Gameplay Cameras are turned off);
  • a Motion Warping component for traversal;
  • the system components below.

docs.title: System components
docs.text:
Component System Initialized with AC_OverlaySystem Overlay poses and body styles the third-person mesh AC_EquipmentSystem Items in hand pawn, third- and first-person meshes, the visual meshes to attach to AC_CameraSystem Perspective, camera attachment, crosshair pawn, visual meshes, Gameplay Camera component AC_RagdollSystem Ragdoll (CMC pawn) pawn, mesh, capsule PhysicsControl, AC_PostABPTick Physical animation and ragdoll strengths (Mover pawn) (set up by the pawn at BeginPlay) AC_DebugTools Demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly (Mover pawn) (reads its owner when used) AC_FirstPersonRendering First-person meshes and visibility (builds itself from its settings) AC_CoverSystem_Mover / _CMC Cover pawn AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer Vault, hurdle, mantle (reads the pawn on every attempt) AC_VisualOverrideManager Visible character (reads the game mode's list) AC_SmartObjectAnimation Using benches and other smart objects (interaction range, box size and object types under GASPALS > Interaction > Trace) (finds the movement component) AC_FoleyEvents Footstep and movement sounds (called by animation notifies)

Components that react to input bind their own input actions (AC_CameraSystem handles the perspective keys, AC_EquipmentSystem the equipment menu, and so on), so adding a component adds its controls. They only receive input when the pawn is player controlled.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
Systems are initialized by the pawn, through the interface BPI_ModularSystems and its event InitializeModularSystems. The pawn calls it at the end of BeginPlay, and AC_VisualOverrideManager calls it again whenever the visible character changes, because the meshes change.

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Pawn
    participant FP as AC_FirstPersonRendering
    participant O as AC_OverlaySystem
    participant E as AC_EquipmentSystem
    participant C as AC_CameraSystem
    participant R as AC_RagdollSystem (CMC)
    participant Cv as AC_CoverSystem
    P->>FP: UpdateFirstPersonVisuals (connect logic mesh, build FP meshes)
    P->>O: InitializeSystem(mesh)
    P->>E: InitializeSystem(pawn, meshes, visual meshes)
    P->>C: InitializeSystem(pawn, visual meshes, camera)
    P->>R: InitializeSystem(pawn, mesh, capsule)
    P->>FP: InitializePrimitives
    P->>Cv: InitializeSystem(pawn)
    P->>Cv: bind OnCoverVaultReady → traversal

Because the event can run several times, every InitializeSystem is written to be safe to call again. Follow the same rule in your own systems.

When a player possesses the pawn, a client RPC runs SetupCamera (activates the Gameplay Camera for the player controller) and SetupInput (adds every mapping context of Input Mapping Contexts, default IMC_Sandbox).

docs.title: Per-frame data flow
docs.text:
Data is pulled. The pawn implements BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn with getters that assemble its state into structs:

Getter Struct Read by Get_PropertiesForAnimation S_CharacterPropertiesForAnimation: input state, movement state and mode, stance, rotation mode, gait, direction, transform, velocity, acceleration, aim rotation, ground, in cover... Character Anim Blueprints, overlay and first-person Anim Blueprints, cover, the bow Get_PropertiesForCamera S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera: perspective, style, mode (free, strafe, aim), shoulder, stance Camera director Get_PropertiesForTraversal S_CharacterPropertiesForTraversal: capsule, mesh, motion warping, mode, gait, speed AC_TraversalLogic Get_PropertiesForRagdoll, Get_MMIResult, Get_MMIAnimContexts Ragdoll and interaction data Mover Anim Blueprint (implemented by the Mover pawn)

The Anim Blueprints copy the struct on the game thread (Update_PropertiesFromCharacter) and compute the pose on a worker thread.

Writes go the other way through layer linking: the overlay and equipment systems call LinkAnimClassLayers on the meshes to swap the Anim Blueprints that implement the overlay layers (ALI_OverlayPose, ALI_OverlayBody, ALI_OverlayFirstPerson).

docs.title: Input to movement
docs.text:
Mover pawnCMC pawn

Input actions set the pawn's input state (PlayerInputState: wants to sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch). Each frame, Mover calls the pawn's ProduceInput, which builds the input command: move direction (after the cover system's remap), cover data from EvaluateCover, control rotation, gait, rotation mode, crouch request. Mover then simulates the movement modes with that command on the owner and the server, and the pawn caches the simulated result for animation and camera (CacheInputsFromMover).

Input actions set CharacterInputState and add movement input. AC_PreCMCTick runs the pawn's pre-movement update before the Character Movement Component each frame: cover (UpdateCoverCMC), rotation and the speed settings for the current gait. The CMC then moves the character and replicates it as usual.

docs.title: Game framework
docs.text:
Class Role GM_Sandbox Game mode. Default pawn SandboxCharacter_CMC; Pawn Classes Soft (CMC, Mover) cycled by DDCvar.PawnClass; Visual Overrides Soft (Kellan, Manny, Quinn) cycled by DDCvar.VisualOverride. Respawns all players in place when the pawn class changes. GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll Child of GM_Sandbox for RagdollLevel; spawns SandboxCharacter_Mover. PC_Sandbox Player controller: next pawn (N), next character (M), teleport (J; through the pawn's AC_DebugTools when it has one); hides the touch joystick when a gamepad is used.

There is no global game mode in the project settings: each level sets it in its World Settings.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text: You want to Do this Use GASPALS as your game's base Start from the template or copy the plugin; see Use GASPALS in your own project. Change a pawn's behavior Make a child Blueprint of a sample pawn and override functions, or edit the sample. Use the systems on another pawn Add the systems to your own pawn. Add an item or overlay Data assets and child Anim Blueprints: Add an equipment item, Add an overlay state. Show another character Add a retargeted character.

docs.title: Characters and visual overrides
docs.text:
Every GASPALS pawn is animated on one skeleton: the UEFN mannequin. The motion matching databases, overlay poses, traversal montages and Control Rigs are all built for it. To show a different character, GASPALS does not re-author any of that: it hides the mannequin and puts a visual override on top, a separate actor whose meshes copy the mannequin's pose through an IK Retargeter, every frame.

The template ships three visual overrides:

Character Blueprint Skeleton Retargeter Manny BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny SK_Mannequin (UE5) RTG_UEFN_to_UE5_Mannequin Quinn BP_RetargetedCharacter_Quinn SK_Mannequin (UE5) RTG_UEFN_to_UE5_Mannequin Kellan (MetaHuman) BP_RetargetedCharacter_Kellan metahuman_base_skel RTG_UEFN_to_Metahuman_nrw

All are in /GASPALS/Blueprints/RetargetedCharacters and derive from BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base.

In the demo, press M to cycle: UEFN mannequin, Kellan, Manny, Quinn, and back.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Pawn[Pawn: SandboxCharacter_Mover or _CMC]
        UEFN[Hidden UEFN mesh<br>character Anim Blueprint<br>motion matching, overlays, IK]
        FPLogic[Hidden UEFN first-person<br>logic mesh]
        CA[Child Actor component<br>VisualOverride]
        Mgr[AC_VisualOverrideManager]
    end
    subgraph Visual[Visual override actor]
        Body[SkeletalMesh<br>ABP_Retarget_*]
        Cloth[Clothing, face, hair]
        FPR[AC_FirstPersonRendering<br>first-person meshes]
    end
    Mgr -->|spawns class| CA --> Visual
    UEFN -->|RetargetPoseFromMesh| Body
    Body -->|leader pose or<br>post-process copy| Cloth
    FPLogic -->|first-person overlay<br>retarget| FPR
  1. The pawn keeps its UEFN mannequin mesh. It runs the full character Anim Blueprint and all gameplay animation. When a visual override is active, it is hidden but keeps ticking.
  2. AC_VisualOverrideManager (on the pawn) holds the override class in its replicated VisualOverride variable. When it changes, ApplyVisualOverride sets the class on the pawn's VisualOverride Child Actor component, hides every skeletal mesh of the pawn, and re-runs InitializeModularSystems so every system picks up the new meshes.
  3. The override actor has a body mesh (SkeletalMesh) running a small retarget Anim Blueprint (ABP_Retarget_UE5, ABP_Retarget_Kellan): a Retarget Pose From Mesh node reading the parent skeletal mesh (the pawn's hidden mannequin), then the hand IK Control Rig. Clothing follows the body by leader pose, or by its own post-process Anim Blueprint for meshes on another skeleton (the MetaHuman hoodie and shoes).
  4. First person builds its meshes from the override's own AC_FirstPersonRendering, and retargets the first-person overlay pose from the pawn's hidden first-person logic mesh with First Person Retargeter.

The override body ticks after the pawn mesh (the base class adds a tick prerequisite), so the retargeted pose is never a frame behind.

docs.title: Which meshes the systems use
docs.text:
The pawn function GetVisualMeshes returns the visible third-person mesh and the first-person lead mesh: the override's meshes when one is active, the pawn's own otherwise. The systems are initialized like this:

System Works on Overlay (anim layers) The pawn's UEFN mesh. The override gets the overlay through retargeting. Equipment Links the overlay layers on the pawn's UEFN meshes; attaches the items to the visual meshes (sockets overlay_*) and computes hand IK in the visual mesh's hand bones. Camera Attaches to the visual meshes: root in third person, the VB Camera virtual bone in first person. Cover, traversal, ragdoll The pawn (capsule, movement, UEFN mesh). The override shows the result. First person The override's own AC_FirstPersonRendering.

Ragdoll simulates on the pawn's UEFN mesh with its physics asset; the override needs no physics asset for it.

docs.title: Choosing the character
docs.text:
The list of overrides is on the game mode, not on the pawn: GM_Sandbox > Visual Overrides Soft (soft class references), in this order by default: Kellan, Manny, Quinn.

The data-driven console variable DDCvar.VisualOverride selects the entry for every pawn in the world:

Value Character -1 (project default) No override: the UEFN mannequin. 0, 1, 2... The entry at that index in Visual Overrides Soft.

M (IA_NextVisualOverride) asks the server (PC_Sandbox.NextVisualOverride, then GM_Sandbox.CycleVisualOverride) to add one to the variable, wrapping back to -1. You can also type DDCvar.VisualOverride 1 in the console. The value lasts for the editor session, so it carries over between Play sessions.

To start with a given character, set the variable's default in Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars.

docs.title: Per pawn
docs.text:
Each pawn's AC_VisualOverrideManager has two settings (GASPALS > Characters > General, editable per instance):

Setting Default Use Follow Global Visual Override true Use GM_Sandbox's list and DDCvar.VisualOverride as above. Off: the pawn always uses Default Visual Override and ignores M. Default Visual Override None (UEFN mannequin) The character this pawn uses when it does not follow the global selection, or when the game mode is not GM_Sandbox or the console variable is missing.

Use it for pawns with a fixed look (an NPC that is always Kellan), or to use the characters in your own game mode.

Requirements of the manager

  • The global selection needs GM_Sandbox (or a child) and the DDCvar.VisualOverride variable (copy the project settings from Installation). Without them the pawn uses its Default Visual Override.
  • Setting Visual Override on the manager component in a pawn's Details panel does nothing by itself: the override is applied when the value replicates, not from a default.

docs.title: Requirements for a character
docs.text:
Requirement Why An IK Retargeter from IK_UEFN_Mannequin to the character's IK Rig, with a Curve Remap op Third-person pose and first-person overlays. The curve op carries the hand IK curves. A VB Camera virtual bone from root to head First-person camera. root, head, hand_l, hand_r bones Camera attachment, first-person head, equipment hand IK. UE-standard spine, clavicle and neck names (spine_01..spine_05, clavicle_l/r, neck_01) The first-person overlay Control Rigs. Other skeletons can use the TrueFirstPerson mode. The seven overlay_* sockets on the Skeleton Where equipment is attached: overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_box, overlay_barrel, overlay_binoculars, overlay_torch.

The UE5 mannequin and MetaHuman skeletons in the plugin already have the virtual bone and the sockets. The step-by-step guide is Add a retargeted character.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: One IK retarget costs about 0.16 ms per character (measured in the editor). First person adds a second retarget for the overlay and keeps the hidden first-person logic mesh ticking. The visible body mesh only animates when rendered.

docs.title: Characters on the UEFN skeleton
docs.text: A character that is itself on the UEFN skeleton (another outfit for the mannequin) needs no retargeting: ABP_CopyPose_UEFN copies the pose with Copy Pose From Mesh instead. Its Copy Curves option is on, so the hand IK curves reach the character. Keep it on if you make your own copy-pose Anim Blueprint; with it off, the hand IK curves read 0.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Every GASPALS system works on a listen server with clients. This page summarizes what replicates and how, so you can extend the systems without breaking it. Blueprint-only replication follows a few patterns, used throughout.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
Owner predicts, server confirms. The owning client applies a change immediately, then tells the server with a reliable Server RPC. The server sets a replicated variable, and other machines apply it in its RepNotify. Equipment, overlays and the camera perspective work this way.

Movement goes through the movement component. On the Mover pawn, anything that affects movement is part of the input command the owner sends: cover data, crouch, gait, ragdoll requests. Mover simulates it on the owner and the server and replays it on simulated proxies, so no extra replication is needed. On the CMC pawn, the owner shapes its acceleration, which the CMC replicates (p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1), and extra state travels in RPCs and replicated variables.

Montages play where they must. Root-motion montages (traversal, interactions, get-ups) are played on the server and the owner. Mover syncs a server-played montage to simulated proxies; the CMC replicates root-motion montages itself.

Cosmetics on every machine. Visual reactions (ragdoll physics profiles, sounds, first-person visibility) run on every machine from replicated state or mode changes, not from RPCs.

docs.title: By system
docs.text: System What replicates How Locomotion (Mover) Movement, crouch, gait, rotation mode Mover input commands with Network Prediction (DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini). Simulated proxies get the inputs (bSyncInputsForSimProxy). Locomotion (CMC) Movement, crouch The CMC. The input state (CharacterInputState) is sent to the server with an RPC and replicated to others. Cover (Mover) Cover state Part of the Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover). Cover (CMC) Cover state, facing Owner-shaped acceleration, plus a 20 Hz server RPC (ServerUpdateCover) and replicated cover state applied on other machines. Aim from cover Result only Runs on the owner; others see position, crouch and facing. Equipment Selected item Replicated with RepNotify; every machine spawns the item locally. Client sends a reliable Server RPC. Overlay Overlay pose and body Replicated with RepNotify; reliable Server RPC from clients. Camera Perspective Server RPC; replicated to other machines (skip owner). Style and shoulder are local. First person Nothing Owner-only meshes; other players see the third-person character. Traversal The traversal action Owner predicts, reliable Server RPC with the result, server plays it; Mover and CMC sync the montage to others. The server does not replay it for a pawn it controls locally, so a listen-server host, a standalone player or a server AI starts each traversal once. Ragdoll (CMC) Start and stop Reliable Server RPC, then a reliable multicast. Ragdoll (Mover pawn) Enter, exit, roll, get-up choice Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Ragdoll), with the injury state replicated. Remote ragdolls are pulled toward the replicated capsule. Takedowns, shoves The interaction Client predicts its own montage and asks the server, which validates and multicasts. Visual override The character class Replicated with RepNotify on the manager component. Pawn switch The pawn class Server RPC from the controller; the game mode respawns players.

docs.title: Testing multiplayer
docs.text:
1. In the Play options, set Number of Players to 2 and Net Mode to Play As Listen Server.
  2. Test on both pawns (N), since they replicate differently.
  3. Watch the client and the server windows: equipment, overlays, cover, traversal and ragdoll should look the same on both.
  4. For the Mover pawn, np.PrintReconciles 1 prints prediction corrections. A handful at events like a takedown is expected; continuous corrections are not.
  5. Use Network Emulation (in the editor's Play settings) with some latency and packet loss to see how the prediction holds up.

docs.title: Rules for your own additions
docs.text:
• Mover: change movement only through the input command and transitions. QueueNextMode from gameplay code runs on one machine only.
  • Never call RPCs every frame for continuous state; send it in the movement input (Mover) or at a fixed rate (the CMC cover sends 20 times a second).
  • Components that use RPCs or replicated variables need Component Replicates on the pawn's component.
  • Make cosmetic reactions run from replicated state so late joiners see them too.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The CMC pawn shows small corrections (2 to 4 cm) at sticky cover edge stops and corners.

The camera, traversal, equipment, overlay and visual override components have Component Replicates on in both sample pawns. If you build your own pawn, turn it on for them too.

docs.title: Mover and CMC pawns
docs.text:
GASPALS ships the same character on two movement back ends. Both run the same systems (camera, cover, equipment, first person, overlays, traversal), the same Anim Blueprint design, and both work in multiplayer.

SandboxCharacter_Mover SandboxCharacter_CMC Base class Pawn Character Movement CharacterMoverComponent (Mover 2.0) with Network Prediction CharacterMovementComponent Movement logic Movement modes (Blueprint classes) and transitions Pawn functions before the CMC update (UpdateMovement_PreCMC) Prediction Input commands simulated on owner and server; rollback and resimulation The CMC's client prediction and server corrections Slide Yes (BP_MovementMode_Slide) No Ragdoll Mover Ragdoll mode with a Physics Control component (press X, Space to get up) AC_RagdollSystem (press X) Takedowns and shoves Yes No Debug tools AC_DebugTools (demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly) Teleport only (player controller) Foot placement CR_Biped_FootPlacement Control Rig Foot Placement node and leg IK Default locomotion setup State machine / blend stack hybrid Full motion matching Capsule radius 30, half height 86 radius 40, half height 86 Cover adapter AC_CoverSystem_Mover AC_CoverSystem_CMC Engine status Mover is experimental in 5.8 Production

docs.title: Switching pawns
docs.text:
The game mode spawns the pawn chosen by DDCvar.PawnClass:

Value Pawn (GM_Sandbox) -1 (default) Default Pawn Class: SandboxCharacter_CMC 0 SandboxCharacter_CMC 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover

Press N in game to cycle, or type DDCvar.PawnClass 1 in the console. Every player is respawned in place. GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll (RagdollLevel) uses SandboxCharacter_Mover.

To start a project on the Mover pawn, set the Default Pawn Class of your game mode, or the default of DDCvar.PawnClass to 1.

docs.title: The Mover pawn
docs.text:
Mover splits movement into modes. Each mode is a Blueprint (or native) class registered by name on the CharacterMover component:

Mode name Class Use Walking BP_MovementMode_Walking Ground movement: gait speeds, acceleration, turning. Falling BP_MovementMode_Falling In the air. Flying B_MovementMode_Flying Traversal montages and the debug fly toggle (Z). Sliding BP_MovementMode_Slide Slide. Cover BP_MovementMode_Cover Movement along cover. Traversing native Flying mode Registered, not used. Ragdoll BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll Physics ragdoll (X).

Transitions move between modes (into cover, into and out of a slide, the ragdoll requests). See Movement.

Every frame Mover asks the pawn for an input command (ProduceInput), simulates the modes with it, and on a remote machine replays the same commands. Anything that changes movement must therefore go through the input command: the cover system adds its data to it (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover), the pawn adds its ragdoll enter and exit requests. Changing a mode directly from gameplay code (QueueNextMode) only affects the local machine.

docs.title: The CMC pawn
docs.text:
The CMC pawn is a classic Character. Its movement settings are changed every frame before the Character Movement Component runs, from the pawn's gait (walk, run, sprint, crouch) and direction:

Speeds (forward, strafe, backward) Value Walk Speeds 200, 180, 150 Run Speeds 500, 350, 300 Sprint Speeds 700, 700, 700 Crouch Speeds 225, 200, 180

AC_PreCMCTick makes this update (and the cover update) run after the controller and before the CMC. The CMC pawn starts with strafing on.

docs.title: Which one to build on
docs.text:
• CMC if you want the mature, well-documented Character pipeline and the widest compatibility with marketplace content.
  • Mover if you want the newer movement framework: modular modes, deterministic prediction and rollback, and an easier path to custom movement such as wall running or climbing. Mover is still experimental in UE 5.8, so expect engine changes.

Both pawns are kept at feature parity in GASPALS, so systems you add should be tested on both.

docs.title: Ragdoll, interactions and debug tools
docs.text: The Mover pawn is also a physics-driven character: a Physics Control component (kinematic by default, physical animation optional), a Ragdoll movement mode with get-up animations, and takedowns and shoves between characters. See Ragdoll and interactions. Its AC_DebugTools component adds the sandbox's demo and debug tools (shoot into ragdoll, spawn or rotate characters, teleport, fly); see Debug tools. These work in every game mode; RagdollLevel is set up to try them.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text: The pawn variables, functions and interfaces are listed in Pawns and Anim Blueprints, and the movement modes in Movement modes.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
• Installation

    Open the template project, or add the plugin to your project with the settings it needs.

  • Quick start

    A ten-minute tour of every feature in the demo levels.

  • Controls

    Every key and gamepad button, per pawn.

  • Project tour

    Where the pawns, systems, animations and levels live.

After that, read Architecture to see how the pieces connect, then pick a tutorial.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: The pawns add one input mapping context when a player possesses them: IMC_Sandbox (/GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox, priority 0), the only mapping context in the plugin. Every control below comes from it, except the debug flying key. The input actions (IA_*) are in /GASPALS/Input. In DefaultLevel, the input wall (BP_InputWall) shows the same mappings.

These work on SandboxCharacter_Mover in every level; RagdollLevel has target characters and physics obstacles to try them on. The demo shot, spawn and rotate come from the pawn's debug tools; see Debug tools.

docs.text:
Action Key Notes Next pawn N Cycles the pawn class (CMC and Mover in DefaultLevel) and respawns every player in place. Next character M Cycles the visual override: UEFN mannequin, Kellan, Manny, Quinn. Teleport J Teleports the pawn to the point you look at (up to 100 m). On the Mover pawn it goes through its debug tools (Teleport Max Distance on AC_DebugTools). Debug flying Z Mover pawn: toggles a flying mode (debug tools). docs.title: Change the controls
docs.text: Edit IMC_Sandbox, or create your own mapping context with the same input actions and list it in the pawn's Input Mapping Contexts (class defaults, GASPALS > Input). The systems listen to the input actions themselves (the cover, camera, equipment and overlay components handle their own actions), so any context that maps the same IA_* assets works. See Add or rebind inputs.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
There are two ways to use GASPALS:

  • Open the template project (GASPALS.uproject). Everything is already configured. Use this to explore the demo, and as the starting point of a new game.
  • Add the plugin to an existing project. Copy the plugin folder, then copy a few project settings that a plugin cannot carry by itself.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Engine Unreal Engine 5.8 Code None. GASPALS is a content plugin with no C++ module; the project can be Blueprint only. Engine plugins Declared in GASPALS.uplugin and enabled automatically with GASPALS (see below). Packaging A C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows). The engine plugins GASPALS uses are not enabled by default, so the packaging tool builds a small game target even for a Blueprint-only project. Running in the editor needs no compiler. Disk space The plugin holds the Game Animation Sample animation set and a MetaHuman, so expect several gigabytes. Engine plugins enabled by GASPALS Area Plugins Animation PoseSearch (motion matching), Chooser, BlendStack, AnimationWarping, MotionWarping, CurveExpression, FullBodyIK, RigLogic, MovieSceneAnimMixer, PhysicsControl Movement Mover, ChaosMover, MoverExamples (Mover brings NetworkPrediction) Interaction and AI GameplayInteractions, SmartObjects, StateTree, GameplayStateTree Characters and UI HairStrands, LiveLink (MetaHuman), ModelViewViewModel, DrawDebugLibrary Editor tools only EditorScriptingUtilities, GeometryScripting

The camera system uses Gameplay Cameras, which is enabled by default in 5.8.

docs.title: Option A: open the template project
docs.text:
1. Get the project folder (it contains GASPALS.uproject, Config/ and Plugins/GASPALS/).
  2. Right-click GASPALS.uproject > Switch Unreal Engine version if it is not associated with 5.8, then open it.
  3. The first launch compiles shaders and builds the motion matching databases. This takes a while once.
  4. The editor opens RagdollLevel. Open /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel for the main demo, then continue with the Quick start.

Development plugins in the template

The template project also enables a few editor-only development plugins (BlueprintAssist and AutoSizeComments for graph formatting, and editor tooling plugins). GASPALS does not need them. If one is missing on your machine, remove its entry from GASPALS.uproject or answer No when the editor offers to disable it.

docs.title: Option B: add GASPALS to your project
1. Copy the plugin
docs.text:
Close the editor, then copy the folder Plugins/GASPALS into your project's Plugins folder (create it if needed):

YourProject/
├── YourProject.uproject
├── Config/
└── Plugins/
    └── GASPALS/
        ├── GASPALS.uplugin
        ├── Content/
        └── Docs/

Open the project. The engine enables GASPALS and the plugins it depends on. In the Content Browser, enable Settings > Show Plugin Content to see the GASPALS Content folder.

docs.title: 2. Copy the project settings
docs.text:
Some settings live in the project's config files, not in the plugin: collision channels and profiles, data-driven console variables, navigation, and a few engine settings. Without them, traversal finds no obstacles, the camera system and the locomotion setup fall back to defaults, and cover runs do not path on clients.

The Project settings reference explains each line. The short version: add these blocks to your project's Config/DefaultEngine.ini (merge with existing sections of the same name).

Also copy these two files from the template's Config/ folder (or merge them if you already have them):

File Contents Needed for DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini Network Prediction settings: independent ticking, interpolated simulated proxies, input send counts. The Mover pawn in multiplayer. DefaultGameplayTags.ini Gameplay tags: Foley.Event.*, MotionMatching.*, SmartObject.*, StateTree.* and redirects. Foley sounds, motion matching database tags, the smart object and NPC demos.

Collision channels after the merge

GASPALS adds four channels in the last slots (ECC_GameTraceChannel15 to 18: Traversable, Mouse, Obstacle, Cover), so they don't take the slots a project fills first. Blueprints store a channel by its position among the custom channels, though, so if your project already has custom channels, open the pawns' components after the merge and pick the channels again by name: Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic), Cover Trace Channel (AC_CoverSystem) and, on the Mover pawn, Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types. The +EditProfiles lines give the engine profiles a Cover response; if your project already edits one of those profiles, add the Cover response to your own line instead (only the first edit of a profile is used). See Project settings.

Rendering settings for the MetaHuman

The demo MetaHuman (Kellan) needs the skinning settings of the template's [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] section: r.GPUSkin.Support16BitBoneIndex=True, r.GPUSkin.UnlimitedBoneInfluences=True, r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True and r.SkinCache.DefaultBehavior=0. Copy them too if you keep Kellan.

docs.title: 3. Packaging settings
docs.text:
In Config/DefaultGame.ini:

Config/DefaultGame.ini
[/Script/Engine.AssetManagerSettings]
+PrimaryAssetTypesToScan=(PrimaryAssetType="GameFeatureData",AssetBaseClass="/Script/GameFeatures.GameFeatureData",bHasBlueprintClasses=False,bIsEditorOnly=False,Directories=((Path="/Game/Unused")),SpecificAssets=,Rules=(Priority=-1,ChunkId=-1,bApplyRecursively=True,CookRule=AlwaysCook))

[/Script/UnrealEd.ProjectPackagingSettings]
+MapsToCook=(FilePath="/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel")

The GameFeatureData entry is required by one of the enabled engine plugins: without it, the cook fails with an unknown cook failure. Replace the map with your own levels.

docs.title: 4. Restart and check
docs.text:
1. Restart the editor so the collision channels and console variables load.
  2. Open /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel and press Play. You control the CMC pawn (press N to switch to the Mover pawn). Run at a low block and press Space to vault: if the character only jumps, the collision channels are not set up (see the warning above).
  3. Set a game mode and default map for your own levels: see Use GASPALS in your own project.

docs.title: Updating GASPALS
docs.text: GASPALS is a template: you are expected to change its assets. To take a newer version later, keep your changes in your own assets where you can (child Blueprints, your own data assets and levels) and replace the plugin folder. Assets you edited inside Plugins/GASPALS need merging by hand.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Quick start: play the demo and try every feature.
  • Controls: every key and gamepad button.
  • Project tour: where things are in the plugin.

docs.title: Project tour
docs.text:
All GASPALS content is in the plugin, mounted as /GASPALS (in the Content Browser: Plugins > GASPALS Content, with Show Plugin Content on). The top level splits in two: Systems holds the GASPALS systems, and the other folders hold the Game Animation Sample foundation they build on.

/GASPALS
├── Systems/              GASPALS systems (one folder each) and shared helpers
├── Blueprints/           pawns, character Anim Blueprints, movement modes, game mode, controller, data
├── Characters/           UEFN mannequin (animation skeleton, all animations), UE5 mannequins
├── MetaHumans/           the MetaHuman Kellan and shared MetaHuman assets
├── Input/                input actions and mapping contexts
├── Levels/               demo levels and the grey-box kit
├── Audio/                foley system and sounds
├── Widgets/              editor panels of the demo (Game Animation Widget, controls, read me)
├── IsolatedExamples/     self-contained examples (look at points of interest)
└── Misc/                 animation curve compression settings

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Each system is a folder with its component, data and assets. They are independent: a pawn uses the ones it needs.

Folder Main assets Page Systems/CameraSystem AC_CameraSystem, CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter, CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter, Rigs/, W_Crosshair Camera Systems/CoverSystem AC_CoverSystem_Base, _Mover, _CMC, W_CoverMarker, enums Cover Systems/EquipmentSystem AC_EquipmentSystem, Data/ (data assets, chooser, enum), Actors/, UI/ Equipment Systems/FirstPersonSystem AC_FirstPersonRendering, ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN, CR_FirstPerson_*, Tools/ First person Systems/OverlaySystem AC_OverlaySystem, ABP_LayerBlending, OverlayPose/, OverlayBody/, FirstPerson/, UI/ Overlay Systems/RagdollSystem AC_RagdollSystem (CMC ragdoll) Ragdoll Systems/DebugTools AC_DebugTools (the Mover pawn's demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly) Debug tools Systems/TraversalSystem AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer, BP_TraversalTester Traversal Systems/ (root) BPFL_GASPALS (function library), BPML_GASPALS (macro library), BPI_ModularSystems (initialization interface) Shared reference

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text: Asset or folder What it is SandboxCharacter_Mover, SandboxCharacter_CMC The two pawns. See Mover and CMC pawns. SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP, SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP The character Anim Blueprints. See Animation pipeline. GM_Sandbox, GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll, PC_Sandbox Game modes (pawn and character lists, pawn switching) and the player controller. BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn, BPI_SandboxCharacter_ABP Interfaces between the pawn, its Anim Blueprint and the systems. AC_VisualOverrideManager Spawns the visible character (Manny, Quinn, Kellan). AC_PreCMCTick, AC_PostABPTick Tick-order helpers: run pawn logic before the CMC, or after the Anim Blueprint. MovementModes/ Mover movement modes (Walking, Falling, Flying, Slide, Cover, Ragdoll) and transitions. RetargetedCharacters/ The visual overrides and their retarget Anim Blueprints. ControlRigs/ CR_Biped_FootPlacement, CR_Humanoid_AimOffset, CR_Humanoid_HandIK, CR_Humanoid_LookAt, CR_Humanoid_CoverLower. Data/ Structs and enums shared by the pawns and Anim Blueprints (S_CharacterPropertiesForAnimation, E_Gait...), choosers and curves. AI/ NPC controller and StateTrees. SmartObjects/ Bench smart object and the player's smart object component. AnimNotifies/, AnimModifiers/ Notifies (foley, early transitions, motion warping, ragdoll) and animation modifiers from the Game Animation Sample. Cameras/ An older copy of the camera assets. Nothing references it; the pawns use Systems/CameraSystem.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This tour takes about ten minutes and touches every system. Keys are listed in Controls.

docs.title: 1. Open the demo level
docs.text:
Open /GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel and press Play (Alt+P). For a bigger view, use Play > New Editor Window.

You start as the CMC pawn (SandboxCharacter_CMC), shown as the UEFN mannequin. The level is a grey-box sandbox: blocks of many heights, walls for cover, teleporters, a target dummy and an input wall that lists the controls.

docs.title: 2. Move around
docs.text:
• Walk, run (default) and sprint (hold Shift). Stop suddenly, turn around, run in circles: motion matching picks starts, stops, pivots and turns from a large animation set.
  • Toggle walking with Ctrl, crouch with C, strafe with the middle mouse button.
  • Press N to switch to the Mover pawn (SandboxCharacter_Mover). It uses the newer Mover movement with Network Prediction. Sprint, then press C: the Mover pawn slides.

docs.title: 3. Traverse
docs.text: Run at a low block and press Space: the character vaults, hurdles or mantles depending on the block's height and depth. Blocks of the traversable kind (LevelBlock_Traversable) are spread across the level. Try them walking, running and sprinting; the animation adapts.

docs.title: 4. Take cover
docs.text:
• Walk into a wall: the character takes cover and moves along it. Low walls make it crouch.
  • Point the crosshair at a wall and tap Q: a marker shows on the wall and the character snaps to it (sticky cover). Hold Q while aiming at a wall farther away: the character runs there.
  • In sticky cover, hold the move key toward the end of the wall: the character stops at the edge, and walks around an outside corner.
  • Hold Right Button in cover: the character aims from cover, stepping out or standing up only as far as needed to see the target. Release it to go back.
  • Press Space behind low cover to vault over it.

docs.title: 5. Equip items
docs.text:
Hold T. The game slows down and a menu opens. Scroll to Rifle and release. The character holds the rifle with the matching overlay pose on top of all locomotion. Hold Right Button to aim: the arms follow the camera pitch.

Try the other items: pistol, bow (aim to draw), torch, binoculars, box and barrel. Unequip returns to the default pose.

docs.title: 6. Change overlays
docs.text: Hold V for the overlay pose menu (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and B for the overlay body menu (Default, Masculine, Feminine). These change how the body is held, on top of locomotion and items.

docs.title: 7. Cameras
docs.text:
• Press 1 to cycle the perspective: third person, top-down, side-scroller, first person.
  • Press 2 to cycle the camera style (close, medium, far, debug view in third person).
  • Press Alt to switch the shoulder.

In first person, look down: you see your own body. Equip the rifle and aim: the sights line up with the eye.

docs.title: 8. Characters
docs.text: Press M to cycle the visible character: the MetaHuman Kellan, Manny, Quinn, and back to the UEFN mannequin. Everything still works, including first person and equipment: the characters retarget the mannequin's animation at runtime.

docs.title: 9. Ragdoll
docs.text:
• On the CMC pawn, press X to ragdoll and again to recover.
  • On the Mover pawn (N), X ragdolls (Space to get up), Left Button from a standstill near another Mover character does a takedown, E shoves. Hold aim and click to shoot characters, or hold aim and press E to spawn one (the debug tools).
  • Open /GASPALS/Levels/RagdollLevel for the full ragdoll demo: you play the Mover pawn, with target characters and physics obstacles.

docs.title: 10. More levels
docs.text: Level Shows NPCLevel AI characters (both pawns) that walk around and use benches through smart objects and StateTrees. Press E near a bench to sit down yourself. RagdollLevel Ragdoll, physical animation, takedowns and shoves, physics obstacles. LookAtPOI_Level An isolated look-at example: characters that look at points of interest you click.

docs.title: Try multiplayer
docs.text: In the Play options (the three dots next to Play), set Number of Players to 2 and Net Mode to Play As Listen Server. Every system is replicated: equip items, take cover and switch perspectives on the client and watch the other window.

docs.title: Debug views
docs.text: The Game Animation Widget button in DefaultLevel opens an editor panel to change the locomotion setup, camera style, physics profile and debug drawing. The same switches are console variables, listed in Console variables.

docs.title: Console variables
docs.text:
GASPALS uses data-driven console variables: variables declared in Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars (stored in DefaultEngine.ini) that Blueprints read with Get Console Variable Int/Float/Bool Value. Some Blueprints also listen to changes (OnDataDrivenCVarChanged), so typing a new value in the console applies it immediately.

Change one at runtime from the console (`):

DDCvar.PawnClass 1
DDCvar.VisualOverride 0
DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 3

In the editor, the values persist for the editor session (across Play sessions). The demo levels also have an editor panel to set them: press the Game Animation Widget button in DefaultLevel or RagdollLevel to open it (it is an editor utility widget, so it only exists in the editor).

They are project settings

The variables are declared in the project's config, not in the plugin. If a project lacks them, every read returns 0 or false, which silently changes behavior (for example the old spring-arm camera instead of Gameplay Cameras). Copy them as described in Installation.

docs.title: Game setup
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read by Values DDCvar.PawnClass Int -1 GM_Sandbox Index into the game mode's Pawn Classes Soft. -1 (or out of range): the game mode's Default Pawn Class. In GM_Sandbox: -1 and 0 = SandboxCharacter_CMC, 1 = SandboxCharacter_Mover. Changing it respawns every player in place. N cycles it. DDCvar.VisualOverride Int -1 GM_Sandbox, AC_VisualOverrideManager Index into the game mode's Visual Overrides Soft. -1: no override (UEFN mannequin). 0 Kellan, 1 Manny, 2 Quinn. M cycles it. DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable Bool true Both pawns (SetupCamera) true: Gameplay Cameras (CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter and the camera director). false: the old spring arm camera. Read when the pawn is possessed, so restart Play after changing it. DDCvar.CameraStyle Int 1 AC_CameraSystem Third-person camera distance: 0 close, 1 medium, 2 far, 3 debug view. Also picks the top-down and side-scroller rig variant. DDCvar.ControlStyle Int 0 Mover pawn 0 standard, 1 twin stick (gamepad only: left stick moves in world space, right stick aims).

docs.title: Locomotion and animation
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read by Values DDCvar.LocomotionSetupMover Int 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP 0 full motion matching, 1 state machine / blend stack hybrid. DDCvar.LocomotionSetupCMC Int 0 SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP 0 full motion matching (work in progress), 1 hybrid. DDCVar.ExperimentalStateMachine.Enable Bool false SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP Experimental state machine path of the CMC Anim Blueprint. DDCvar.MMDatabaseLOD Int 0 Both character Anim Blueprints Pose search databases: 0 dense, 1 sparse, 2 extreme sparse. Sparser is cheaper and less precise. DDCvar.StrafeStyle Int 1 Mover pawn Directions used while strafing: 0 forward, back, left, right; 1 forward and back; 2 forward only. Also changes when sprint is allowed while strafing. DDCvar.AimStyle Int 0 Mover pawn The same direction sets while aiming. DDCvar.AnalogInputStyle Int 1 Mover pawn 0 single gait (always run); 1 walk or run by stick deflection (run above 0.7). DDCvar.FootPlacementMode Int 1 SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP 0 off, 1 foot placement node, 2 biped Control Rig. DDCvar.OffsetRootBone.TranslationRadius Float 0 Both character Anim Blueprints How far the root bone may drift from the capsule. DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable Bool true Character, layer blending and overlay Anim Blueprints Run the animation update on worker threads. Overlay Anim Blueprints read it once at start. DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile Int 0 SandboxCharacter_Mover Physics profile when not ragdolling: 0 kinematic (default), 1 physical animation (limbs react to contacts but can catch on walls).

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Adapter A small component that connects a shared system core to one movement back end. AC_CoverSystem_Mover and AC_CoverSystem_CMC are the cover adapters. Aim sweep Additive animations that raise and lower a weapon's arms with the aim pitch (AO_<Item>_<Stance>_Sweep). ALS Advanced Locomotion System, a community locomotion framework. GASPALS borrows its overlay layering: per-body-part blending driven by animation curves. Anim layer interface (ALI) An interface of linked animation layers. A character Anim Blueprint calls the layer; another Anim Blueprint that implements the interface is linked at runtime to provide the pose. GASPALS uses ALI_OverlayPose, ALI_OverlayBody and ALI_OverlayFirstPerson. Auto cover (soft cover) Cover taken by walking into a wall, kept while staying close, left by moving away. CMC The Character Movement Component, Unreal's classic character movement. SandboxCharacter_CMC uses it. Component template The copy of a component inside a Blueprint (shown in its Components panel). Its values override the component class defaults for that Blueprint. GASPALS settings are tuned on the pawns' component templates. Cover run Holding the cover button while aiming at distant cover: the character sprints there along a navmesh path and takes sticky cover. Data-driven console variable (DDCVar) A console variable declared in Project Settings (Data Driven CVars) rather than in code. GASPALS uses them for runtime switches and debug drawing. Equipment item Something the character holds: a data asset (DA_Equipment_*), an actor (BP_Equipment_*) and overlay poses. First-person modes TrueFirstPerson (the third-person pose seen from the eyes), FirstPersonOverlay (first-person arm poses on the full body) and FirstPersonOverlaySplit (separate arms and body meshes). Game Animation Sample (GASP) Epic Games' sample project for motion matching locomotion and traversal. GASPALS starts from it. Layering curves Animation curves (layering_*, enable_*) that set how much of each body part an overlay pose takes over. Logic mesh The hidden UEFN mannequin on the pawn. It is animated by the character Anim Blueprint; visible characters copy or retarget its pose. Motion matching Animation selection by searching a database of poses for the frame that best matches the character's current pose and future trajectory (the PoseSearch plugin). Mover Unreal's newer movement component framework with Network Prediction. SandboxCharacter_Mover uses it. Its behavior is split into movement modes (Walking, Falling, Cover, Slide...) and transitions between them. Overlay A pose layered over locomotion: what the hands hold (overlay pose) and the body style (overlay body). Retargeting Transferring animation from one skeleton to another with an IK Rig and IK Retargeter. GASPALS retargets from the UEFN mannequin to Manny, Quinn and MetaHumans at runtime. Sticky cover Cover taken with the cover button. It holds the character to the wall until it is left on purpose. Traversal Vault, hurdle and mantle moves over obstacles, chosen by a chooser table and played as montages with motion warping. UEFN mannequin The mannequin skeleton of Unreal Editor for Fortnite. GASPALS animates on it. Visual override A separate actor that shows a different character on top of the pawn, driven by the pawn's logic mesh. Manny, Quinn and Kellan are visual overrides. VB Camera A virtual bone from root to head that carries the first-person camera position.

docs.title: Input actions
docs.text: Input actions are in /GASPALS/Input, mapped in /GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox (the context the pawns add). "Mover" is SandboxCharacter_Mover, "CMC" is SandboxCharacter_CMC.
