docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
Action Keys Handled by Does IA_NextPawn N PC_Sandbox Next pawn class (server RPC to the game mode). IA_NextVisualOverride M PC_Sandbox Next character. IA_TeleportToTarget J PC_Sandbox; AC_DebugTools on the Mover pawn Teleport to the point under the view (up to 100 m).

The Mover pawn also toggles a debug flying mode with Z (keyboard only, through its AC_DebugTools). This is a raw key node in the Mover pawn's Event Graph, not an input action.

docs.title: Unused
docs.text: Asset Note IA_TwinStick_AimDirection Read by the Mover pawn's twin-stick mode but not mapped.

docs.title: By design
docs.text:
• Blueprint only. No C++ module. Everything can be changed in the editor; nothing needs compiling to run in the editor.
  • One animation skeleton. All animation, overlays, montages and Control Rigs are authored on the UEFN mannequin. Other characters are shown through runtime retargeting (about 0.16 ms per character).
  • Mover is experimental in Unreal Engine 5.8. The Mover pawn may need changes with future engine versions.
  • Pawn features differ slightly: slide, the physics-driven ragdoll, takedowns and shoves, and the debug tools are Mover-only; the simple ragdoll toggle is CMC-only.
  • Demo framework. GM_Sandbox, PC_Sandbox, the menus and the editor widgets are a demo setup, meant to be replaced or extended by your game.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text: System Limitation Cover No peek (lean out without aiming). Pose lowering expects UEFN bone names. Cover runs need a navmesh to avoid obstacles. Small corrections at sticky edge stops on the CMC pawn in multiplayer. First person TrueFirstPerson weapons can clip into walls and lag one frame. Split mode's body receives the hidden body's shadow. Only rifle, pistol and bow have first-person poses. Overlay Stances and item poses share one layer, so they cannot combine. Overlay changes are instant (no transition animation). Equipment Menus change global time dilation (the whole world slows down while one is open). Torch, binoculars, box and barrel have no first-person pose. Camera New styles or modes need chooser rows. Offsets apply in third person only; in first person the camera follows the head, so it lowers when crouching without an offset. Traversal Only the Traversable channel counts. Obstacles under 70 cm wide are jumped. Input Some actions have no gamepad binding. The Mover debug flying toggle is on Z (keyboard only).

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
These are open in the current version:

  • Starting overlay pose: an Overlay Pose set on the pawn's overlay component is replaced at spawn, because the equipment system initializes after the overlay system and links the equipment's pose last (Unequip uses the Default pose). Pick overlays through the menu or Select|NewOverlayPose after the pawn has spawned.
  • Unused animation: OverlaySystem/Transitions/Stand_Transition is kept in the plugin but nothing plays it.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text: A plugin carries content, not project configuration. These settings live in the project's Config/*.ini files. The template project has them all; a project that adds the GASPALS plugin needs to copy them. The copy-ready block is in Installation.

docs.title: Collision
docs.text: Project Settings > Engine > Collision. Stored in DefaultEngine.ini, section [/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile].

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Slot Name Kind Default response Used for ECC_GameTraceChannel15 Traversable Trace Ignore Traversal finds obstacles to vault, hurdle and mantle with this channel. Level geometry that should be traversable blocks it. ECC_GameTraceChannel16 Mouse Trace Ignore Mouse click traces of the look-at example level (PC_LookAtPOI). The GASPALS systems do not trace it (the fixed-camera cursor aim uses Visibility). ECC_GameTraceChannel17 Obstacle Object Ignore Moving obstacles of the physics obstacle course in RagdollLevel; the Ragdoll profile blocks it. ECC_GameTraceChannel18 Cover Trace Block What counts as cover: every cover probe (wall search, sticky entry, cover height, aim edges, the cover target under the crosshair) traces it. Every collision profile answers it like Visibility; set an object to Ignore Cover to keep it from being cover.

GASPALS uses the last four slots so that projects whose own channels start at slot 1 can merge the settings without a clash.

Channels in Blueprints are stored by position

A Blueprint stores a trace channel as TraceTypeQueryN, where N counts the custom trace channels in slot order (Visibility and Camera are 1 and 2). In this project Traversable is TraceTypeQuery3, Mouse 4 and Cover 5; Obstacle is ObjectTypeQuery7. If your project already has custom channels, these numbers shift after the merge: open the pawn's components and pick the channels again by name in Traversable Trace Channel (AC_TraversalLogic) and Cover Trace Channel (AC_CoverSystem), and the obstacle types in Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types on the Mover pawn. Object types set on components with a Custom collision setup are also stored by slot.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Profile Object type Notes TraversalObjectPreset WorldDynamic Blocks everything, including Traversable. Use it on meshes the character can vault, hurdle or mantle. The demo levels use the LevelBlock_Traversable Blueprint instead, which sets the same response on its mesh. ObstaclePreset Obstacle Moving obstacles of the obstacle course: ignores world, pawns and camera; blocks the Ragdoll profile. CharacterCapsule Pawn Capsule of the Mover pawn: ignores Visibility, Camera and Cover, so the camera, visibility and cover traces pass through characters. The CMC pawn's capsule uses a custom setup with the same responses. Ragdoll (edited) PhysicsBody The engine profile, edited to ignore Camera and Cover and block Obstacle. Engine profiles (edited) Pawn, Spectator, CharacterMesh, Trigger, InvisibleWall, InvisibleWallDynamic, NoCollision, WaterBodyCollision ignore Cover; OverlapAll and OverlapAllDynamic overlap it, the same as their Visibility response.

Custom collision and the Cover channel

Components with a Custom collision setup store their own responses, and a new channel takes its default response (Block). Triggers or volumes that ignore Visibility should ignore Cover too, or they block cover probes. The GASPALS content is already set up this way.

docs.title: Data-driven console variables
docs.text:
Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars. Section [/Script/Engine.DataDrivenConsoleVariableSettings].

These are console variables declared by the project, which Blueprints read with Get Console Variable * Value and can react to when they change. GASPALS uses them for runtime switches (camera style, pawn class, character) and debug drawing. If they are missing, the reads return 0 or false, which changes behavior silently: for example DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable false switches the pawns to the old spring-arm camera, and DDCVar.ThreadSafeAnimationUpdate.Enable false moves the animation update to the game thread.

The list, with what each one does, is in Console variables.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
[/Script/NavigationSystem.NavigationSystemV1]
bAllowClientSideNavigation=True

The cover run builds its path on the owning client. Without client-side navigation, clients get no path and run in a straight line. Levels also need a NavMeshBoundsVolume (with the navmesh built) for the cover run to path around obstacles.

docs.title: Motion matching
docs.text:
[/Script/PoseSearch.PoseSearchSettings]
AvailabilitiesBufferSize=230

Buffer size for the pose search availabilities, from the Game Animation Sample.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.PhysicsSettings]
bSubstepping=True
MaxSubstepDeltaTime=0.016667
MaxSubsteps=16

Physics substepping keeps ragdolls and physical animation stable at low frame rates.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.Engine]
NearClipPlane=1.000000

A 1 cm near clip plane. First person with aim down sights puts the rear sight a few centimeters from the camera; the default (10 cm) clips it.

docs.title: Console variables set at startup
docs.text:
[ConsoleVariables]
p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1
net.SubObjects.DefaultUseSubObjectReplicationList=1
fx.Niagara.ForceLastTickGroup=1
Variable Why p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication The CMC replicates the owner's acceleration to simulated proxies. Motion matching on remote CMC characters reads it, and the CMC cover movement relies on it. net.SubObjects.DefaultUseSubObjectReplicationList Replicated subobjects use the registered subobject list (Mover and Network Prediction). fx.Niagara.ForceLastTickGroup Niagara effects tick last, after the animation, so effects attached to bones follow the final pose.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
The template's [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings] section matches the Game Animation Sample (Lumen, virtual shadow maps, Nanite, TSR...). Four lines matter for the characters:

Setting Why r.GPUSkin.Support16BitBoneIndex=True MetaHuman meshes have more than 256 bones per section. r.GPUSkin.UnlimitedBoneInfluences=True MetaHuman meshes use more than 8 influences per vertex. r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True Skin cache shaders, used by MetaHuman deformers and grooms. r.SkinCache.DefaultBehavior=0 Skin cache off unless a mesh asks for it (inclusive mode).

docs.title: Network Prediction
docs.text:
DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini (whole file):

[/Script/NetworkPrediction.NetworkPredictionSettingsObject]
Settings=(PreferredTickingPolicy=Independent,ReplicatedManagerClassOverride=None,FixedTickFrameRate=60,bForceEngineFixTickForcePhysics=True,SimulatedProxyNetworkLOD=Interpolated,FixedTickInterpolationBufferedMS=100,IndependentTickInterpolationBufferedMS=100,IndependentTickInterpolationMaxBufferedMS=250,FixedTickInputSendCount=6,IndependentTickInputSendCount=6,MaximumRemoteInputFaultLimit=6)

The Mover pawn runs Network Prediction with independent ticking (each client simulates at its own frame rate) and interpolated simulated proxies. Without this file the engine defaults apply, which changes how remote Mover characters move.

docs.title: Gameplay tags
docs.text: DefaultGameplayTags.ini declares the tags the content uses: Foley.Event.* (footsteps, jumps, landings, ragdoll impacts), MotionMatching.* (database tags), SmartObject.ObjectType.* and StateTree.* (NPC and bench demos), plus a few redirects. Copy the file, or merge its +GameplayTagList lines into yours.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
[/Script/Engine.InputSettings]
DefaultPlayerInputClass=/Script/EnhancedInput.EnhancedPlayerInput
DefaultInputComponentClass=/Script/EnhancedInput.EnhancedInputComponent
DefaultTouchInterface=/GASPALS/Input/TIS_MobileControls.TIS_MobileControls

GASPALS uses Enhanced Input only (the engine default in 5.8). The touch interface is optional.

docs.title: Maps and modes
docs.text:
[/Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings]
EditorStartupMap=/GASPALS/Levels/RagdollLevel.RagdollLevel
GameDefaultMap=/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel.DefaultLevel

There is no global default game mode: each GASPALS level sets its game mode in its World Settings (GM_Sandbox for DefaultLevel and NPCLevel, GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll for RagdollLevel, GM_LookAtPOI for the look-at example). Set your own maps here.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
DefaultGame.ini:

Setting Why +PrimaryAssetTypesToScan=(PrimaryAssetType="GameFeatureData", ...) One of the enabled engine plugins is a game feature plugin. Without this entry the cook fails (UAT exit code 25, unknown cook failure). +MapsToCook=(FilePath="/GASPALS/Levels/DefaultLevel") The demo level is cooked. Replace with your levels.

Packaging also needs a C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows): the engine plugins GASPALS enables are not on by default, so the packaging tool builds a game target for the project even though it has no code.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the basics: are the project settings copied, and does the problem happen in the template's DefaultLevel? If it works there, compare your level, pawn or character with the sample.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The camera is a plain spring arm; no shoulder, crouch or cover offsets DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable missing or false Copy the data-driven console variables. Restart Play after changing it. Kellan appears on every pawn although nothing was selected DDCvar.VisualOverride is not declared, so it reads 0 (the first character) Copy the console variables (default -1). Characters never change with M The level's game mode is not GM_Sandbox or a child Use GM_Sandbox or derive from it. Errors about missing gameplay tags, no foley sounds DefaultGameplayTags.ini not copied Copy it. Packaging fails with exit code 25 Missing GameFeatureData asset type Add the entry from Installation. Packaging asks for a compiler The plugins GASPALS uses are not on by default Install Visual Studio 2022 with the game development workload. Traversal, cover or the obstacle course stop working after merging the collision settings Your project has its own custom channels, so the channel positions the Blueprints store changed Pick the channels again by name: Traversable Trace Channel, Cover Trace Channel, Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types (see Project settings). The player has no controls; InputMappingContexts is empty on this pawn The pawn's Input Mapping Contexts map is empty Add IMC_Sandbox (or your context) in the pawn's class defaults.

docs.title: Locomotion and traversal
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Pressing jump at an obstacle only jumps It does not block the Traversable channel, Traversable Trace Channel points at another channel, or it is too narrow See Make objects traversable; check the setting on the pawn's AC_TraversalLogic. No slide The CMC pawn has none; on the Mover pawn, slides need sprint speed (over 380) and wait for the 0.75 s cooldown Sprint, then crouch. The character keeps strafing The CMC pawn starts with strafe on Toggle strafe (middle mouse), or change CharacterInputState > Wants To Strafe on the pawn. The Mover pawn suddenly flies Z is the Mover debug flying toggle Press Z again, or delete the debug Input Key node in the Mover pawn's Event Graph. Feet slide or float on a new character Retargeting Check the IK Retargeter's chains and retarget pose.

docs.title: Cover
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix No cover at all on your pawn Enable Cover was turned off on its component (it is on by default) Turn it on in the pawn's cover component. Cover never triggers on some walls The wall ignores the Cover channel Use a preset that blocks Visibility (they all block Cover), or set its Cover response to Block. Characters take cover on foliage or fences Those objects block Cover Set their Cover response to Ignore (Build a cover level). The cover button does nothing Enable Sticky Cover off, nothing within Sticky Cover Reach, or first person with First Person Sticky Cover = Disabled Check the settings and the crosshair (it turns green over valid cover). Cover run goes straight into obstacles No navmesh Add a NavMeshBoundsVolume and build paths. Cover run fails on clients only Client-side navigation is off bAllowClientSideNavigation=True (project settings). Mover and CMC behave differently in cover Their cover components are tuned separately Compare the component settings; the cover reference shows where the samples differ.

docs.title: Equipment and overlays
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The item floats near the feet The attach socket is missing on the skeleton Add the overlay_* sockets to the character's Skeleton. The support hand does not reach the item No HandIK socket (or the item's Hand IK Socket name), or the pose's enable_handik_* curve is 0 Add the socket; set the curve in the pose's curve map. The item is not in the hands in first person The item actor has no AC_FirstPersonRendering Keep the component on every item actor. A new overlay child has snapping arms when aiming Its Aim Sweep Interp Speed values are 0 Set 30 / 10 on the child. The Overlay Pose set on the pawn does not show An item is equipped at spawn; its pose wins Start with Selected Equipment Unequip, or pick the stance later. OverlayPoseLayers has no anim layer class for the selected OverlayPose (or OverlayBodyLayers) The enum value has no row in the map Add the row on AC_OverlaySystem (and on the pawn's component if it overrides the map).

docs.title: First person
docs.text:
The first-person component prints setup problems on screen, in orange, for the local player. Each message starts with GASPALS First Person (<owner>):.

Message (abridged) Fix no third-person Skeletal Mesh Component found Set Third Person Mesh Name to the body component's name. no first-person mesh was generated Fill First Person Full Meshes (or Arms and Body for Split). the first-person skeleton has no FirstPersonCameraBone Add a virtual bone from root to head named VB Camera, or set First Person Camera Bone on the character's AC_FirstPersonRendering. the first-person skeleton has no FirstPersonHeadBone Set First Person Head Bone to the skeleton's head bone. this skeleton is not the UEFN mannequin, so the first-person overlay poses need FirstPersonRetargeter Set First Person Retargeter, or use TrueFirstPerson. FirstPersonOverlaySplit needs both FirstPersonArmsMeshes and FirstPersonBodyMeshes Fill both lists. Symptom Cause Fix The camera sees the inside of the head or the chest Eye offset Tune First Person Eye Offset ((0, 12, 0) for UE5 and MetaHuman heads). ADS sights do not line up Eye offset or the item's ADS socket Fix the eye offset first, then the socket. The rear sight is clipped Near clip plane NearClipPlane=1 in the project settings. The camera does not follow the body on a retargeted character CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera not compiled after an edit Open and compile the Control Rig.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The character is a frame behind the pawn The body mesh is not the first child of Root Reorder the components in the visual override Blueprint. The hands do not grip items on a retargeted character The hand IK curves do not reach the retargeted mesh Add a Curve Remap op (copy all source curves) to the IK Retargeter. MetaHuman clothing tears or stays in bind pose A follower with its own skeleton uses leader pose Leave its anim class empty and keep its post-process Anim Blueprint.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix A system works on the host but not for clients The component does not replicate Turn on Component Replicates on the pawn's component (see Networking). Remote Mover characters stutter Network Prediction settings missing Copy DefaultNetworkPrediction.ini. Remote CMC characters animate stiffly Acceleration not replicated p.EnableCharacterAccelerationReplication=1. Corrections during Mover play Something changed movement outside the input command Route movement changes through ProduceInput and transitions; np.PrintReconciles 1 lists corrections.

docs.title: Camera reference
docs.text:
The camera component on both pawns, and the camera director that picks the rigs.

How to read these tables

Settings are the values you tune: select the component in your pawn Blueprint (or open the asset) and look in the Details panel under the category shown. Runtime state is written by the system while it runs; read it, do not set it. Functions marked pure have no execution pins. The descriptions are the same as the Details panel tooltips. Default is the class default; where a sample pawn sets a different value on its component, the description says so ().

docs.title: Camera > Crosshair
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Show CrosshairbShowCrosshair Boolean true Show the crosshair dot (W_Crosshair) for the local player. When off, the dot is collapsed; aiming, cover targeting and the cover marker (bShowCoverMarker on the cover system) still work. Any widget works: it is positioned by the camera and picks its own look (W_Crosshair polls the pawn's cover system for its colour).

docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Camera PerspectiveCameraPerspective E_CameraPerspective ThirdPerson Active camera mode: third person, first person, or one of the two fixed cameras (top-down, side-scroller). Sent to the server on change. docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Camera Offset RigsCameraOffsetRigs S_CameraOffsetRigs Offset rigs the camera director layers on the main rig: crouch, right shoulder, cover low, cover edges, first-person scale, and per movement mode (in air, sliding, traversing, ragdoll; needs bPassMovementModeToCamera). Clear an entry to turn that offset off.Offset rigs the camera director layers on the main rig (crouch, right shoulder, cover low, cover edges, first-person scale). Clear an entry to turn that offset off. Read by CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter every frame. Pass Movement Mode to CamerabPassMovementModeToCamera Boolean true Pass the pawn's real movement mode to the camera director (S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera.MovementMode): the director then stacks the InAir, Sliding, Traversing and Ragdoll offset rigs, and chooser rows can match on the mode. Off = constant OnGround (the camera before 2026-10-07). The CMC pawn reports OnGround, InAir, Traversing and Ragdoll; Sliding only exists on the Mover pawn. Default true. Runtime state (3 variables) Variable Type Default Description Crosshair WidgetCrosshairWidget UserWidget ref Crosshair widget created on the local player's screen. Removed when the pawn is destroyed. docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description GetCrosshairAim (pure) AimOrigin (Vector), AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), bAimHit (Boolean), AimPlanarDirection (Vector) Where the player aims, for the crosshair and cover targeting. Third/first person: the camera ray through the screen center. Top-down/side-scroller: the ray under the mouse cursor, or with a gamepad a point 3 m out along the stick aim. Returns the ray, the world point it hits (bAimHit) and a planar aim direction. GetFixedCameraAimRotation LookGamepad (Vector2D), LookMouse (Vector2D) AimRotation (Rotator) Updates and returns the aim rotation for the fixed cameras: from the gamepad stick when it moves, else from the mouse cursor. Also sets bCrosshairGamepadAim. UpdateCrosshair Local player only, called every tick. Shows the crosshair dot when bShowCrosshair is on and moves it to the current aim point (GetCrosshairAim), or collapses it when off. Then asks the pawn's cover component for a cover target (UpdateCoverTargetMarker, which also places the cover marker) and turns the dot green while one is aimed. CanCyclePerspective (pure) bCanCycle (Boolean) Perspective key gate: camera control is allowed (not during a ragdoll that locks it) and another perspective is available. GetFirstAvailablePerspective (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) The first AllowedPerspectives entry that is available; ThirdPerson when none is. GetNextAvailablePerspective (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) The next available perspective after the current one in AllowedPerspectives order, wrapping; the current one when there is no other. OnRagdollEnded Called when the ragdoll ends. Restores camera control and the perspective saved before the ragdoll. OnRagdollStarted Called when the ragdoll starts. Applies the ragdoll camera control setting and optionally switches perspective. InitializeSystem ParentPawn (Pawn ref), ParentMesh (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), ParentMesh_FP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), GameplayCamera (GameplayCameraComponent ref) Stores the pawn, mesh and camera references, attaches the camera for the current perspective, and binds the ragdoll camera events if enabled. ValidatePerspectives Called by InitializeSystem. A start CameraPerspective that is not available becomes the first available one (the perspective listeners are told). On-screen warnings: FirstPerson listed without AC_FirstPersonRendering; on pawns with AC_RagdollSystem, an unavailable CameraPerspectiveDuringRagdoll. GetFirstPersonCameraBone (pure) BoneName (Name) First-person camera socket of the active character: FirstPersonCameraBone of the AC_FirstPersonRendering that owns the first-person mesh; VB Camera without one. IsPerspectiveAvailable (pure) Perspective (E_CameraPerspective) bAvailable (Boolean) True when Perspective is in AllowedPerspectives and, for FirstPerson, the pawn has an AC_FirstPersonRendering. Read by the perspective key, the start and ragdoll perspectives, AC_FirstPersonRendering (builds first-person meshes only when FirstPerson is available) and cover (sticky cover's switch to third person).

docs.title: Cover reference
docs.text:
The cover core component and its two movement adapters. Add AC_CoverSystem_Mover to a Mover pawn or AC_CoverSystem_CMC to a Character pawn: both inherit every setting of AC_CoverSystem_Base.

How to read these tables

Settings are the values you tune: select the component in your pawn Blueprint (or open the asset) and look in the Details panel under the category shown. Runtime state is written by the system while it runs; read it, do not set it. Functions marked pure have no execution pins. The descriptions are the same as the Details panel tooltips. Default is the class default; where a sample pawn sets a different value on its component, the description says so ().

docs.title: AC_CoverSystem_Base
docs.text: /GASPALS/Systems/CoverSystem/AC_CoverSystem_Base · parent ActorComponent

docs.title: Cover > Aim
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable Cover AimbEnableCoverAim Boolean true Aim from cover: aiming (WantsToAim) in cover steps out to the best aim position instead of leaving cover. Off: aiming leaves cover as before. Cover Aim Keep StandingbCoverAimKeepStanding Boolean true Low cover: once standing to aim over the wall (Over), stay standing while the target can still be hit from there, and only crouch back into cover (InPlace) when the cover spot can hit it, never side-step to an edge. Off: the order cover, edge, stand is re-applied every time. Cover Aim Muzzle Height StandCoverAimMuzzleHeightStand Float 145 Aim from cover: muzzle height (cm above the capsule bottom) used for line-of-fire traces while standing. Adjust for very short or tall characters. Cover Aim Muzzle Height CrouchCoverAimMuzzleHeightCrouch Float 95 Aim from cover: muzzle height (cm above the capsule bottom) used for line-of-fire traces while crouched. Cover Aim Hit ToleranceCoverAimHitTolerance Float 30 Line of fire: a hit this close (cm) to the aim point still counts as a clear shot (the target itself). Cover Aim Cover DepthCoverAimCoverDepth Float 80 A hit of the aim ray within this depth (cm) behind the cover face counts as the cover in use (wall thickness): aiming at your own cover means aiming past it. Cover Aim Min Pose TimeCoverAimMinPoseTime Float 0.25 Aim from cover: minimum time (seconds) in an aim pose before it can change to another one. Cover Aim Blocked DelayCoverAimBlockedDelay Float 0.15 Seconds the current pose must be blocked before the pawn moves to a more exposed pose. Ignores short blocks such as the aim sweeping past an obstacle edge. Cover Aim Return DelayCoverAimReturnDelay Float 0.3 Seconds a safer pose must stay clearly valid before the pawn switches back to it. Cover Aim Return MarginCoverAimReturnMargin Float 10 Clearance (cm) a safer pose needs before the pawn switches back to it: a sphere of this radius must pass the first CoverAimReturnMarginReach of its shot. Stops flicker when a shot grazes the wall top or end. Cover Aim Return Margin ReachCoverAimReturnMarginReach Float 300 Length (cm) of the shot, from the muzzle, checked with the CoverAimReturnMargin sphere: the part near the cover where grazing matters. Beyond it a plain line test is used, so ground targets do not block the return. Cover Aim Edge ClearanceCoverAimEdgeClearance Float 20 Aim from cover: extra distance (cm) past the edge, beyond the capsule radius, when stepping out to aim around it. Cover Aim Slow RadiusCoverAimSlowRadius Float 30 Aim from cover: steering input slows down inside this distance (cm) to the target point. Cover Aim Arrive ToleranceCoverAimArriveTolerance Float 4 Aim from cover: the step-out and return stop within this distance (cm) along the wall. Cover Aim Return TimeoutCoverAimReturnTimeout Float 1 Aim from cover: after releasing aim, the lock ends after this time (seconds) even if the pawn could not get back to the return point.

docs.title: Cover > Camera
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable Cover Shoulder SwitchbEnableCoverShoulderSwitch Boolean true Cover shoulder switch: at a cover edge the third-person camera moves to the edge side (a temporary shoulder swap; the player's shoulder setting is untouched). When off, the camera stays on the player's shoulder in cover. Enable Cover Camera OffsetsbEnableCoverCameraOffsets Boolean true Cover camera offsets: in third person, the camera rises behind low cover and pushes past the cover edge the character is at (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow / CoverEdgeLeft / CoverEdgeRight). When off, the camera keeps its normal framing in cover.

docs.title: Cover > Collision
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Trace ChannelCoverTraceChannel ETraceTypeQuery TraceTypeQuery5 Trace channel of every cover geometry probe: wall search and sticky entry (TraceWall), cover height, aim wall ends and steps, and the cover target under the crosshair. Default Cover, a channel that every collision profile answers like Visibility. Set objects to Ignore Cover to keep them from counting as cover. Pick Visibility if your project has no Cover channel.

docs.title: Cover > CornerTurn
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Corner Turn Hold TimeCornerTurnHoldTime Float 0.3 Sticky cover: how long (s) the player holds toward an edge before the character turns around the corner. Corner Turn AngleCornerTurnAngle Float 100 Sticky cover: largest corner angle (degrees between the two wall normals) the character turns around. Corner Turn Min WidthCornerTurnMinWidth Float 50 Sticky cover: how deep (cm) the wall around a corner must be to turn around it. Thinner ends (e.g. a thin wall) stop at the edge. Corner Remap Release TimeCornerRemapReleaseTime Float 0.15 Seconds the player must release or change the held direction before the corner input remap stops. Ignores single frames without input, so chained corner turns keep going.

docs.title: Cover > CoverRun
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Run RangeCoverRunRange Float 1500 Cover run: how far (cm) the cover under the camera crosshair (or the wall straight ahead) can be for the cover button to run to it. Cover within StickyCoverReach is taken directly. Cover Run Max TimeCoverRunMaxTime Float 2 Cover run: extra seconds allowed on top of the path length at 5 m/s before the run is cancelled (e.g. when blocked on the way). Cover Run Path ToleranceCoverRunPathTolerance Float 60 Cover run: distance (cm) at which the next navmesh path point is followed. Cover Run Arrive DistanceCoverRunArriveDistance Float 80 Cover run: on the last path leg, distance (cm) from the stand point (60 cm in front of the wall) at which the character snaps into sticky cover. Cover Run Arrive SpeedCoverRunArriveSpeed Float 150 Speed (cm/s) the cover run slows down to when it reaches CoverRunArriveDistance and takes sticky cover, so the character does not slide along the wall. Cover Run Brake DecelCoverRunBrakeDecel Float 700 Deceleration (cm/s2) the cover run plans with on its last leg: the run input is scaled down so the speed reaches CoverRunArriveSpeed at CoverRunArriveDistance. Keep it below what the pawn can brake (Mover StoppingDeceleration, CMC braking). Cover Run Expected SpeedCoverRunExpectedSpeed Float 500 Speed (cm/s) used to plan a cover run: the run time limit is the path length divided by this. Default 500. Cover Run Stand OffsetCoverRunStandOffset Float 60 Distance (cm) from the target wall where a cover run stops, before sticky cover snaps the character in. Default 60. Cover Run Crouch Block TimeCoverRunCrouchBlockTime Float 0.4 Seconds after a cover run during which crouch requests are ignored (the run sprint would turn a crouch into a slide). Default 0.4. Cover Run Reentry DelayCoverRunReentryDelay Float 0.2 Minimum delay (s) before cover can be taken again after a cover run ends. Default 0.2.

docs.title: Cover > Debug
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable DebugbEnableDebug Boolean false Draw the cover traces for one frame each (wall, cover target, top height, and the aim traces), through GetCoverDebugDrawType. bCoverAimDebug prints the aim pose changes separately. Default false.Reserved for drawing the cover traces. Currently unused: the old CMC cover trace that read it was replaced by the shared sensor. Cover Aim DebugbCoverAimDebug Boolean false Debug: print every aim pose change on screen and to the log ("Cover aim: Old > New") and draw the aim target.

docs.title: Cover > Detection
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Enter DistanceCoverEnterDistance Float 80 How far from the character (cm) a wall can be to take cover when moving into it. Cover Enter Input DotCoverEnterInputDot Float 0.3 How directly the move input must point into the wall to take cover (dot product: 0 = anything toward the wall, 1 = straight into it). Cover Hold DistanceCoverHoldDistance Float 50 Max distance (cm) between the character and the wall for cover to be kept. Must be larger than the Cover mode TargetWallDistance. Cover Trace RadiusCoverTraceRadius Float 12 Radius (cm) of the sphere traces used to find cover. High Cover HeightHighCoverHeight Float 148 Walls at least this tall (cm above the character's feet) are high cover; lower walls are low cover (crouch behind them). Measured from the feet, so crouching doesn't change the answer. 148 = the standing probe of the sample characters.Height (cm) above the character origin that is checked for wall; if there is none, the cover counts as low cover. Low cover needs a crouching character (or sticky cover on the Mover): standing characters do not take it automatically, and standing up in soft low cover leaves it. Edge Probe OffsetEdgeProbeOffset Float 45 Sideways distance (cm) of the edge, look-ahead and corner probes from the character. Max Cover Turn AngleMaxCoverTurnAngle Float 90 Largest change in wall direction (degrees) the character follows while moving along cover. Bends are followed automatically; corners (e.g. 90 on a table) only while the camera looks at the cover. Sharper changes release cover. Cover Probe PaddingCoverProbePadding Float 20 Extra length (cm) added to the wall probes beyond the wall gap, so a probe still reaches the wall when the character drifts a little. Internal tuning. Default 20. Cover Top Probe HeightCoverTopProbeHeight Float 300 Height (cm) above the cover point where the downward trace that measures the cover height starts; taller walls count as this high. Raise it for levels with very tall cover. Default 300.

docs.title: Cover > Exit
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Exit Input DotCoverExitInputDot Float 0.7 How directly the move input must point away from the wall to start leaving cover (dot product; 0.7 = more than 45 degrees away). Lower values leave cover more easily but can drop cover while strafing around corners. Cover Exit DelayCoverExitDelay Float 0.15 Seconds the player must keep pushing away from the wall before cover is released. Sticky Exit Input DotStickyExitInputDot Float 0.9 How directly the input must point away from the wall to leave sticky cover (dot product; higher = more deliberate). Sticky Exit DelayStickyExitDelay Float 0.35 Seconds the player must keep pulling away before sticky cover is released.

docs.title: Cover > Facing
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Facing Stand AutoFacing_StandAuto E_CoverFacingStyle ShoulderToWall Facing while standing in automatic (soft) cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Stand StickyFacing_StandSticky E_CoverFacingStyle BackToWall Facing while standing in sticky cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Crouch AutoFacing_CrouchAuto E_CoverFacingStyle FaceWall Facing while crouched in automatic (soft) cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Facing Crouch StickyFacing_CrouchSticky E_CoverFacingStyle ShoulderToWall Facing while crouched in sticky cover: FaceWall (towards the wall, offset by the shoulder angles), ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the last move direction) or BackToWall. Character Rotation Right ShoulderCharacterRotationRightShoulder Float 25 Yaw offset in degrees added to the wall-facing direction while the camera is on the right shoulder (FaceWall style, and the CMC mesh rotation). Character Rotation Left ShoulderCharacterRotationLeftShoulder Float -25 Yaw offset in degrees added to the wall-facing direction while the camera is on the left shoulder (FaceWall style, and the CMC mesh rotation).

docs.title: Cover > FirstPerson
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description First Person Sticky CoverFirstPersonStickyCover E_CoverFirstPersonSticky SwitchToThirdPerson Sticky cover while the camera is in first person: SwitchToThirdPerson (camera goes to third person in sticky cover and back when it ends) or Disabled (no sticky cover in first person). First Person Auto CoverFirstPersonAutoCover E_CoverFirstPersonAuto MovementOnly Auto (soft) cover while the camera is in first person: MovementOnly (wall hug and edges, the body follows the camera) or Disabled (no auto cover in first person).

docs.title: Cover > General
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Enable CoverbEnableCover Boolean true Master switch. When off, the character never takes cover. Enable Auto CoverbEnableAutoCover Boolean true Auto cover: take cover by moving into a wall (or crouching in front of it). When off, only the cover button (sticky cover) takes cover. Needs bEnableCover. Enable Sticky CoverbEnableStickyCover Boolean true Sticky cover: the cover button (IA_Cover) snaps into cover under the crosshair, upgrades auto cover to sticky, and runs to far cover when bEnableCoverRun is on. When off, the button does nothing and the crosshair does not target cover. Needs bEnableCover. Enable Cover RunbEnableCoverRun Boolean true Cover run: holding the cover button sprints to cover farther than StickyCoverReach (under the crosshair, up to CoverRunRange). When off, the button only takes cover within StickyCoverReach, and the cover marker and the green crosshair only show for cover the button can take from where the character stands (never while already in cover). Needs bEnableStickyCover. Engage RuleEngageRule E_CoverEngageRule Automatic When cover can be taken: Automatic (walk into a wall) or WhileCrouched (only while crouching). Move Into CoverbMoveIntoCover Boolean true When on, the character is moved against the wall when it takes cover (pulled to TargetWallDistance; the Mover through the Cover movement mode, the CMC through ShapeCoverMoveInput). When off, it is simply in cover when close enough and out of cover when too far, without being moved. Sticky cover always pulls in. Auto Crouch Low CoverbAutoCrouchLowCover Boolean true Crouch automatically behind low cover.

docs.title: Cover > Marker
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Show Cover MarkerbShowCoverMarker Boolean true Show the Division-style marker on the targeted cover (local player only). The crosshair still turns green when this is off. Cover Marker Widget ClassCoverMarkerWidgetClass UserWidget class W_CoverMarker Widget shown by the cover marker on the targeted wall (a world-space widget component created on first use). Default W_CoverMarker. Cover Marker Draw SizeCoverMarkerDrawSize Vector2D (100, 12) Draw size of the cover marker widget in world units (X wide, Y high). Default (100, 12). Cover Marker Wall OffsetCoverMarkerWallOffset Float 3 Distance in cm between the cover marker and the wall face, so it does not clip into it. Default 3.

docs.title: Cover > Movement
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Wall Distance Stand AutoWallDistance_StandAuto Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in soft (auto) cover while standing. 0 = touching the wall. The wall spring holds it, pushing out at up to WallPushSpeed and pulling in at up to MaxWallPullSpeed; tolerance WallPullDeadZone. Keep the gap plus the capsule radius under CoverHoldDistance. Wall Distance Stand StickyWallDistance_StandSticky Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in sticky cover while standing. 0 = touching the wall. Pulled in at up to StickyPullSpeed, pushed out at up to WallPushSpeed. Wall Distance Crouch AutoWallDistance_CrouchAuto Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in soft (auto) cover while crouched. 0 = touching the wall. Raise it if a crouched pose clips into the wall. Wall Distance Crouch StickyWallDistance_CrouchSticky Float 0 Gap (cm) between the capsule and the cover wall in sticky cover while crouched (sticky low cover crouches automatically). 0 = touching the wall. Wall Spring StrengthWallSpringStrength Float 8 Strength of the spring that holds the character at the wall distance: pull speed (cm/s) per cm of distance error. Wall Pull Dead ZoneWallPullDeadZone Float 2 Distance in cm around TargetWallDistance where the wall spring does nothing, so the character settles instead of creeping back and forth (Mover Cover mode and CMC). Max Wall Pull SpeedMaxWallPullSpeed Float 200 Fastest speed (cm/s) at which soft cover pulls the character toward the wall (when bMoveIntoCover is on). Wall Push SpeedWallPushSpeed Float 100 Max speed (cm/s) the wall spring pushes the pawn away from the wall when it is closer than its WallDistance gap. 0 = never push (the pawn stays wherever it touched the wall). Sticky Pull SpeedStickyPullSpeed Float 600 Fastest speed (cm/s) at which sticky cover pulls the character toward the wall. Stop at EdgesbStopAtEdges Boolean false Soft cover also stops at the ends of the wall. Sticky cover always stops at edges. Cover Side Input ThresholdCoverSideInputThreshold Float 0.2 How much sideways stick input (0..1 along the wall) counts as moving along cover: edge stops, peeking and corner turns. Raise it for gamepads with a loose stick. Default 0.2.

docs.title: Cover > Pose
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Cover Lower Max StandCoverLower_MaxStand Float 10 Most the pelvis is lowered (cm) when standing in cover. The amount adapts to the cover height: just enough to keep the top of the capsule CoverLower_HeadClearance under the cover top; 0 behind cover taller than the pawn. Cover Lower Max CrouchCoverLower_MaxCrouch Float 15 Most the pelvis is lowered (cm) when crouched in cover (typically behind low cover). Adapts to the cover height like CoverLower_MaxStand. Cover Lower Head ClearanceCoverLower_HeadClearance Float 5 How far (cm) under the cover top the top of the capsule should be after lowering. Higher = ducks deeper (up to the max).

docs.title: Cover > Sticky
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Sticky Cover ReachStickyCoverReach Float 250 How far (cm) along the camera direction the cover button searches for a wall; also how far sticky cover holds on to the wall while pulling the character in. Sticky Tap TimeStickyTapTime Float 0.25 Cover button: presses shorter than this (s) count as a tap. A tap in sticky cover leaves it; in cover, a cover run to other cover only starts once the button is held longer. Sticky Reentry CooldownStickyReentryCooldown Float 0.5 Seconds after leaving cover before sticky or auto cover can grab the character again. Default 0.5.

docs.title: Cover > Traversal
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description Vault Facing DotVaultFacingDot Float 0.9 Space in cover while not facing the wall this closely (dot product; 0.9 = within about 25 degrees) first turns the character to face the wall, then starts the traversal. Vault Facing TimeoutVaultFacingTimeout Float 0.75 Longest time (seconds) the character spends turning toward the wall before the traversal is tried anyway. Runtime state (10 variables) Variable Type Default Description Cover Target AimedbCoverTargetAimed Boolean false Output: true when the last FindCoverTarget found a cover point along the crosshair aim (not only near the character). Drives the crosshair colour and the cover marker. Cover Run ActivebCoverRunActive Boolean false Output: true while the character sprints toward cover (cover run). Read by the character in ProduceInput to force the Sprint gait. Not meant to be set by hand. Cover Run Crouch BlockbCoverRunCrouchBlock Boolean false Output: true during a cover run and shortly after it (unless in cover). Read by the character in ProduceInput to block crouching, so the sprint never turns into a slide. Not meant to be set by hand. Cover MarkerCoverMarker WidgetComponent ref Runtime: the world-space cover marker widget component, created on demand by GetCoverMarker. Parent PawnParentPawn Pawn ref Set by InitializeSystem: the pawn that owns this cover component. Internal; read by the CMC and Mover cover components. Is Character in CoverbIsCharacterInCover Boolean false Output: true while the character is in cover. Read by the character for animation (Get_PropertiesForAnimation). Not meant to be set by hand. Sticky CoverbStickyCover Boolean false Internal state: true while in sticky cover. Cover StateCoverState S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover Internal state: the cover result sent to the Mover every frame (normal, point, in cover, low cover, edges). Cover NormalCoverNormal Vector (0, 0, 0) Output: current wall normal (flattened, pointing away from the wall). Not meant to be set by hand. Cover Press PendingbCoverPressPending Boolean false The current cover button press found a far run target and waits: held past StickyTapTime it runs there, released sooner it does the tap action.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description CanCoverAimPoseHit (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) bCanHit (Boolean) True when the pose is available and its muzzle has a clear line of fire to AimPoint (TestCoverAimLineOfFire with Radius). CanStartCoverAim (pure) bCanStart (Boolean) True when an aim lock can start: aim is requested while in cover, outside a corner turn and a cover run. FindCoverAimPose (pure) AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) The least exposed pose that can hit AimPoint, in this order: InPlace (stay in cover), the edge the aim points to, the other edge, Over (stand up). None when no pose can. Radius > 0 asks for a clear margin around the shot. FindCoverAimWallEnd Side (Float) Distance (Float) Distance along the wall from the return point to the wall end on Side (-1 left, +1 right): a line trace 5 cm behind the wall face, from EdgeProbeOffset+40 past the pawn back toward it. No end within reach returns EdgeProbeOffset; an inside corner (the probe starts in the perpendicular wall) counts as no end. FinishCoverAim bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Cover outputs while the aim lock is active: writes CoverState from the frozen snapshot, with the stepped-out edge cleared so neither movement (Mover input or CMC shaping) stops at it. Low-cover force crouch stays on except when standing to aim over it. GetAimTraceSettings (pure) AimTraceChannel (ETraceTypeQuery), AimTraceDistance (Float) Aim trace channel and length for the cover line-of-fire checks: the values of the pawn's AC_CameraSystem (AimTraceChannel, AimTraceDistance), so cover aim and the crosshair always trace the same way. Without a camera system: Visibility and 10000 cm. GetCoverAimCameraState (pure) bLowCover (Boolean), EdgeSide (Float) bAimLowCover (Boolean), AimEdgeSide (Float) Camera hook (end of GetCoverCameraState): no low-cover camera offset while aiming, and the shoulder side taken from the stepped-out edge. GetCoverAimDirection (pure) AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), AimForward (Vector), bFixedCamera (Boolean) Aim of the player camera: planar aim direction, crosshair point, 3D camera forward and whether the camera is fixed (top-down, side-scroller). AI pawns and pawns without a camera system use the base aim rotation. GetCoverAimEdgeDistance Side (Float) Distance (Float), bOpen (Boolean) Distance along the wall from the return point to the wall end on Side (FindCoverAimWallEnd) and whether the step out past it is open (IsCoverAimStepOpen). Impure so its two outputs come from one measurement; called once per side in StartCoverAim. GetCoverAimEdgeOrder (pure) AimDirection (Vector) First (E_CoverAimPose), Second (E_CoverAimPose) The edge the aim points toward (First) and the other edge (Second). GetCoverAimEdgeProbe (pure) Side (Float) Start (Vector), End (Vector) Probe line for the wall end on Side: starts EdgeProbeOffset + 40 past the return point along the wall, 5 cm behind the wall face, and runs back toward the pawn for twice EdgeProbeOffset + 40. GetCoverAimFacing (pure) Facing (Vector) AimFacing (Vector) Facing while aiming from cover: the planar aim direction. Returns Facing unchanged when not aiming from cover. GetCoverAimFallbackPose (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Pose used when no pose can hit the target as the aim starts: Over in low cover, InPlace in high cover. GetCoverAimMoveInput MoveInput (Vector) AimMoveInput (Vector) Move input while the aim lock is on (end of RemapCoverMoveInput): watches for exit input (UpdateCoverAimExitRequest) and steers along the wall to the pose location (GetCoverAimSteering). Passes MoveInput through when not locked. GetCoverAimMuzzle (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Muzzle (Vector) Muzzle stand-in for a pose: the pose location, CoverAimMuzzleHeightStand above the floor when standing (Over, or the aim started standing), CoverAimMuzzleHeightCrouch otherwise. GetCoverAimPoseLocation (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Location (Vector) Where the pawn stands for a pose: the return point, or for an edge pose the point just past the wall end (edge distance + capsule radius + CoverAimEdgeClearance). GetCoverAimPoseRank (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Rank (Integer) Exposure rank for comparing poses: InPlace 0, edges 1, Over 2, None 3. GetCoverAimPoseSide (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) Side (Float) -1 for EdgeLeft, +1 for EdgeRight, 0 for the poses that stay at the cover spot. GetCoverAimStartPoint (pure) Point (Vector) Return point for a new aim: the previous one when the pawn is still within 2x CoverAimArriveTolerance of it (it came back from the last aim), so repeated aims do not creep along the wall; otherwise the current location. GetCoverAimStartPose (pure) BestPose (E_CoverAimPose) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) First pose of an aim: BestPose, or GetCoverAimFallbackPose when no pose can hit the target. GetCoverAimSteering (pure) MoveInput (Vector) Move input along the wall toward the current pose location: full speed beyond CoverAimSlowRadius, slowing to 25% near it, zero within CoverAimArriveTolerance. The cover movement keeps the wall distance. GetCoverAimTarget (pure) AimForward (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), bFixedCamera (Boolean) Target (Vector) The world point the aim pose has to hit. Camera-independent so the pose cannot feed back into it: a ray along AimForward from standing eye height above the cover spot. When that ray hits your own cover (IsOnCoverAimWall), the target is whatever lies behind it: aiming at your cover means aiming past it. Fixed cameras (top-down, side-scroller) use the cursor point (AimPoint). GetCoverAimWallAxes (pure) WallNormal (Vector), Tangent (Vector) Flattened wall normal and wall tangent of the frozen cover snapshot. Tangent = cross(Z, -normal): +Tangent points to the right edge, -Tangent to the left edge. IsCoverAimPoseAvailable (pure) Pose (E_CoverAimPose) bAvailable (Boolean) True when the cover allows the pose: InPlace always, Over in low cover only, an edge pose when the snapshot is at that edge and the step-out path is open. IsCoverAimPoseSafer (pure) Candidate (E_CoverAimPose), Current (E_CoverAimPose) bSafer (Boolean) True when Candidate is less exposed than Current. With bCoverAimKeepStanding, a pawn standing in Over only goes back to InPlace, never to an edge. IsCoverAimRequested (pure) bRequested (Boolean) True when the player wants to aim from cover: bEnableCoverAim is on, the aim input is held and the pawn may move. IsCoverAimReturned (pure) bReturned (Boolean) True when the pawn is back at its cover spot along the wall (within CoverAimArriveTolerance), and crouched again when the aim started crouched. IsCoverAimStepOpen (pure) Side (Float), Distance (Float) bOpen (Boolean) True when the pawn can step out past the wall end on Side: traces at capsule height and 40 cm lower along the wall, out to Distance + capsule diameter + CoverAimEdgeClearance. IsOnCoverAimWall (pure) Point (Vector) bOnCover (Boolean) True when Point lies on the cover being used: between 10 cm in front of the wall face and CoverAimCoverDepth behind it (face and top of the wall). SelectCoverAimPose AimDirection (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Picks CoverAimPose for the target each frame while aiming: the first pose of the aim (GetCoverAimStartPose), then keeps a pose that can hit, going back to a safer one when clearly possible (UpdateCoverAimSaferPose), or leaves a blocked one (UpdateCoverAimBlockedPose). StartCoverAim Starts the aim lock: freezes the cover state (CoverAimSnapshot) and the return point, remembers the crouch state and measures both edges once. StopCoverAim Ends the aim lock and clears the pose. SwitchCoverAimPose NewPose (E_CoverAimPose) Changes the aim pose: sets CoverAimPose and restarts the pose timers (CoverAimPoseTimer, CoverAimSaferTimer). Every pose change goes through here. TestCoverAimLineOfFire (pure) Muzzle (Vector), AimPoint (Vector), Radius (Float) bClear (Boolean) True when Muzzle has a clear shot at AimPoint: nothing blocks the line, or the first hit is within CoverAimHitTolerance of the aim point. With Radius > 0 the first CoverAimReturnMarginReach of the shot must also clear a sphere of that radius. UpdateCoverAim DeltaSeconds (Float) bLocked (Boolean) Aim from cover, called from EvaluateCover every frame: starts the lock when aiming in cover (CanStartCoverAim, StartCoverAim); while locked stops when cover is lost, leaves cover on exit input, picks the pose while aiming (SelectCoverAimPose, target from GetCoverAimTarget) and walks back after release (UpdateCoverAimReturn). Returns whether the lock is on. UpdateCoverAimBlockedPose BestPose (E_CoverAimPose), DeltaSeconds (Float) The current pose cannot hit the target: count CoverAimBlockedTimer and switch to BestPose once the pose has been blocked for CoverAimBlockedDelay (and held CoverAimMinPoseTime). Short blocks, like the aim sweeping past an obstacle edge, are ignored. UpdateCoverAimExitRequest MoveInput (Vector) While aiming in cover, input away from the wall (CoverExitInputDot) requests leaving cover (bCoverAimExitRequested); UpdateCoverAim acts on it. UpdateCoverAimReturn DeltaSeconds (Float) Aim released: the pawn walks back to the return point (GetCoverAimMoveInput), and the lock ends once it is there (IsCoverAimReturned) or after CoverAimReturnTimeout. UpdateCoverAimSaferPose SaferPose (E_CoverAimPose), DeltaSeconds (Float) The current pose can hit the target: switch back to SaferPose once it has been safer (IsCoverAimPoseSafer, found with the CoverAimReturnMargin clearance) for CoverAimReturnDelay. UpdateCornerTurn MoveInput (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Sticky cover: turns the character around a wall corner once the player holds toward an edge for CornerTurnHoldTime and a side wall within CornerTurnAngle and CornerTurnMinWidth is found. FindCoverTarget bTargetFound (Boolean) Looks along the crosshair or camera ray, within cover run range, for cover to run to and stores the run target. Returns whether one was found. FindFarCoverRunTarget Location (Vector) bFar (Boolean) Looks for a cover-run target under the crosshair (FindCoverTarget) and returns true when one is found farther than StickyCoverReach and cover runs are enabled. RemapCoverMoveInput MoveInput (Vector) RemappedInput (Vector) Remaps the move input in sticky cover: corner turn remap, steering to the cover run target at a braking speed, then the aim steering. Returns the input for the movement code. RunToCoverTarget Location (Vector) bStarted (Boolean) Starts a cover run to the far target under the crosshair, leaving the current cover when it starts. Returns whether the run started. StartCoverRun bRunStarted (Boolean) Starts a cover run to the found cover: builds a navmesh path (straight line without navmesh), sets the time limit and turns bCoverRunActive on. Returns whether it started; always false when bEnableCoverRun is off. UpdateCoverRun Location (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float), bBlocked (Boolean) Per frame during a cover run: follows the path to the target cover, cancels on button release, timeout or blocked cover, and takes the cover on arrival. GetCoverDebugDrawType (pure) DrawDebugType (EDrawDebugTrace) Debug draw mode for every cover trace: ForOneFrame when bEnableDebug is on (wall, cover target, top height, aim line of fire, aim target, wall end and step traces are drawn), else None. CanEnterSoftCover Location (Vector), Normal (Vector) bAllowed (Boolean) Pure: true when automatic cover can be taken at Location: the character is crouching or the wall reaches HighCoverHeight, and auto cover is allowed in this camera. EvaluateCover MoveInput (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Per-frame cover evaluation on the owner: updates the cover button, crouch edge and aim lock, then corner turn and cover run, and enters, keeps or leaves cover. Returns force-crouch and the cover state for the movement code. FinishCover bKeep (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector), MoveInput (Vector) bForceCrouch (Boolean), CoverInputs (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover) Builds the cover state output for the frame. Keeping cover: probes the wall at the character and both sides to set the high-cover and edge flags. Otherwise returns the out-of-cover state. Also returns force-crouch for low cover. GetHighCoverProbeOffset (pure) Offset (Float) Height to add to the actor location for the high-cover probe: HighCoverHeight above the feet (capsule bottom), whatever the crouch state, so a wall between the crouched and standing probe heights no longer flips between low and high cover. ResolveCoverSurface Location (Vector), MoveInput (Vector) bHit (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Re-traces the wall while in cover (center, leading side and camera-forward probes) and picks the cover point and normal to follow. Bends up to MaxCoverTurnAngle are followed. TraceWall Start (Vector), Direction (Vector), Distance (Float) bHit (Boolean), Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Pure: sphere trace (CoverTraceRadius) from Start along Direction for Distance. Returns whether a wall was hit, the impact point and the flattened wall normal. UpdateCrouchEdge Tracks crouch changes: sets bWasCrouching and bJustCrouched (true for the frame crouching started). IsAutoCoverAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) False in first person when FirstPersonAutoCover is Disabled (no soft cover from walking into walls). IsFirstPersonCamera (pure) bFirstPerson (Boolean) True when the owner AC_CameraSystem is in FirstPerson (false without a camera system). IsStickyCoverAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) False in first person when FirstPersonStickyCover is Disabled, or when it is SwitchToThirdPerson but ThirdPerson is not an available perspective on the camera system (a first-person-only pawn). The cover button then does nothing. UpdateFirstPersonCoverCamera Sticky cover in first person: switch the camera to third person (FirstPersonStickyCover = SwitchToThirdPerson), and back to first person when sticky cover ends if we switched it. Owner only, called from EvaluateCover. UsesCoverFacing (pure) bCoverFacing (Boolean) False in first-person auto cover (MovementOnly): the body follows the camera instead of the cover facing. Sticky cover in first person switches to third person, so it keeps the cover facing. GetCoverMarker Marker (WidgetComponent ref) Returns the world-space cover marker (a Widget Component showing W_CoverMarker). Creates it on the pawn the first time it is needed: hidden, absolute transform, no collision, no shadow. IsCoverTargeted (pure) bTargeted (Boolean) True while the cover button would take the character to the cover under the crosshair (in reach, or a cover run target). Updated every frame by UpdateCoverFeedback for the local player; the crosshair widget polls it to turn CoverTargetCrosshairColor. UpdateCoverFeedback Per-frame cover feedback for the locally controlled player: UpdateCoverTarget, then UpdateCoverMarker. Called from the cover component's own update (Mover tick, CMC UpdateCoverCMC); other pawns skip it. UpdateCoverMarker Shows the cover marker (CoverMarkerWidgetClass, created on first use) on the targeted wall, CoverMarkerWallOffset in front of it, while bCoverTargeted and bShowCoverMarker. UpdateCoverTarget Each frame out of a cover run: finds the cover under the crosshair (FindCoverTarget) and sets bCoverTargeted, which shows the cover marker when that cover can be taken (sticky within StickyCoverReach, or a cover run when enabled). GetCoverTopHeight Height (Float) Height (cm above the pawn floor) of the top of the cover wall in CoverState: one line trace down from 300 cm, 10 cm inside the wall. 300 when nothing is hit (the wall is at least that tall, or thinner than 10 cm). InitializeSystem ParentPawn (Pawn ref) Stores the owning pawn. Called once by the pawn; the Mover and CMC components extend it. GetCoverCameraState (pure) bLowCoverCamera (Boolean), EdgeSide (Float), ShoulderSide (Float) Cover camera state for the camera director (local player). bLowCoverCamera: in low cover. EdgeSide: -1 / +1 when a cover edge is within reach on the left / right of the screen (both edges: the side last moved to), 0 otherwise. bLowCoverCamera and EdgeSide pick the offset rigs and are off when bEnableCoverCameraOffsets is off; ShoulderSide is the same side for the shoulder swap and is 0 when bEnableCoverShoulderSwitch is off. GetCoverFacingDirection (pure) Direction (Vector) Pawn hook: the direction the character visibly faces (Mover: actor forward; CMC: the mesh, which the CMC cover rotates). Used to wait for the turn to the wall before a vault. GetCoverLowerAmount bCrouched (Boolean) Lower (Float) How far (cm) CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis in cover: enough to bring the top of the capsule CoverLower_HeadClearance under the cover top (GetCoverTopHeight), capped by CoverLower_MaxStand / CoverLower_MaxCrouch. 0 out of cover and when standing behind low cover (aiming over it). Called by the character ABPs (Update_CoverLower) on every machine. GetCoverOrientationIntent CurrentIntent (Vector) bInCover (Boolean), Intent (Vector) Facing hook for the movement code: in cover returns the facing from the Facing settings (toward the wall, along it or back to it), the aim direction when aiming, or the wall while a vault turn is pending. Out of cover it returns CurrentIntent. GetCoverWallDistance (pure) bCrouched (Boolean), bSticky (Boolean) Distance (Float) Distance (cm) from the cover wall plane to the pawn center that the wall spring holds: the WallDistance_{Stand,Crouch}{Auto,Sticky} gap picked by crouch and sticky state, plus the pawn capsule radius. Read by the Mover cover mode (AdjustDesiredMove) and the CMC adapter (ShapeCoverMoveInput). IsCoverAiming (pure) ReturnValue (Boolean) True while aiming from cover (CoverAimPose is not None). Local owner only; not replicated. IsCoverCrouchBlocked (pure) ReturnValue (Boolean) Crouch is blocked: during a cover run (and its grace time), or while standing up to aim over low cover. Pawns use it for their crouch input. IsCoverCrouching (pure) bCrouching (Boolean) Pawn hook: true while the owning pawn is crouched. Override in the pawn-specific cover component (Mover / CMC). IsCoverMovementAllowed (pure) bAllowed (Boolean) Pawn hook: true while the pawn moves in a mode where cover is allowed (on the ground or already in cover). Override in the pawn-specific cover component (Mover / CMC). DoCoverTapAction Location (Vector), bRelease (Boolean) The tap action, sticky first: soft cover becomes sticky; sticky cover exits (on release only); out of cover takes sticky cover nearby, else (on release) runs to the far target. EnterStickyCover Point (Vector), Normal (Vector) Starts sticky cover on the wall at Point and Normal: ends any cover run, sets bStickyCover, resets the exit timer and writes the cover state. ExitCover Leaves sticky cover: clears bStickyCover and the cover state and starts a 0.5 s re-entry cooldown. HandleStickyToggle Location (Vector), DeltaSeconds (Float) Per frame on the owner: counts the cover button hold time and applies toggle requests (enter, upgrade to sticky), then searches for a cover target while held and starts a cover run or snaps to cover under the crosshair. ReleaseStickyCover Cover button released: clears bCoverButtonHeld, which cancels a cover run, and flags the release for HandleStickyToggle. RequestStickyCover Cover button pressed: requests a sticky cover toggle when sticky cover is enabled and allowed in this camera, and marks the button as held. TakeStickyCover Location (Vector) bTaken (Boolean) Out of cover: takes sticky cover on the wall in front (camera forward, within CoverEnterDistance), else on the targeted cover when it is within StickyCoverReach. Returns whether cover was taken. UpdateCoverHold Location (Vector) Cover button held past StickyTapTime: runs to the far target first; without one, takes sticky cover when out of cover (retried every frame while held). UpdateCoverPress Location (Vector) Cover button press: cancels a running cover run; with a far run target the press waits for hold or tap (bCoverPressPending); otherwise the tap action runs at once. UpdateCoverRelease Location (Vector) Cover button release: a quick release of a waiting press does the tap action (sticky first); otherwise a quick unused tap in sticky cover exits it. RequestCoverVault bDeferred (Boolean) Jump pressed in cover: when the character does not face the wall closely enough (VaultFacingDot) it starts turning to the wall first and returns true. Returns false when the vault can start directly. UpdateCoverVault DeltaSeconds (Float) Per frame while a vault turn is pending: counts the turn time and calls OnCoverVaultReady once the character faces the wall or VaultFacingTimeout passes. Cancels when cover is lost.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: • OnCoverVaultReady (event dispatcher): Dispatcher called when the character faces the wall (or the facing timeout passed) after a vault from cover was requested; the pawn then starts the traversal.

docs.title: Settings

docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description GetEquipmentMesh (pure) bFirstPerson (Boolean) Mesh (PrimitiveComponent ref) Mesh of the spawned equipment for hand IK sockets: the first first-person or third-person primitive of its AC_FirstPersonRendering (generated FP copies or tagged components), else its first MeshComponent. No rendering tags needed. GetHandIK SocketName (Name), TargetBoneName (Name), bIsFirstPerson (Boolean) Result (Transform), Result_Location (Vector), Result_Rotation (Rotator), Result_Scale (Vector) Returns an equipment socket's transform in the bone space of TargetBoneName on the TP or FP attach mesh. Returns identity if the equipment or meshes are invalid. UpdateHandIK Recomputes all six hand IK transforms (left, right, ADS; TP and FP) from the spawned equipment: the equipment data's HandIKSocket / ADSSocket in the space of LeftHandBone / RightHandBone. Called after spawning and every tick by the bow. InitializeSystem ParentPawn (Pawn ref), ParentMesh_TP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), ParentMesh_FP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), AttachMesh_TP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref), AttachMesh_FP (SkeletalMeshComponent ref) Stores the pawn and mesh references, spawns the initial equipment and binds cleanup to the pawn's OnDestroyed. Called by the owning character. DestroySpawnedActors DestroyedActor (Actor ref) Bound to the parent pawn's OnDestroyed. Destroys the spawned equipment actor so it does not outlive its owner. LinkFirstPersonOverlayPose Links the slot's OverlayPose_FP onto the first-person lead mesh (ParentMesh_FP) and the first-person attach mesh, skipping a mesh that does not exist: a third-person-only pawn (AllowedPerspectives without FirstPerson) builds no first-person meshes. Called by UpdateEquipment. LinkThirdPersonOverlayPose Links the third-person overlay pose for the current slot. An item that spawns an actor links its own pose (EquipmentData OverlayPose_TP). With nothing in hand (Unequip) the pawn's AC_OverlaySystem applies its selected stance (Default, Injured, HandsTied...), so a stance chosen on the pawn survives spawn and unequipping; without an overlay system the slot's pose is linked as before. Called by UpdateEquipment. UpdateEquipment Destroys the old equipment, evaluates CHT_Equipment for the selected slot, links the overlay anim layers, spawns the actor, attaches its TP and FP parts and refreshes hand IK. Called from EndPlay, so a pawn destroyed with the menu open does not leave the game slowed down. ConfirmEquipmentMenu Equips HighlightedEquipment (SelectNewEquipment) and closes the menu. docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Function Inputs Outputs Description Get_FirstPersonBob (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Bob target from the bob shape curves at the current phase, scaled by the speed curve; zero in the air. Get_FirstPersonBreathing (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Breathing target: slow vertical motion and pitch. Get_FirstPersonLookSway (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Look sway target: lag opposite to the view turn rate (through the look response curve), roll from yaw, clamped. Get_FirstPersonMoveSway (pure) Profile (PDA_FirstPersonMotion ref) Position (Vector), Rotation (Vector) Move sway target: roll and side shift into strafes, pull back when moving forward, clamped. Update_FirstPersonMotion Computes the motion rig inputs: sums look sway, move sway, bob and breathing from the active profile, applies the ADS, crouch, intensity and disable_fp_motion scales, and sets the spring settings and pivot. Update_FirstPersonMotionInputs Reads what the motion needs this frame: profile, look rates and velocity, in air / crouched, breathing time, aim alpha, bob and kicks, and the disable_fp_motion curve. Update_FirstPersonMotionKicks Bob phase (advanced by ground distance) and the one-frame jump and landing kicks from the active profile. Update_FirstPersonMotionLook Look rates (degrees per second) from the aim rotation change, and the pawn velocity in the view yaw frame. Update_FirstPersonMotionProfile Active motion profile: the equipped item's FirstPersonMotionProfile, else the character's (AC_FirstPersonRendering), and the motion intensity. Update_ADSSettings Per-weapon ADS settings from the equipped item (PDA_Equipment ADSEnterSpeed, ADSExitSpeed, ADSHandOffset) for CR_FirstPerson_ADS; keeps the last values when nothing is equipped. Update_FirstPersonMode Game thread: copies the AC_FirstPersonRendering mode settings, sets bTrueFirstPerson and bFirstPersonRunADS and computes the ADS and hand IK weights. Update_PropertiesFromCharacter Game thread: reads the pawn animation properties and the retarget setup (retargeter, logic mesh, bRetargetOverlay, bLogicOnly). Update_Values Thread-safe: sets bDisableOverlay, the enable_cr_fp_* and hand IK curve values, ControllerPitch and the aim offset and head pitch inputs.
