docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
Each system lives in its own folder under /GASPALS/Systems and is a component on the pawn. They are independent: a pawn uses the ones it needs. Every page follows the same order: what the system does, how it works, configuration, Blueprint API, networking and limitations. The full settings of each are in the reference.

  • Camera

    Gameplay Cameras with a camera director: four perspectives, styles, crouch and cover offsets, crosshair.

  • Cover

    Soft and sticky cover, cover run, corner turns, vault, aim from cover, pose lowering.

  • Equipment

    Data-driven items with overlay poses, attach sockets and hand IK.

  • First person

    Full-body first person built at runtime, three modes, aim down sights.

  • Overlay

    ALS-style overlay poses and body styles blended by curves.

  • Ragdoll and interactions

    Ragdoll on both pawns, physical animation, get-ups, takedowns and shoves.

  • Debug tools

    Demo shot into ragdoll, spawn or rotate characters, teleport and fly on the Mover pawn.

  • Traversal

    Vault, hurdle and mantle with ledge detection and motion warping.

  • Movement

    Gaits, rotation modes, speeds, Mover modes and transitions, slide.

docs.title: Camera system
docs.text:
The camera is built on Unreal's Gameplay Cameras. A Blueprint camera director picks camera rigs every frame from the character's state, and the component AC_CameraSystem handles the perspective, attaches the camera to the right mesh, and draws the crosshair.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem Component AC_CameraSystem (on both pawns) Camera asset CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter (the pawns' Gameplay Camera component uses it) Director CameraDirector_SandboxCharacter (Blueprint camera director) Rigs Rigs/ (chooser tables CHT_CameraRig* and camera rigs) Widget W_Crosshair Camera shake CameraShake_Basic (played by the takedown montages' camera shake notify) Input Perspective 1, style 2, shoulder Alt / ++r3++ Settings Camera reference

docs.title: Perspectives
docs.text:
Perspective Camera Attached to ThirdPerson (default) Over-the-shoulder camera with collision push and damping. The visible mesh's Third Person Camera Bone (root) TopDown Fixed-angle camera above the character; the character aims at the mouse cursor or with the right stick. The visible mesh's Third Person Camera Bone (root) SideScroller Fixed side view; aims like top-down. The visible mesh's root FirstPerson Eye camera on the first-person mesh. See First person. The first-person lead mesh's First Person Camera Bone (VB Camera virtual bone, set per character on AC_FirstPersonRendering)

1 cycles through Allowed Perspectives in their order. By default: third person, top-down, side-scroller, first person, back to third person. The visible mesh is the retargeted character's when one is active, so the camera follows it.

docs.title: Choosing the perspectives
docs.text:
Allowed Perspectives lists the views players can use. Common setups:

Game Allowed Perspectives Result First person only FirstPerson Starts in first person; 1 does nothing. Third person only ThirdPerson No first-person meshes are built; 1 does nothing. You can also delete AC_FirstPersonRendering from the pawn and the characters. Third and first person ThirdPerson, FirstPerson 1 toggles between them.

If Camera Perspective (the start view) is not in the list, the camera starts in the first allowed one and shows an on-screen warning. FirstPerson only counts as available when the pawn has AC_FirstPersonRendering. With only first person allowed, cover's First Person Sticky Cover setting SwitchToThirdPerson acts like Disabled (Cover); a Camera Perspective During Ragdoll that is not allowed keeps the current view.

docs.title: Styles
docs.text:
The style picks a variant per perspective. 2 cycles it; DDCvar.CameraStyle sets it too.

Style Third person Top-down / side-scroller Style_1 Close CameraRig_TD_1 / CameraRig_SS_1 Style_2 (default) Medium _2 Style_3 Far _3 Style_4 Debug view (CameraRig_DebugView) _4

docs.title: How the rig is chosen
docs.text:
Every frame the director:

  1. Reads the pawn's Get_PropertiesForCamera: perspective, style, mode (Free, Strafe or Aim, from the pawn's rotation mode and aim input), shoulder side and stance.
  2. Evaluates the chooser table CHT_CameraRig, which branches by perspective into CHT_CameraRigs_ThirdPerson, _FirstPerson, _TopDown or _SideScroller. Third person picks by style and mode: nine rigs CameraRig_TP_<Close|Medium|Far>_<Freecam|Strafe|Aim>; the Aim rigs blend in smoothly. The fallback is CameraRig_TP_Medium_Freecam.
  3. Activates the result, and the First Person Scale Rig in first person when the character uses the Split first-person mode.
  4. In third person (except the debug style), stacks the offset rigs from Camera Offset Rigs on AC_CameraSystem:
Entry Default rig When Offset Crouch Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Crouch Crouched 50 cm down Right Shoulder Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Right Right shoulder (or a cover edge on the right) 100 cm side Cover Low Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow Behind low cover 80 cm up Cover Edge Right Rig / Cover Edge Left Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeRight / Left At a cover wall end 60 cm to the open side First Person Scale Rig CameraRig_FP_Scale First person, Split mode First-person scale 0.25 (keeps arms and weapon out of walls) In Air Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_InAir Jumping or falling 30 cm back, 20 cm up Sliding Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Sliding Sliding (Mover pawn) 30 cm down Traversing Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Traversing Vaulting or climbing 40 cm back Ragdoll Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Ragdoll Ragdolling in third person 60 cm back, 40 cm up

Each pawn sets its own rigs on its camera component, so two characters can use different offsets. Point an entry at your own rig to change an offset, or clear it to turn that offset off. The director's own Camera Offset Rigs is only used for a pawn without AC_CameraSystem.

The chooser table itself is fixed in the director (the engine's Evaluate Chooser node takes the table as a node setting, not an input). To change which main rig is used when, edit CHT_CameraRig and its nested tables, or duplicate them and the director.

First person needs no crouch offset: the first-person camera follows the head bone, so it lowers with the head when the character crouches (about 26 cm, measured on the Mover pawn with the UEFN mannequin).

The persistent layers CameraRig_Layer_Global and CameraRig_Layer_Base are activated when the director starts.

The base rigs hold the shared parameters, and the variants override them:

Base rig Parameters ThirdPerson/CameraRig_TP_Base Boom arm offset, camera offset, field of view, forward / lateral / vertical damping, collision push TopDown/CameraRig_TopDown_Base, SideScroller/CameraRig_SideScroller_Base Camera translation and rotation, field of view, damping FirstPerson/CameraRig_FP_Base Field of view, offset, a First Person node (keeps first-person meshes out of the third-person shadow; do not remove it)

To change the look, open the rigs in the Gameplay Cameras editor. To change which rig is used when, edit the chooser tables. See Customize the camera.

docs.title: Crosshair and aim
docs.text:
For the locally controlled player, AC_CameraSystem creates the Crosshair Widget Class (default W_Crosshair) and keeps it centered on the aim point:

  • Third and first person: a line trace (Aim Trace Channel, default Visibility; Aim Trace Distance, default 100 m) from the camera along its forward vector; the dot sits where it hits.
  • Top-down and side-scroller: the world point under the mouse cursor (Fixed Camera Mouse Aim Type), or with a gamepad, 3 m out along the right stick direction.

GetCrosshairAim returns the aim origin, direction, point, whether it hit, and a flattened direction. The pawns pass it on through the pawn interface function Get_AimRay (with the trace channel and distance), which is what cover targeting and aim from cover read; aim from cover traces with the same channel and length, so the crosshair and the cover line of fire never disagree.

The camera component only creates and places the crosshair, at the point the aim ray hits. The widget decides how it looks: W_Crosshair is a dot in its Default Color (white). Cover targets are shown by the cover marker, not the crosshair; a custom crosshair can still ask the cover system (IsCoverTargeted).

Turn Show Crosshair off to hide the dot (it is collapsed, not destroyed). The aim ray, cover targeting and the cover marker keep working.

docs.title: Ragdoll camera
docs.text: With Change Perspective During Ragdoll on (default), the camera switches to Camera Perspective During Ragdoll (top-down) while the CMC pawn ragdolls (AC_RagdollSystem), and back afterwards. It only switches when that perspective is in Allowed Perspectives. Allow Camera Control During Ragdoll decides whether the player can still look around. The Mover pawn uses its own ragdoll (a movement mode) and keeps the camera.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
On AC_CameraSystem:

Setting Default Use Camera Perspective ThirdPerson Start perspective. Must be in Allowed Perspectives. Allowed Perspectives ThirdPerson, TopDown, SideScroller, FirstPerson Views the player can use; 1 cycles them in this order. Third Person Camera Bone root Bone or socket the third-person and top-down cameras attach to. Camera Style Medium (Style_2) Start style. Is Camera Right Shoulder false Start shoulder. Show Crosshair true Show the crosshair dot for the local player. Crosshair Widget Class W_Crosshair Any User Widget; it is added to the viewport and centered on the aim point. Camera Offset Rigs the ten rigs above Offset rigs the director stacks on the main rig. Clear an entry to turn that offset off. Pass Movement Mode To Camera true The pawn tells the camera whether it is on the ground, in the air, sliding, traversing or ragdolling, for the movement mode rigs (and for your own chooser rows). Off = always on the ground. The CMC pawn has no slide. Aim Trace Channel Visibility Channel of the aim ray (crosshair, aim from cover). Aim Trace Distance 10000 Length of the aim ray in cm. Change Perspective During Ragdoll true See above. Camera Perspective During Ragdoll TopDown See above. Allow Camera Control During Ragdoll false See above. Fixed Camera Mouse Aim Type MouseTraceWithPositionFallback Fixed cameras: aim at the world point under the cursor, or use the cursor's screen position.

DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable (project setting, default on) must stay on. Off, the pawns fall back to a plain spring arm camera and none of this runs.

docs.title: Using the camera from Blueprints
docs.text: Call Use SetCameraPerspective(NewPerspective) Change the perspective (re-attaches the camera, tells the server, fires OnCameraPerspectiveChanged). OnCameraPerspectiveChanged Event dispatcher with the new perspective. First-person rendering listens to it. IsPerspectiveAvailable(Perspective) True when the perspective is allowed (and, for first person, the pawn has AC_FirstPersonRendering). GetNextAvailablePerspective, GetFirstAvailablePerspective What 1 would switch to; the fallback start view. GetCrosshairAim The aim ray and point. Only valid for player-controlled pawns. Get_AimRay (pawn interface) The same ray plus the trace channel and distance; zeros when the pawn has no camera system or no player controller. CameraPerspective, CameraStyle, bIsCameraRightShoulder Current state.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: The perspective is set on the owning client and sent to the server (Server_SetCameraPerspective); it replicates to other machines. Style, shoulder and crosshair are local to the player.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• A new style or mode needs matching chooser rows and rigs.
  • The offset rigs (crouch, shoulder, cover) apply in third person only.
  • The main rig chooser table can't be swapped per pawn (see How the rig is chosen).
  • Rig graph edits need the Gameplay Cameras editor; save each rig asset after editing.

docs.title: Cover system
docs.text:
The cover system lets a character take cover against walls and low obstacles, move along them, run from cover to cover, turn around corners, vault over cover and aim from it. It works on both sample pawns and in multiplayer.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/CoverSystem Components AC_CoverSystem_Base (core), AC_CoverSystem_Mover or AC_CoverSystem_CMC (adapter). Both sample pawns name it AC_CoverSystem. Mover assets BP_MovementMode_Cover, BP_MovementTransition_Cover, input struct S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover Animation CR_Humanoid_CoverLower at the end of both character Anim Blueprints Widgets W_CoverMarker (cover marker), crosshair tint in W_Crosshair Input IA_Cover (sticky cover and cover run), plus the regular move, crouch, aim and jump inputs Level needs Walls the traces can hit; a NavMeshBoundsVolume for cover runs around obstacles Settings Cover reference

docs.title: Kinds of cover
docs.text:
Soft (auto) coverSticky coverLow cover

Walk into a wall and the character takes cover. It is kept while the character stays close to the wall and is left by moving away from it. Corners and wall ends release soft cover, unless the camera still looks at a wall.

Soft cover is what most "walk up to a wall and hug it" games do. Turn it off with Enable Auto Cover.

Press the cover button (IA_Cover) and the character snaps to the wall under the crosshair. Sticky cover pulls the character to the wall, always stops at wall ends, allows corner turns, and is only left deliberately: a quick tap of the cover button, a firm push away from the wall, a cover run, a vault or aiming out of it.

Pressing the button in soft cover upgrades it to sticky cover. Turn the button off with Enable Sticky Cover.

A wall that does not reach High Cover Height (148 cm above the character's feet) is low cover. The character crouches behind it (Auto Crouch Low Cover), the camera rises over it, and aiming can stand up over it. A standing character takes low cover only through sticky cover or by crouching in front of it, and standing up leaves soft low cover.

docs.title: What the player can do
docs.text:
Action Input (demo) Result Take soft cover Move into a wall The character turns to its cover facing and moves along the wall. Take sticky cover Tap Q (IA_Cover) Snaps to the wall in front or under the crosshair, within Sticky Cover Reach (250 cm). A tap prefers sticky cover even when farther cover is targeted. Leave sticky cover Tap Q again, or push away from the wall A tap must be shorter than Sticky Tap Time (0.25 s). Cover run Hold Q while aiming at farther cover Held past Sticky Tap Time, sprints to the cover under the crosshair, up to Cover Run Range (15 m), and takes sticky cover there, also from sticky cover and right in front of other cover. The run finishes after the button is released; press Q again to cancel it. Off with Enable Cover Run. Move along cover Move left or right Stops at wall ends (sticky always, soft with Stop At Edges). Turn a corner Hold toward the wall end in sticky cover After Corner Turn Hold Time (0.3 s) the character moves around the corner if a side wall is there. Chained corners keep following the wall. Crouch C Crouches. Behind low cover the character crouches by itself. Vault Space Turns to the wall if needed, then vaults over it with the traversal system. Aim from cover Hold Right Button Picks the least exposed pose that can hit the target (see below).

The cover marker (a widget on the targeted wall) shows where the cover button will take the character.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The core component evaluates cover every frame on the owning machine, then hands the result to the movement back end.

flowchart LR
    Input[Move input<br>camera, cover button] --> Eval[EvaluateCover<br>AC_CoverSystem_Base]
    Eval -->|Mover| MoverIn[S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover<br>in the Mover input]
    MoverIn --> Mode[BP_MovementMode_Cover<br>along-wall movement, wall spring]
    Eval -->|CMC| Shape[ShapeCoverMoveInput<br>shaped acceleration]
    Shape --> CMC[Character Movement Component]
    Eval --> Facing[GetCoverOrientationIntent<br>facing]
    Eval --> Cam[GetCoverCameraState<br>camera director offsets]
    Eval --> Pose[GetCoverLowerAmount<br>CR_Humanoid_CoverLower]
  1. Sensing. Sphere traces (Cover Trace Radius) in the move direction find a wall within Cover Enter Distance. A second trace at High Cover Height above the feet decides high or low cover (the same standing or crouched, so walls near that height don't flip between the two). Probes at Edge Probe Offset to each side find the wall ends and corners.
  2. Deciding. The move input must point into the wall (Cover Enter Input Dot). Cover is kept while the wall is within Cover Hold Distance, and left after the input points away from it (Cover Exit Input Dot) for Cover Exit Delay.
  3. Moving. In cover, the move input is turned into movement along the wall, and a spring holds the capsule at the Wall Distance gap for the current case (stand or crouch, soft or sticky).
    • Mover: the cover data travels in the Mover input (S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover). BP_MovementTransition_Cover switches between Walking and the Cover mode; BP_MovementMode_Cover moves along the wall (walk 150 cm/s, run and sprint 250 cm/s) and runs the wall spring.
    • CMC: AC_CoverSystem_CMC shapes the acceleration before the Character Movement Component runs, and turns the mesh to the cover facing.
  4. Facing. Four settings pick the facing per case: FaceWall, ShoulderToWall (along the wall, in the move direction) or BackToWall.
  5. Camera. The camera director reads GetCoverCameraState: it raises the camera behind low cover (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow), offsets it at wall ends (CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeLeft/Right) and swaps the shoulder toward the open side. Enable Cover Camera Offsets turns off the raise and the wall-end offset; Enable Cover Shoulder Switch keeps the camera on the player's shoulder in cover.
  6. Pose. CR_Humanoid_CoverLower lowers the pelvis so the head stays under the cover top, and plants the legs on the animated feet.

docs.title: Cover run
docs.text:
Hold the cover button while the crosshair is on cover beyond Sticky Cover Reach. The character sprints along a navigation path to a stand point 60 cm in front of the wall, slows down for the arrival (Cover Run Arrive Speed, Cover Run Brake Decel) and snaps into sticky cover at Cover Run Arrive Distance. A new press of the cover button, a blocked path or a time limit (path length at 5 m/s plus Cover Run Max Time) cancel the run; releasing the button does not.

When farther cover is targeted, the press waits to see whether it is a tap or a hold: released within Sticky Tap Time it does the sticky action (soft cover becomes sticky, sticky cover is left, a wall within Sticky Cover Reach in front is taken; with none, it runs); held longer it runs. Without farther cover the tap acts at once.

Turn it off with Enable Cover Run. The cover button then only takes cover within Sticky Cover Reach, and the marker only shows for cover the button can take from where the character stands.

The path comes from the navigation mesh (FindPathToLocationSynchronously). Without a navmesh, or when no path is found, the character runs in a straight line and can get blocked. Clients build their own path, which needs bAllowClientSideNavigation=True in the project settings.

docs.title: Corner turn
docs.text: In sticky cover, hold the move input toward a wall end. If the wall continues around the corner (an outside corner up to Corner Turn Angle, 100 degrees between the two wall normals, with at least Corner Turn Min Width of wall), the character walks around it and stays in cover. The held input keeps working after the turn, so a round pillar or a run of corners is followed in one go.

docs.title: Vault from cover
docs.text: Jump in cover asks for a vault (RequestCoverVault). If the character does not face the wall within Vault Facing Dot, it turns first (up to Vault Facing Timeout). The component then fires the OnCoverVaultReady dispatcher; the pawn handles it and starts the traversal. If the traversal finds nothing to vault, the Mover pawn falls back to a jump.

docs.title: Aim from cover
docs.text:
With Enable Cover Aim on (default), aiming in cover does not leave cover. The character takes the least exposed pose that can hit what the camera aims at, faces the aim direction, and walks back to its cover spot when aim is released.

Pose Meaning Exposure InPlace Stay at the cover spot (crouched behind low cover). Lowest EdgeLeft, EdgeRight Step out past the end of the wall. Medium Over Stand up behind low cover. Highest

The order is: in place, then the edge the aim points toward, then the other edge, then over. A pose "can hit" when a line from its muzzle position (Cover Aim Muzzle Height Stand/Crouch) reaches the target. The target is found along the camera direction from standing eye height above the cover spot, so the choice does not chase the camera as it moves with the pose. Aiming at your own cover counts as aiming past it.

Switching is damped so the pose does not flicker: a more exposed pose is taken only after the current one has been blocked for Cover Aim Blocked Delay, and a safer pose is taken back only after it has been clearly valid for Cover Aim Return Delay. With Cover Aim Keep Standing (default), a character standing over low cover only crouches back down, never side-steps to an edge.

While aiming, pushing away from the wall leaves cover and keeps aiming. Lateral input is ignored. The camera drops its low-cover offset and takes the shoulder of the side the character stepped out to. Turn on Cover Aim Debug to print every pose change and draw the target.

docs.title: Pose lowering
docs.text:
CR_Humanoid_CoverLower runs at the end of SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP and SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP. It measures the cover top with a trace down into the wall and lowers the pelvis until the capsule top is Cover Lower Head Clearance (5 cm) under it, clamped to Cover Lower Max Stand (10 cm) or Cover Lower Max Crouch (15 cm). Behind cover taller than the character it lowers nothing, and it does not lower while standing over low cover to aim. The amount is computed on every machine from the replicated cover state, so remote players look the same.

The rig uses the UEFN mannequin bone names (pelvis, thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l...). Retargeted characters get it through the animation skeleton.

docs.title: First person in cover
docs.text: Setting Options First Person Sticky Cover SwitchToThirdPerson (default): sticky cover switches the camera to third person and back when it ends. Disabled: the cover button does nothing in first person. First Person Auto Cover MovementOnly (default): walking into a wall gives cover movement (wall hug, edges), but the body follows the camera instead of the cover facing. Disabled: no auto cover in first person.

docs.title: Cover marker
docs.text: With Show Cover Marker on, the local player sees the Cover Marker Widget Class (default W_CoverMarker, Cover Marker Draw Size 100 x 12, Cover Marker Wall Offset 3 cm off the wall) on the cover under the crosshair. Other widgets can ask the cover system the same thing (IsCoverTargeted); the cover system never calls them. In cover, only farther cover (a cover run target) is marked; with Enable Cover Run off, only cover within Sticky Cover Reach is marked, and nothing while in cover. The marker is a widget component the system creates on demand; restyle it by editing W_CoverMarker or set your own widget class. Targeting and the marker run only for the locally controlled player. Cover reads the aim ray from the pawn interface function Get_AimRay, so a pawn without AC_CameraSystem can still provide one.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All settings are on the cover component of the pawn. Select AC_CoverSystem in the pawn's Components panel and look under Cover in the Details panel. The categories are:

Category Controls General Master switches: Enable Cover, Enable Auto Cover, Enable Sticky Cover, Enable Cover Run, Engage Rule (Automatic or WhileCrouched), Move Into Cover, Auto Crouch Low Cover. Detection Trace distances, radius, low/high cover height, edge probes, how sharp a bend cover follows; Cover Top Probe Height (300 cm, walls taller than this count as this high) and the advanced Cover Probe Padding (20 cm). Movement Wall gaps per case, the wall spring, pull and push speeds, stopping at edges in soft cover; Cover Side Input Threshold (0.2, sideways stick needed to move along the wall, peek or turn a corner). Facing Facing style per case, shoulder yaw offsets (and on the CMC adapter, the mesh turn speed). Exit How firmly and how long to push away to leave soft and sticky cover. Sticky Cover button reach and tap time, and Sticky Reentry Cooldown (0.5 s before cover can grab the character again after leaving it). CoverRun Range, time limit, path following and arrival; Cover Run Expected Speed (500, plans the time limit), Cover Run Stand Offset (60 cm from the wall), Cover Run Crouch Block Time (0.4 s) and Cover Run Reentry Delay (0.2 s) after a run. CornerTurn Hold time, corner angle and width. Traversal Facing needed before a vault, and its timeout. Aim Aim from cover: switch, muzzle heights, damping, edge clearance. Debug Enable Debug (draws every cover trace for one frame) and Cover Aim Debug (prints aim pose changes and draws the aim target). Pose Pelvis lowering limits and head clearance. FirstPerson Behavior when the camera is in first person. Camera Enable Cover Camera Offsets (low-cover raise, wall-end offset) and Enable Cover Shoulder Switch (camera moves to the open side at a wall end). Marker Cover marker on or off, its widget class, draw size and wall offset, and the crosshair color on a cover target. Collision Cover Trace Channel (default Cover): the channel of every cover probe. Mover / CMC Adapter settings: the Mover's cover and ground mode names; the CMC's forced crouch delay and mesh turn speed.

Every setting with its default is in the Cover reference. Recipes for common setups (no auto cover, Gears-style sticky only, crouch-only cover, wider wall gaps) are in Configure cover behavior.

Check settings on the pawn's component

Enable Cover and Auto Crouch Low Cover are on by default, so adding a cover component to your own pawn enables cover without further setup; the sample pawns also set them on their components. Check settings on the pawn's component rather than on the class: a value changed in AC_CoverSystem_Base does not reach pawns that already set their own.

docs.title: What counts as cover
docs.text:
Cover probes trace the Cover channel. Every collision profile answers it like Visibility, so anything that blocks visibility is cover, and characters, triggers and invisible walls are not. To change that per object, set its collision to Custom and change the Cover response:

  • Ignore: the object is never cover (foliage, a fence you see through, a prop too small to hide behind).
  • Block: the object is cover even if it ignores Visibility.

To trace another channel (for example Visibility in a project without the Cover channel), set Cover Trace Channel on the pawn's cover component. Aiming from cover traces the camera's Aim Trace Channel instead (see Camera), so a wall that isn't cover still blocks shots.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
• Mover pawn. The cover state is part of the Mover input, so the server and the other clients run the same cover movement as the owner. Simulated proxies get it through the synced inputs. No extra replication is needed.
  • CMC pawn. The owner shapes its own acceleration (replicated by the CMC). The cover state is sent to the server about 20 times a second (ServerUpdateCover) and replicated to other machines, which apply it in ApplyRemoteCoverState. Small corrections (2 to 4 cm) can happen at sticky edge stops and corners.
  • Aim from cover runs on the owner only. Other machines see its result: position, crouch and facing.
  • Cover run paths are built on each client, so bAllowClientSideNavigation must be on.

docs.title: Using cover from Blueprints
docs.text:
Call On Use RequestStickyCover / ReleaseStickyCover Base Cover button pressed / released (sticky cover, tap and cover run). EvaluateCover Base Runs the cover logic for this frame. Mover pawns call it in ProduceInput; the CMC adapter calls it from UpdateCoverCMC. RequestCoverVault Base Ask for a vault from cover; listen to OnCoverVaultReady to start the traversal. IsCoverAiming Base True while aiming from cover. GetCoverCameraState Base Low cover, edge side and shoulder side (each already filtered by the camera settings), for your own camera logic. GetCoverOrientationIntent Base The facing the pawn should turn to. IsCoverTargeted Base True while the cover button would take the local player to cover (what the marker and the green crosshair show). UpdateCoverCMC CMC adapter Call before the CMC updates (the sample pawn calls it from AC_PreCMCTick). UpdateMoverCoverState Mover adapter Keeps the in-cover flag in step with the Cover mode, every tick.

The CMC pawn's state is also readable on any machine from the component's CoverState. To put cover on your own pawn, follow Add the systems to your own pawn.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Cover needs walls the traces can hit (the Cover channel by default). Very thin walls (under 10 cm) count as tall for the pose lowering.
  • Peek (leaning out without aiming) is not implemented.
  • The cover run runs straight when no navmesh path exists, and can then be blocked.
  • The pose-lowering rig expects the UEFN mannequin bone names.
  • In first person, only the two behaviors of the First Person settings are available.
  • The CMC pawn shows small corrections at sticky edge stops and corners in network play.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:

  • Configure cover behavior
  • Camera system for the cover camera rigs
  • Traversal system for vaulting

docs.title: Debug tools
docs.text: /GASPALS/Systems/DebugTools/AC_DebugTools is a component on SandboxCharacter_Mover that groups the sandbox's demo and debug tools: shooting characters into ragdoll, spawning or rotating characters, teleporting and flying. It works on any SandboxCharacter_Mover (or a child of it), in any game mode; RagdollLevel, with its placed target characters and physics obstacles, is the place to try it.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Input Condition Action Left Button aim held (Right Button) Shoot: the character hit goes ragdoll, with an impulse at the bone that was hit. Without aim, Left Button is a takedown. E aim held Spawn or rotate: rotate the character you aim at by 90 degrees, or spawn a new character on the floor where you aim. Without aim, E is a shove or a bench interaction. J Teleport to the point under the view. Z keyboard only Fly: toggle the Mover Flying mode.

N (next pawn) and M (next character) belong to the player controller, not to this component. See Controls.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Shoot. The component takes the view from the pawn's camera. The server traces along it; when it hits a Mover character, that character ragdolls and the impulse is applied to the bone that was hit once its body is simulating.
  • Spawn or rotate. The server traces along the view. A Mover character hit is turned 90 degrees; anything else spawns a new character of the same class at the hit point (or at the end of the trace), facing you. Only the last Max Spawned Characters spawned characters are kept: the oldest is destroyed.
  • Teleport. The player controller (PC_Sandbox) asks the pawn's debug tools to teleport it. A sphere trace runs from the eyes along the view; the pawn moves just off the surface hit, or to the end of the trace. Pawns without the component (the CMC pawn) use the controller's own teleport, with the controller's Teleport Max Distance.
  • Fly. Switches the Mover pawn between the Flying mode and falling, with an on-screen message.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings on the AC_DebugTools component of the Mover pawn:

Setting Category Default Use Enable Debug Tools Debug Tools > General true Master switch for the shot, spawn / rotate, teleport and fly tools of this component. Shot Trace Distance Debug Tools > Demo 100000 Length of the shot trace in cm. Shot Impulse Debug Tools > Demo 2500 Impulse applied to the bone hit by a shot. Spawn Trace Distance Debug Tools > Demo 1000 Reach of the spawn / rotate trace in cm; with no hit the character spawns at the end of the trace. Max Spawned Characters Debug Tools > Demo 3 Spawned characters kept alive; the oldest is destroyed beyond this. Teleport Max Distance Debug Tools > Teleport 10000 Reach of the teleport trace in cm.

Shipping a game

Turn Enable Debug Tools off on your pawn, or remove the component, so players can't spawn characters or teleport. The component is optional: nothing else in GASPALS depends on it.

The full variable and function list is in the Pawns and Anim Blueprints reference.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
Tool How it replicates Shoot The owner sends its view to the server (reliable server RPC); the server traces and starts the ragdoll, and the impulse is multicast to every machine. Spawn or rotate The owner sends its view to the server (reliable server RPC). Spawned characters replicate as actors. Rotating another player's pawn is done by that player's machine (a replicated counter tells it to turn), so its own prediction doesn't undo it. Teleport, fly Run locally on the owner, so they work in standalone and for the listen server host. A client's teleport or fly is overridden by the server: both are single-player debug helpers.

In a listen server test, expect one correction when the host shoots or rotates a client's pawn.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The component needs SandboxCharacter_Mover (or a child) as its owner; on another pawn it does nothing.
  • The demo shot is a debug tool, not a weapon system: no damage, ammunition or effects.
  • The movement debug shapes (DDCvar.DrawCharacterDebugShapes) are drawn by the Mover pawn itself, not by this component.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Ragdoll and interactions
  • Mover and CMC pawns

docs.title: Equipment system
docs.text:
The equipment system puts an item in the character's hands. Selecting an item spawns its actor, attaches it to a hand socket, links the item's overlay poses (third and first person) and updates the hand IK targets. Items are described by data assets, so adding one needs no code.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem Component AC_EquipmentSystem (on both pawns) Data Data/PDA_Equipment (class), Data/DA_Equipment_<Item> (one per item), Data/CHT_Equipment (chooser), Data/Enum_Equipment (slots) Actors Actors/BP_Equipment_<Item> Menu UI/W_Switcher_Equipment, UI/W_Button_Equipment Input T (hold for the menu), mouse wheel / D-pad to choose Settings Equipment reference

docs.title: Included items
docs.text:
Slot Actor Third-person overlay First-person overlay Attach socket Unequip none ABP_Overlay_Default none none Rifle BP_Equipment_Rifle ABP_Overlay_Rifle ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle overlay_rifle Pistol BP_Equipment_Pistol ABP_Overlay_Pistol2H ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Pistol2H overlay_pistol Bow BP_Equipment_Bow ABP_Overlay_Bow ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Bow overlay_bow Torch BP_Equipment_Torch ABP_Overlay_Torch none overlay_torch Binoculars BP_Equipment_Binoculars ABP_Overlay_Binoculars none overlay_binoculars Box BP_Equipment_Box ABP_Overlay_Box none overlay_box Barrel BP_Equipment_Barrel ABP_Overlay_Barrel none overlay_barrel

The rifle, pistol and bow are skeletal meshes with HandIK and ADS sockets; the bow animates its string while you aim (Bow_AnimBP, driven by the actor's Draw value). The others are static meshes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Sel[SelectedEquipment<br>Enum_Equipment] --> Ch[CHT_Equipment<br>chooser]
    Ch --> DA[DA_Equipment_Item<br>PDA_Equipment]
    DA -->|Overlay Pose TP| L1[LinkAnimClassLayers<br>third-person mesh]
    DA -->|Overlay Pose FP| L2[LinkAnimClassLayers<br>first-person meshes]
    DA -->|Spawned Actor| Sp[Spawn actor<br>attach to socket]
    Sp --> IK[UpdateHandIK<br>IK_* transforms]
    IK --> ABP[Character Anim Blueprints<br>CR_Humanoid_HandIK]

When Selected Equipment changes (UpdateEquipment):

  1. The previous item's actor is destroyed.
  2. CHT_Equipment turns the slot into its data asset (fallback DA_Equipment_Unequip).
  3. Overlay Pose TP is linked on the pawn's third-person mesh; Overlay Pose FP on the first-person meshes. An empty Overlay Pose FP resets the first-person layers to their defaults.
  4. If the data asset has an actor class, the actor is spawned (owned by the pawn) and attached to the visible third-person mesh at Attach Socket TP, with Attach Offset TP.
  5. The actor's AC_FirstPersonRendering creates a first-person copy of its mesh, which is attached to the first-person mesh at Attach Socket FP with Attach Offset FP. Meshes tagged DoNotAttach are left where they are.
  6. UpdateHandIK computes the hand targets. It runs for every slot, so after Unequip (no actor) the hand IK transforms are reset instead of keeping the previous item's values.

docs.title: Hand IK
docs.text:
Two sockets on the item mesh place the hands (names set per item in the data asset):

Socket (default name) Use HandIK (Hand IK Socket) Where the support hand grips the item. ADS (ADS Socket) The sight point, lined up with the eye when aiming down sights in first person.

UpdateHandIK stores six transforms (IK_HandLeft, IK_HandRight, IK_ADS and their _FP versions), each expressed relative to the hand that holds the item (Left Hand Bone / Right Hand Bone on AC_EquipmentSystem, default hand_l / hand_r), so they follow it. The character Anim Blueprints (and the retarget and first-person Anim Blueprints) read them and run CR_Humanoid_HandIK. The hand IK weight comes from the overlay pose's enable_handik_l / enable_handik_r curves, so each pose decides when the support hand grips. Items without a HandIK socket (torch, box, barrel) rely on their overlay pose alone.

The bow moves its sockets as it draws, so it updates the hand IK every frame.

docs.title: Sockets on the character
docs.text: The items attach to overlay_* sockets on the character's Skeleton: overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_torch, overlay_binoculars, overlay_box, overlay_barrel. On the UEFN mannequin they hang from weapon_r / weapon_l; on the UE5 and MetaHuman skeletons from hand_r / hand_l. Retargeted characters need them on their own skeleton (see Add a retargeted character).

docs.title: The menu
docs.text:
Hold T: the world slows to Menu Time Dilation (0.35) and the Equipment Menu Widget Class (default W_Switcher_Equipment) opens with one button per Enum_Equipment value. Scroll up (mouse wheel up, D-pad up) to move the highlight up the list and down to move it down (it wraps at the ends); release T to equip it. A new enum value appears in the menu automatically.

The component owns the menu: it keeps the highlighted item (HighlightedEquipment), moves it on scroll and equips it on release. The widget only shows it, reading the component every frame, so a custom menu widget needs no calls from the component; read HighlightedEquipment (and SelectedEquipment) from the owning pawn's AC_EquipmentSystem.

If the pawn is destroyed while the menu is open, the component's EndPlay calls CloseEquipmentMenu: it removes the menu widget and sets the world speed back to normal.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text: When the pawn is destroyed, DestroySpawnedActors (bound to the pawn's On Destroyed) destroys the item actor.

docs.title: Data asset fields
docs.text:
PDA_Equipment:

Field Use ADS Enter Speed / ADS Exit Speed First-person aim down sights blend speeds for this item (15 / 5). ADS Hand Offset First person: moves the hands (and the item) toward or away from the eyes while aiming, in the head's space at the reference pose (0, 0, 0). Spawned Actor Actor class to spawn. Empty for Unequip. Overlay Pose TP Overlay Anim Blueprint linked on the third-person mesh (a child of ABP_OverlayPose_Base). Overlay Pose FP First-person overlay Anim Blueprint (a child of ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base). Optional. Attach Socket TP / FP Socket on the visible third-person / first-person mesh. Attach Offset TP / FP Transform relative to the socket. Is Left Handed The ADS target follows the left hand (the bow). Hand IK Socket / ADS Socket Socket names on the item mesh (HandIK, ADS).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
On AC_EquipmentSystem:

Setting Default Use Selected Equipment Unequip The item the pawn starts with (Equipment > Selection). Left Hand Bone / Right Hand Bone hand_l / hand_r Hand bones the hand IK targets are expressed in. Change them for skeletons with other hand names. Equipment Menu Widget Class W_Switcher_Equipment The menu opened while T is held. Any User Widget. Menu Time Dilation 0.35 World speed while the menu is open. 1 turns the slow motion off.

Everything else is runtime state. With no first-person meshes (first person not in the camera's Allowed Perspectives), the first-person links are skipped.

docs.title: Using equipment from Blueprints
docs.text: Call Use SelectNewEquipment(Slot) Equip a slot. Call it on the owning client or the server; it replicates. SelectedEquipment The current slot. SpawnedActor The current item actor. EquipmentData The current data asset. GetHandIK(Socket, TargetBone, bFirstPerson) A socket of the item in a hand bone's space.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Selected Equipment is replicated with a RepNotify. The owning client sets it and sends it to the server with one reliable RPC; every machine spawns and attaches its own copy of the item in the RepNotify.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The menu slows the whole world (also on a listen server host) while it is open.
  • The torch, binoculars, box and barrel have no first-person overlay pose.

docs.title: First person system
docs.text:
GASPALS first person shows the character's own body from its eyes, not floating arms. The first-person meshes are generated at runtime from lists you set on a component, so you never add or tag first-person components by hand. On top of the third-person pose, a first-person Anim Blueprint adds a stable camera, first-person arm poses, aim down sights (ADS) and an arm aim offset.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem Component AC_FirstPersonRendering (on the pawn, on each visual override, and on each equipment actor) Anim Blueprint ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN (and the template ABP_FirstPerson_Host for meshes on other skeletons) Control Rigs CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera, CR_FirstPerson_Camera, CR_FirstPerson_ADS, CR_FirstPerson_AimOffset Overlays ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base and its children (Rifle, Pistol2H, Bow) Camera rigs CameraRig_FP_Base, CameraRig_FP_Scale (Split mode) Tools Tools/EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh (cut a mesh into arms and body) Settings First person reference

Switch the camera to first person with the camera perspective input (see Controls). First person must be in the camera's Allowed Perspectives; without it the component builds nothing (Choosing the perspectives).

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Set First Person Mode on the character's AC_FirstPersonRendering.

FirstPersonOverlay (default)FirstPersonOverlaySplitTrueFirstPerson

First-person arm poses on the full body: the classic shooter look while keeping legs and shadow. Looking down, the arms follow the view pitch up to First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit (45 degrees) and the spine leans for the rest; the camera follows the lean by First Person Camera Follow Lean (0.75).

One full-body mesh (plus clothing). Needs First Person Retargeter on skeletons other than the UEFN mannequin.

The same image, but arms and body are separate meshes sharing one pose. The camera director adds CameraRig_FP_Scale, which draws the arms and the weapon at 0.25 scale toward the camera, so they do not clip into walls. The image looks the same; only depth changes.

Needs First Person Arms Meshes and First Person Body Meshes.

The third-person animation seen from the eyes, unchanged, plus ADS and a small, always-on weapon presentation (True First Person Weapon Presentation, 0.3: how far the weapon is pulled toward the sight line when not aiming). The head is pitched by the view. No first-person overlay poses.

Works on any skeleton, with no retargeter. Weapons can clip into walls.

docs.title: Mesh generation
docs.text:
When the pawn initializes its systems, AC_FirstPersonRendering.BuildFirstPersonMeshes creates the first-person meshes once:

  • Overlay modes: the first entry of First Person Full Meshes becomes the lead mesh: it runs the first-person Anim Blueprint. The other entries (clothing, hair) follow it.
  • Split mode: the first Arms mesh is the lead; the other arms meshes and all Body meshes follow.
  • Empty lists: the third-person mesh is reused as the lead, with the head bone hidden.

Every generated mesh is attached to the third-person mesh, visible to the owning player only, casts no shadow and only animates when rendered. Material overrides are copied from the matching third-person component (same mesh, or a mesh named <Name>_FP...). Followers that have their own skeleton and post-process Anim Blueprint (the MetaHuman hoodie and shoes) keep that Anim Blueprint, which copies the lead's pose and drives their corrective bones; other followers use leader pose.

When the camera switches perspective, the component swaps visibility: in first person the first-person meshes show for the owner and the third-person meshes become world-space representations (other players and shadows still see them).

docs.title: The first-person pose
docs.text:
ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN runs on the lead mesh:

flowchart TD
    A[Copy pose from the third-person mesh] --> B[CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera<br>VB Camera follows the body head]
    B --> C{Overlay?}
    C -->|TrueFirstPerson, montage, no overlay| E
    C -->|overlay modes| D[First-person overlay from spine_03 up<br>retargeted from the UEFN logic mesh if needed]
    D --> E[CR_FirstPerson_Camera<br>stable head, camera at the eyes]
    E --> F[CR_FirstPerson_ADS<br>hands to the sight line when aiming]
    F --> G[CR_FirstPerson_AimOffset<br>arms follow the view, spine leans]
    G --> H[Hand IK]
  1. Copy the third-person pose (all locomotion, montages and overlays come along).
  2. Body camera: VB Camera follows the body's head, smoothed vertically, so the view follows crouches, traversal and landings. That is why first person needs no crouch camera offset.
  3. Overlay: the first-person arm pose (ALI_OverlayFirstPerson) replaces the upper body from spine_03. On other skeletons it is retargeted from the pawn's hidden UEFN first-person logic mesh with First Person Retargeter.
  4. Camera rig: keeps the head stable, puts the head at its reference rotation (plus the view pitch) and places VB Camera at the eyes (First Person Eye Offset).
  5. ADS: while aiming, the hands move so the item's ADS socket sits on the sight line in front of the eye. The blend speeds and a hand offset come from the equipped item (ADS Enter Speed, ADS Exit Speed, ADS Hand Offset on its equipment data asset).
  6. Aim offset: the arms rotate with the view pitch up to the limits; the spine takes the rest.

The camera attaches to the lead mesh's First Person Camera Bone (VB Camera by default; by AC_CameraSystem).

docs.title: Equipment in first person
docs.text: Equipment actors have one mesh and their own AC_FirstPersonRendering. At runtime it creates one first-person copy of each mesh on the actor (same mesh, same anim class), attached to the source, visible to the owner only, with no collision. The equipment system attaches the copies to the first-person hand socket. In third person the copy is hidden; in first person it shows and the original becomes a world-space representation. Meshes you tag FirstPersonRendering or ThirdPersonRendering yourself are used as tagged instead. The first-person meshes the component generated itself are never copied again (IsGeneratedFirstPersonMesh), so a visual override actor gets one first-person mesh per source mesh.

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text: First-person overlay Blueprints (ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_<Item>) are linked by the equipment system from the item's data asset (Overlay Pose FP). They hold first-person arm poses and curves for the first-person rigs (enable_cr_fp_stable_arms, enable_cr_fp_stable_head, enable_cr_fp_ads, enable_cr_fp_aimoffset, hand IK). Rifle, Pistol2H and Bow have one; items without one show the third-person overlay in first person.

docs.title: Hand and item motion
docs.text:
On top of the first-person pose, the hands and the held item move with the player: they lag behind view turns, lean into strafes, bob with the steps, breathe at rest and take a jolt on jumps and landings. While aiming down sights the motion fades so the sight stays steady. The camera never moves.

  • The rig CR_FirstPerson_Motion (in ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN, after the aim offset and before the hand IK) moves both arms and the item together around a point in front of the eyes, with springs. The left hand stays on two-handed items.
  • The values come from motion profiles (PDA_FirstPersonMotion data assets in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Motion): the equipped item's First Person Motion Profile, else the character's. Four ship with the template: Unarmed, Pistol, Rifle and Heavy.
  • On AC_FirstPersonRendering (FirstPerson > Motion): First Person Motion Profile (the character's default, DA_FPMotion_Unarmed) and First Person Motion Intensity (1; 0 turns the motion off); Debug First Person Motion is under FirstPerson > Debug.
  • A montage curve disable_fp_motion (0 to 1) pauses the motion during an animation.
  • It works in all three modes and on retargeted characters. It is local only: other players don't see first-person meshes, and shots and the crosshair use the camera, so the motion never changes where shots go.

Recipes and the full setting list: Tune first-person motion.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
On AC_FirstPersonRendering, under FirstPerson in the Details panel:

Setting Category Use First Person Mode FirstPerson > General See Modes. First Person Full Meshes FirstPerson > Setup Meshes for the overlay and true modes. First = lead. Use headless meshes when you have them. First Person Arms Meshes / Body Meshes FirstPerson > Setup Meshes for the Split mode. Third Person Mesh Name FirstPerson > Setup The body Skeletal Mesh Component to copy from (SkeletalMesh on the Mover pawn and visual overrides, CharacterMesh0 on the CMC pawn). First Person Retargeter FirstPerson > Setup IK Retargeter from the UEFN mannequin to this skeleton. Needed by the overlay modes on non-UEFN skeletons. First Person Camera Bone FirstPerson > Setup Bone the first-person camera attaches to (VB Camera). First Person Head Bone FirstPerson > Setup Head bone, hidden when the third-person mesh is reused as the lead (head). First Person Eye Offset FirstPerson > Camera Camera point relative to the head bone, in mesh space at the reference pose (X right, Y forward, Z up, cm). UEFN (0,0,0); Manny, Quinn, Kellan (0,12,0). First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit / Up Limit FirstPerson > Arms Degrees the arms follow the view before the spine leans (45 / 90). First Person Camera Follow Lean FirstPerson > Camera How much the camera follows the spine lean looking down (0 stays, 1 follows; 0.75). True First Person Weapon Presentation FirstPerson > General TrueFirstPerson weapon raise when not aiming (0.3). First Person Full Body View FirstPerson > Camera How much of the view pitch the arms follow before the spine takes the rest (1). First Person Camera Vertical Smoothing FirstPerson > Camera How quickly the camera height follows the body (12; lower = softer crouches and landings). First Person Max Root Yaw Lag FirstPerson > Camera Degrees the body may lag behind the view before it turns (60). Read from the pawn's component. First Person Pipeline Anim Class (advanced) FirstPerson > Setup Anim Blueprint of the lead mesh (ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN). Replace it with a child to extend the first-person pipeline. Empty = default. First Person Retarget Host Anim Class (advanced) FirstPerson > Setup Anim Blueprint used when the pipeline class cannot run on the lead's skeleton (ABP_FirstPerson_Host). Empty = default. First Person Mesh Suffix (advanced) FirstPerson > Setup Suffix that pairs a first-person mesh with its third-person component for material copies (_FP). Empty = _FP.

For retargeted characters these are set on the visual override's own component (see Add a retargeted character). Recipes are in Configure first person.

docs.title: Skeleton requirements
docs.text:
• A VB Camera virtual bone from root to head (or set First Person Camera Bone). The retargeter does not animate virtual bones, so GASPALS writes it from the body's head in CR_FirstPerson_BodyCamera.
  • A head bone (or set First Person Head Bone; the first-person rigs and the eye offset still use head).
  • For the overlay modes: UE-standard spine, clavicle and neck names (spine_01..spine_05, clavicle_l/r, neck_01).

Missing pieces are reported on screen for the local player, in orange, starting with GASPALS First Person (...).

docs.title: Cover and traversal in first person
docs.text:
• Cover: sticky cover switches to third person by default; auto cover gives wall-hug movement while the body follows the camera. See Cover system.
  • Traversal: during a traversal move in first person, the view turns toward the ledge when it is more than 15 degrees off.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: First-person meshes exist only for the owning player's view; other players see the third-person character. The camera perspective is sent to the server, so the server knows which representation the owner uses. Nothing else in the first-person pipeline replicates.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• TrueFirstPerson: weapons can clip into walls (no first-person scale), and the weapon follows the third-person aim with a frame of delay.
  • FirstPersonOverlaySplit: the body is not scaled, so it receives the hidden third-person body's shadow.
  • EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh gives a usable first cut; hand-authored arm and body meshes look cleaner, especially with dense clothing.
  • Only the rifle, pistol and bow have first-person overlay poses.
  • Cost: the first-person Anim Blueprint copies and re-poses a full body. One extra IK retarget runs for the overlay on retargeted characters.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text: This page covers how the pawns move: gaits and rotation modes (both pawns), the Mover movement modes and transitions, and the slide. The animation side is in Animation pipeline.

docs.title: Input state
docs.text: Both pawns keep an input state (S_PlayerInputState): WantsToSprint (hold Shift), WantsToWalk (toggle Ctrl), WantsToStrafe (toggle middle mouse), WantsToAim (hold Right Button), WantsToCrouch (toggle C). Movement, animation and camera are derived from it. Each of these five can be switched between hold and toggle per pawn (Toggle Crouch, Toggle Walk, Toggle Sprint, Toggle Aim, Toggle Strafe).

docs.title: Gait
docs.text:
Gait When (Mover pawn) Sprint Sprint held, not aiming, and (while strafing) the input is within Sprint Max Angle From Facing of the facing direction. Walk Walk toggled on, or a small stick deflection (DDCvar.AnalogInputStyle 1: below 0.7). Run Otherwise.

In cover the gait is Walk (unless crouched), and during a cover run it is Sprint. The CMC pawn decides the same way (GetDesiredGait), with Movement Stick Mode and Analog Walk/Run Threshold (0.7) for the stick.

Sprint Max Angle From Facing (on the pawn, GASPALS > Movement > Sprint): the Mover pawn has one angle per DDCvar.StrafeStyle (60 / 95.7 / 95.7 degrees), the CMC pawn one value (50). Raise it to let the character sprint sideways while strafing.

docs.title: Rotation mode
docs.text:
Mode When The character faces OrientToMovement Default in third person Where it moves Strafe Strafe toggled on, in first person, while auto-strafing, or near a targeted actor The camera direction (the target when locked on) Aim Aim held The aim direction

The camera uses the same mode to pick its Free, Strafe or Aim rig.

Auto-strafe (GASPALS > Strafe on both pawns): with Auto Strafe Enabled, the third-person character strafes while the player looks around and orients to movement again Auto Strafe Delay (1 s) after the look input stops. It only matters while strafe is toggled off; the CMC pawn starts strafing. On the CMC pawn the state is sent to the server with the rest of the input state, so other players see the same facing.

Target lock: actors that call AddTarget / RemoveTarget on the pawn (the TargetDummy does on overlap) can be locked on; the nearest one is marked with a red cone and the character keeps facing it, out of cover. Both pawns support it; the CMC pawn turns toward the target at Target Lock Interp Speed (10).

docs.title: Speeds
docs.text:
Mover pawnCMC pawn

Set on the Walking mode instance of each pawn's CharacterMover component (category Blueprint Overrides (Change These)):

Setting Default Walk Speed / Walk Acceleration 165 / 500 Run Speed / Run Acceleration 375 / 800 Sprint Speed / Sprint Acceleration 585 / 300 Crouch Speed 165 Walk/Run Turn Strength / Sprint Turn Strength 8 / 4 Gait Change Deceleration / Stopping Deceleration 300 / 1000 Walk/Run Facing Time / Sprint Facing Time / Idle Facing Time 0.4 / 0.8 / 0.2 (the sample pawns use 0.1 for walk/run and idle)

The Cover mode (a child of Walking) moves at 150 (walk) and 250 (run and sprint).

Right after landing the Walking mode brakes with Just Landed Deceleration (20000) for Just Landed Duration (0.2 s), so the character doesn't slide. The Falling mode turns at most Falling Rotation Rate (300 degrees per second).

Set on the pawn (class defaults). Each is a vector: forward, strafe, backward speed, blended by direction with Curve_StrafeSpeedMap while strafing.

Setting Forward, strafe, backward Walk Speeds 200, 180, 150 Run Speeds 500, 350, 300 Sprint Speeds 700, 700, 700 Crouch Speeds 225, 200, 180

UpdateMovement_PreCMC writes the resulting max speed, acceleration, braking and friction into the Character Movement Component every frame, before it moves, so change them on the pawn (GASPALS > Movement > CMC), not on the component:

Setting Default Gait Max Acceleration 800, 800, 300 (walk, run, sprint at top speed) Sprint Acceleration Speed Range 300 to 700 (sprint acceleration eases from the run value to the sprint value over this speed range) Gait Ground Friction 5, 5, 3 Sprint Ground Friction Speed Range 0 to 500 Braking Deceleration 500 with movement input, 2000 when stopping (also in cover) Stopping Braking Friction 3 Falling Rotation Rate 200 degrees per second

docs.title: Mover movement modes
docs.text:
Registered on CharacterMover > Movement Modes of the Mover pawn:

Name Class Use Walking BP_MovementMode_Walking (Smooth Walking) Ground movement with gait speeds, turning and facing. Falling BP_MovementMode_Falling Air: air control 0.5. Flying B_MovementMode_Flying Traversal moves, debug flying (max speed 1000). Sliding BP_MovementMode_Slide Slide. Cover BP_MovementMode_Cover Along cover (see Cover). Traversing Flying (native) Registered but not used. Ragdoll BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll Physics ragdoll (X); see Ragdoll and interactions.

Shared settings: legacy movement settings (max step height 30, perch radius 20) and stance settings (crouched half height 60). Sync Inputs For Sim Proxy is on, so remote characters receive the inputs for animation.

The pawn's Movement Mode Map translates mode names into the animation's movement modes (E_MovementMode): Cover counts as on ground, Sliding as sliding, and so on.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Transition Where Condition BP_MovementTransition_Cover Global Walking to Cover and back, from the cover input. BP_MovementTransition_ToSlide Walking and Cover modes Speed over Slide Enter Speed (380), crouching, not in cover, cooldown over. BP_MovementTransition_FromSlide Sliding mode Not crouching, or speed at or below Slide Exit Speed (200). BP_MovementTransition_SuggestedMode Global Applies a mode requested in the input (ragdoll enter and exit).

Transitions are instanced per mode: each mode carries its own copy.

docs.title: Slide
docs.text:
Sprint, then crouch: the Mover pawn slides. BP_MovementMode_Slide is a smooth walking mode whose speed and deceleration depend on the slope:

Setting Default Initial Boost Time / Speed / Acceleration 0.2 s / 800 / 2000 After Boost Acceleration 300 Steep Slope Angle / Shallow Slope Angle 40 / 10 degrees Steep Slope Speed / Shallow Slope Speed / Flat Ground Speed 800 / 500 / 100 Steep Slope Deceleration / Flat Ground Deceleration 2000 / 500 Slide Cooldown 0.75 s Slide Enter Speed / Slide Exit Speed 380 / 200

The slide starts when the speed is over Slide Enter Speed (380; running forward is about 375, so it needs a sprint), the character crouches, is not in cover, and the cooldown is over. It ends when the character stands up or slows to Slide Exit Speed (200). The transitions read both from the Slide mode.

Slide Cooldown stops crouch-tapping from restarting the slide with a fresh boost: a new slide can start only 0.75 s after the last one started or ended. It is measured in Mover simulation time, so the server and the predicting client agree. It is set on the Slide mode instance of each pawn.

The CMC pawn has no slide.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
• p.VisualizeMovement 1 shows the movement state.
  • On the Mover pawn, Z (keyboard only) toggles a debug flying mode (debug tools).

docs.title: Overlay system
docs.text:
An overlay is a pose layered on top of locomotion. The legs keep walking, running and turning with motion matching; the overlay decides how the upper body is held: a rifle at the ready, a torch held up, a box carried in both arms, hands tied, an injured stance. This is the layering approach of the Advanced Locomotion System (ALS), on the Game Animation Sample.

There are two independent overlays:

  • Overlay pose: what the character holds or how it holds itself. Item poses come from the equipment system; stance poses (Default, Injured, HandsTied) from the overlay menu.
  • Overlay body: a body style applied to the whole figure: Default, Masculine, Feminine.
Folder /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem Component AC_OverlaySystem (on both pawns) Layer interfaces ALI_OverlayPose, ALI_OverlayBody, ALI_OverlayFirstPerson Pose Anim Blueprints OverlayPose/ABP_OverlayPose_Base and children ABP_Overlay_<Item> Body Anim Blueprints OverlayBody/ABP_OverlayBody_Base and children (Default, Masculine, Feminine) First-person poses FirstPerson/ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base and children (Rifle, Pistol2H, Bow) Blending ABP_LayerBlending (linked into both character Anim Blueprints) Menus UI/OverlayPose/W_Switcher_Pose, UI/OverlayBody/W_Switcher_Body Input V (hold, pose menu), B (hold, body menu), mouse wheel / D-pad Settings Overlay reference

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The character Anim Blueprints call two linked anim layers, OverlayPose and OverlayBody. Which Anim Blueprint implements them is decided at runtime with Link Anim Class Layers on the character mesh:

  • AC_OverlaySystem links the class its Overlay Pose Layers map gives for the selected stance (ABP_Overlay_Default, _Injured, _HandsTied), and the class from Overlay Body Layers for the body (ABP_OverlayBody_<Style>). A value with no row keeps the current layer and prints an orange warning.
  • AC_EquipmentSystem links the item's pose (ABP_Overlay_Rifle...) from its data asset.

The last link wins: equipping an item replaces a stance pose, and choosing a stance in the menu replaces the item pose. With nothing in hand (Unequip), the equipment system applies the selected stance instead of a pose of its own, so an Overlay Pose set on the pawn's component shows at spawn and comes back when the item is put away. Overlay changes are instant (no transition animation plays). Each linked Anim Blueprint outputs a pose; ABP_LayerBlending blends it onto locomotion per body part using curves. See Animation pipeline for where this sits in the full graph.

docs.title: Pose Anim Blueprints
docs.text:
ABP_OverlayPose_Base holds the logic; its children only hold data. A state machine (SM_OverlayPose) chooses between three states:

State Meaning Enters when Relaxed Item lowered Start state. From Ready: when sprinting, after Ready Hold Time Moving (2 s) of moving, or after Ready Hold Time Idle (3 s). Ready Item raised, not aiming From Relaxed: aim pressed (and not sprinting). From Aiming: aim released or sprint, after at least Aim Min Time (0.75 s) of aiming. Aiming Aiming From Ready: aim held, once Ready is a quarter blended in.

With Can Aim off (box, barrel, default and the stance poses), the machine stays in Relaxed. Within each state, the pose is picked by stance (stand, crouch) and speed:

Variable (class defaults of the child) Used for Stand_Relax_Idle, _Walk, _Run, Stand_Relax_Sprint Standing, relaxed Stand_Ready_Idle, _Walk, _Run Standing, ready Stand_Aim_Idle, _Walk, _Run Standing, aiming Crouch_Relax_Idle, _Move; Crouch_Ready_Idle, _Move; Crouch_Aim_Idle, _Move Crouched Stand_Aim_Sweep, Crouch_Aim_Sweep Additive aim sweep: arms up and down with the aim pitch

Each pose variable is a Struct_OverlayCurves: an animation (usually a single-frame pose) and a curve map (curve name to value). The pose Anim Blueprint writes the curve map onto the pose, and ABP_LayerBlending reads those curves.

docs.title: Curves
docs.text:
The curve map decides how much of the body each pose takes over. Names are lowercase:

Curve 0 1 layering_legs, layering_pelvis Locomotion legs and pelvis Overlay legs and pelvis (carry stances) layering_spine Locomotion spine Overlay spine layering_spine_add No additive Locomotion spine motion added on top layering_head, layering_head_add Locomotion head Overlay head / additive layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r Locomotion arm Overlay arm layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add No additive Arm swing added on top of the overlay arm layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls Arm in mesh space (keeps its aim while the spine moves) Arm in local space (follows the spine) layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r Locomotion fingers Overlay fingers enable_handik_l, enable_handik_r Hand IK off Hand IK to the item's HandIK socket enable_cr_aimoffset Aim offset rig off Aim offset rig on disable_cr_aimoffset_pitch, _yaw Axis on Axis off

The rifle's ready pose, for reference: all layering_* at 1 except the head and the additive arms (0), right arm local space at 0.5, left hand IK on.

docs.title: Aim sweep
docs.text: While aiming, the arms follow the camera pitch through the aim sweep additive, blended by AimSweepValue (the pitch mapped from up to down). Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local (30) and Remote (10) set how fast it follows on the owning machine and on others. See Animation pipeline.

docs.title: Body Anim Blueprints
docs.text: ABP_OverlayBody_Base picks one of four poses by stance and movement: Pose Stand Idle, Pose Stand Move, Pose Crouch Idle, Pose Crouch Move. The children set those four animations.

docs.title: First-person poses
docs.text: ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Base has the same pose variables (without the aim sweeps) for the first-person arms, with curves for the first-person rigs. The equipment data's Overlay Pose FP links it. See First person.

docs.title: The menus
docs.text:
Hold V (pose) or B (body): the world slows to Menu Time Dilation (0.35), the Overlay Pose Menu Widget Class / Overlay Body Menu Widget Class opens with one entry per enum value, mouse wheel up or D-pad up moves the highlight up the list and down moves it down (wrapping at the ends), and releasing the key selects it. As with the equipment menu, the component keeps the highlight (HighlightedOverlayPose / HighlightedOverlayBody) and the widgets only read it. The entries come from Enum_OverlayPose (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and Enum_OverlayBody (Default, Masculine, Feminine).

If the pawn is destroyed while a menu is open, the component's EndPlay calls CloseOverlayMenus: it closes both menus, removes their widgets and sets the world speed back to normal.

docs.title: Shipped overlays
docs.text:

Injured holds one hand to the side and HandsTied keeps the hands behind the back. Their relaxed standing poses use Pose_Injured_Stand / Pose_HandsTied_Stand and their relaxed crouch poses Pose_Injured_Crouch / Pose_HandsTied_Crouch, with the same layering curve values as the box. They are complete examples of a stance overlay: see Add an overlay state. Pistol1H has poses but no equipment slot uses it; link it from a data asset to try it.

docs.title: Animation modifiers
docs.text: AnimModifiers/ holds four animation modifiers for authoring: Create_LayeringCurves keys every layering curve (value 1) on an animation, Copy_Curves and Copy_Curves_Pose copy curves from another animation, and Create_Curves creates curves from parameters. Apply them from the animation's Animation Modifiers window. The shipped overlays use curve maps instead, so the modifiers are optional: use them if you prefer layering curves authored in the animations.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: Overlay Pose and Overlay Body are replicated with RepNotify. The owner changes them locally and sends a reliable Server RPC; every machine links the Anim Blueprints in the RepNotify.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The menus slow the whole world while open.
  • An item's pose replaces the stance while the item is held (see How it works).
  • The stance poses (Default, Injured, HandsTied) and the item poses share the pose layer, so a stance and an item cannot be combined.
  • Adding a value to Enum_OverlayPose needs a row in Overlay Pose Layers (otherwise the warning OverlayPoseLayers has no anim layer class for the selected OverlayPose shows and the layer is unchanged).
  • Variables added to ABP_OverlayPose_Base do not reach existing children's class defaults: set them on each child.

docs.title: Ragdoll and interactions
docs.text:
GASPALS has two ragdoll implementations, one per pawn type:

CMC pawn Mover pawn Pawn SandboxCharacter_CMC SandboxCharacter_Mover Implementation AC_RagdollSystem component A Mover movement mode (BP_MovementMode_Ragdoll) plus a Physics Control component Input X toggles ragdoll X ragdolls, Space gets up Entry Keeps the movement momentum (Inherited Velocity Scale); the legs collide with each other The Ragdoll physics profile; the legs collide with each other Get-up Get-up animation chosen from the pose (front, back) and the held item Get-up animations chosen from the pose (front, back, roll) Physical animation No Off by default (kinematic); DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile 1 turns it on Interactions No Takedowns and shoves between characters; demo shooting and spawning (debug tools) Level Any (DefaultLevel starts on the CMC pawn) Any (N to the Mover pawn in DefaultLevel); RagdollLevel has targets and obstacles

docs.title: CMC ragdoll (AC_RagdollSystem)
docs.text:
/GASPALS/Systems/RagdollSystem/AC_RagdollSystem. Press X (IA_Ragdoll) to toggle.

Start: the owner calls StartRagdoll, which asks the server (Server_StartRagdoll) to multicast it to everyone. Each machine stops montages, turns the capsule's collision off, switches the mesh to physics (Ragdoll profile, simulating the bodies below the pelvis), applies the entry physics (ApplyEntryPhysics, below), and sets the movement mode to none. OnRagdollStarted fires.

Entry physics: right after the bodies start simulating, and before the movement mode is cleared, the bodies get the pawn's velocity times Inherited Velocity Scale, so a running character keeps its momentum instead of dropping in place, and collision is turned on between the left and right leg bodies so the legs don't pass through each other (the Mover ragdoll profile does the same for the legs). Settings on AC_RagdollSystem (Ragdoll > Entry), set per pawn because the bone names depend on the skeleton:

Setting Default Use Inherited Velocity Scale 1.0 Share of the movement velocity the ragdoll starts with. 1 keeps the momentum, 0 drops in place (the behavior before this setting). Left Leg Bones thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l Bodies of the left leg. Right Leg Bones thigh_r, calf_r, foot_r Bodies of the right leg; each collides with each left leg body.

Stop: StopRagdoll reverses it the same way and fires OnRagdollEnded. Each machine turns physics off and puts the mesh back where it sat on the capsule when the ragdoll started (CacheMeshTransform / RestoreMeshTransform: the simulated pelvis drags the mesh away during the ragdoll). The capsule and mesh get back the collision settings they had when the ragdoll started (cached by CacheCollisionState), so a pawn with its own collision setup keeps it. On the ground the pawn walks again and plays a get-up montage picked from the pose (lying on the back or the front) and the held item (Get Up Back / Front settings: Default, right hand, left hand, two hands); in the air it falls with the body's last velocity.

While ragdolling the CMC accepts the client's position (client-authoritative flags), so the capsule follows the body without corrections. The camera system listens to the two dispatchers to switch to the ragdoll perspective (see Camera).

Settings and functions: Ragdoll reference.

docs.title: Mover ragdoll
docs.text:
SandboxCharacter_Mover is the player pawn of RagdollLevel (game mode GM_Sandbox_Ragdoll), and it is the Mover pawn of every other level too: the ragdoll, takedowns and debug tools work wherever it plays. It has:

  • a Physics Control component: when not ragdolling, DDCVar.CharacterPhysics.DefaultProfile picks kinematic (0, default: the body plays the animation exactly) or physical animation (1: every limb is a simulated body pulled toward the animation, so it reacts to contacts, but hands and arms can catch on walls, for example in cover). An AC_PostABPTick helper updates the strengths from animation curves right after the Anim Blueprint runs.
  • the Ragdoll movement mode and the BP_MovementTransition_SuggestedMode transition;
  • interactions with other characters (takedowns, shoves);
  • the debug tools component (AC_DebugTools): demo shot, spawn or rotate characters, teleport, fly.

docs.title: Entering and leaving ragdoll
docs.text:
1. X (IA_Ragdoll) sets an injury state and, on the owner, writes a ragdoll request into the Mover input. The suggested-mode transition switches to the Ragdoll mode inside the simulation, so the owner and the server agree. (A server forcing a remote player into ragdoll queues the mode directly.)
  2. Every machine applies the ragdoll look when the mode changes: physics on, the Ragdoll physics profile.
  3. While ragdolling, the owner can roll the body with the move input; the roll travels in the input too. Remote ragdolls are pulled toward the replicated capsule so they stay in sync.
  4. Space on the ground leaves the ragdoll. Entering and leaving ragdoll put the capsule back on the collision profile the pawn was built with (GetDefaultCapsuleProfile, CharacterCapsule in the sample), which also clears a takedown's collision override. The owner picks a get-up montage from the body's pose (lying on the back or the front, rolling) and sends it in the input; the server and the owner play it.

docs.title: Settling
docs.text:
The ragdoll's arms are pulled toward the animated pose, which keeps moving while the body lies still, so the hands would keep shaking. Once the body has stayed slower than Ragdoll Settle Speed for Ragdoll Settle Delay, the physics control strengths fade to zero over Ragdoll Settle Blend Time; when the body moves again (pushed, shot, rolled) they come back four times faster. In a test, the hand of a settled ragdoll moved about 16 times less per frame (0.33 to 0.02 cm) and drifted 0.25 cm instead of 8 cm over three seconds.

Settings on SandboxCharacter_Mover (GASPALS > Ragdoll > Settle):

Setting Default Use Ragdoll Settle Speed 15 Body speed (cm/s) below which the ragdoll counts as still. Ragdoll Settle Delay 0.3 Seconds below that speed before the strengths start fading. Ragdoll Settle Blend Time 0.5 Seconds to fade the strengths to zero (coming back takes a quarter of it).

docs.title: Takedowns and shoves
docs.text:
Near another character:

Input Action Left Button Takedown: a paired takedown animation on both characters. E Shove.

The interaction is matched with multi-character motion matching (MMI): the best paired animation for both characters' poses and positions is chosen, and both are warped into place. On a client, the initiator plays its part at once and asks the server (Server_TryCharacterInteraction), which checks the victim (walking, not already in a root-motion animation, within 3.5 m) and multicasts the interaction. Each machine sets up the participants (ignored collisions, tick order, the animation contexts the Anim Blueprint uses for constraints).

docs.title: Demo tools
docs.text:
The AC_DebugTools component on the Mover pawn. Hold aim (Right Button), then:

Input Action Left Button Shoot: the character hit goes ragdoll with an impulse. E Spawn a character where you aim, or rotate the one you aim at.

Clients send these to the server with the view; the server traces, applies the ragdoll and multicasts the impulse. Settings (trace distances, impulse, spawn limit, an on/off switch) and the teleport and fly keys are on the Debug tools page.

docs.title: Physics obstacles
docs.text:
RagdollLevel has moving obstacles (bumpers, hammers, turnstiles, moving platforms) on the Obstacle collision channel, which the Ragdoll profile blocks. Walk into them with physical animation on, or ragdoll into them.

The locally controlled Mover pawn sweeps a sphere from the neck to between the feet every frame; an obstacle hit knocks it into ragdoll. Settings on SandboxCharacter_Mover (GASPALS > Ragdoll > Obstacles):

Setting Default Use Ragdoll On Obstacle Hit true Off: obstacles only push the capsule. Ragdoll Obstacle Object Types Obstacle Object types that knock the pawn over. Ragdoll Obstacle Trace Radius 15 Radius of the sweep in cm.

docs.title: Networking summary
docs.text:
Event CMC pawn Mover pawn Start / stop Server RPC, then reliable multicast Mover input request and transition; cosmetics on mode change Roll n/a Mover input Get-up Played on every machine by the stop multicast Montage chosen by the owner, sent in the input, played on server and owner Interactions n/a Client predicts, server validates, reliable multicast

In a listen server test, expect one correction for each of: a takedown or shove from the host on a client, a shot from the host, the host rotating a client. Ragdoll bodies agree within a few centimeters across machines.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The two implementations are separate: the CMC pawn has no physical animation, settling or interactions.
  • Takedowns and shoves are on the Mover pawn only, between Mover characters.
  • The CMC ragdoll simulates the bodies below the pelvis, with no physical animation and no roll.
