docs.title: Traversal system
docs.text:
Traversal moves the character over obstacles: vault (over and land on the other side), hurdle (over and keep running), mantle (climb up onto). It is the Game Animation Sample traversal, shared by both pawns and triggered by jump and by vaulting from cover.

Folder /GASPALS/Systems/TraversalSystem Components AC_TraversalLogic (orchestration), AC_TraversalTracer (ledge measurement) Preview actor BP_TraversalTester Choosers /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Animations/Traversal/CHT_TraversalMontages_Mover, _CMC Montages Traversal/Vault, Hurdle, Mantle, Climb, Catch folders Collision The Traversable trace channel Input Space (jump) Settings Traversal reference

docs.title: How a traversal happens
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    J[Jump pressed] --> CV{In cover?}
    CV -->|facing away| Turn[Turn to the wall] --> T
    CV -->|no| T[TryTraversalAction]
    T --> Tr[Capsule trace<br>Traversable channel]
    Tr --> L[Measure ledges<br>AC_TraversalTracer]
    L --> R[Room checks]
    R --> C[Chooser picks montage]
    C --> P[Play montage<br>with motion warping]
    T -->|nothing found| Jmp[Normal jump]
  1. Trigger. Jump calls TryTraversalAction with inputs from the pawn's GetTraversalCheckInputs: a trace forward whose length grows with speed (on the ground) or a short trace (in the air), sized by the Check settings below. In cover, the cover system first turns the character to the wall (RequestCoverVault). Held jump keeps retrying every frame.
  2. Find the obstacle. A capsule trace on the Traversable Trace Channel (the Traversable channel). No hit: the pawn jumps instead.
  3. Measure it. AC_TraversalTracer finds the front ledge, checks the width (Min Ledge Width, 70 cm), and finds the back ledge and the floor behind.
  4. Room checks. Capsule traces on the Room Check Trace Channel (Visibility) check the character fits on top of the front ledge and between the ledges. They give the obstacle height and depth, and whether there is a back ledge and a back floor.
  5. Pick the montage. The chooser (CHT_TraversalMontages_Mover or _CMC) gets the action type, ledge data, height, depth, distance, movement mode, gait, speed and the pose history, and returns a montage with a start time and play rate. No match: the pawn jumps.
  6. Play it. The montage plays with motion warping targets FrontLedge, BackLedge and BackFloor, so the animation lands exactly on the measured ledges. During the montage the character ignores the obstacle's collision and moves in flying mode; afterwards it returns to falling (vault) or walking.

docs.title: Mover and CMC
docs.text:
Mover pawn CMC pawn Montage playback Mover's montage support (root motion through the movement modes) Anim instance montage with root motion Movement mode during the move Flying (queued) MOVE_Flying Replication behavior Prediction handles it Client-authoritative position during the move Can traverse when On the ground or in the air, no montage playing, not already traversing Not already traversing

Set Is Mover Character on AC_TraversalLogic to match the pawn (on for Mover pawns): it selects the chooser and the movement path.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text: The owner predicts: it runs the checks and plays the montage at once, then sends the result to the server (PerformTraversalAction_Server, reliable). The server plays it too, except for a pawn it controls locally (a listen-server host, a standalone player or a server AI), which already started the move itself, so every traversal starts once. Other machines see the montage through the movement component's montage replication. AC_TraversalLogic has Component Replicates on in both sample pawns.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Tool Shows DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 1 Ledge points ... 2 Plus the initial trace ... 3 Plus the room checks and printed ledge data DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugDuration How long the shapes stay BP_TraversalTester Place it in a level: it previews the tracer in the editor without playing Show Trace / Persistent Show Trace on AC_TraversalTracer Tracer debug lines

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
AC_TraversalTracer:

Setting Default Use Min Ledge Width 70 Narrowest traversable ledge. Min Front Ledge Depth 37.52 Depth of the width check into the obstacle. Trace Complex true Trace complex collision for the ledges. Show Trace / Persistent Show Trace false Debug drawing.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > Collision, set on each pawn's component):

Setting Default Use Traversable Trace Channel Traversable Channel of the obstacle search. Only geometry that blocks it can be traversed. Room Check Trace Channel Visibility Channel of the three room checks; anything that blocks it stops the move.

AC_TraversalLogic (Traversal > Check): the obstacle search the pawns' GetTraversalCheckInputs builds. The Mover and CMC pawns set their own speed and reach ranges.

Setting Default Use Traversal Check Radius 30 Radius of the capsule traced forward. Traversal Check Half Height 60 on the ground, 86 in the air Half height of that capsule. Traversal Check Speed Range / Traversal Check Distance Range Mover 0 to 375 / 75 to 300; CMC 0 to 500 / 75 to 350 On the ground the reach grows with speed: the speed range maps onto the distance range. Traversal Check Air Distance / Traversal Check Air End Offset 75 / (0, 0, 50) Reach and end offset in the air.

In first person the view turns toward the obstacle during a traversal: First Person Traversal Turn Speed (2; 0 leaves the view alone) when it is more than First Person Traversal Turn Threshold (15 degrees) off (Traversal > First Person).

AC_TraversalLogic also has Is Mover Character.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Obstacles must block the Traversable channel. See Make objects traversable.
  • The montages' motion warping windows must be named FrontLedge, BackLedge and BackFloor.
  • The pawn implements Get_PropertiesForTraversal (capsule, mesh, motion warping component, mode, gait, speed) and GetTraversalCheckInputs.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only geometry on the Traversable channel is considered; everything else is jumped.
  • Very thin or narrow obstacles (under Min Ledge Width) are not traversed.
  • In first person the view turns toward the ledge during the move when it is more than 15 degrees off.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: Each tutorial goes step by step from start to a working result, and ends with how to check it in Play.

docs.title: Characters and animation
docs.text: Tutorial You will Add a retargeted character Bring your own skeletal mesh in, with first person and equipment. Add an equipment item Add a weapon or carried item with its poses, sockets and data. Add an overlay state Create stance poses and body styles, starting from the Injured overlay. Configure first person Pick a mode, set meshes, place the camera at the eyes, add first-person poses.

docs.title: Levels and gameplay
docs.text: Tutorial You will Set up cover in a level Build cover that works with every cover feature. Configure cover behavior Sticky-only, crouch-only, wall gaps, facing, exits, aim from cover. Make objects traversable Let characters vault, hurdle and mantle your geometry. Customize the camera Change rigs, offsets, styles and the perspective cycle. Add or rebind inputs Rebind keys, add gamepad bindings, add inputs to systems.

docs.title: Your project
docs.text: Tutorial You will Use GASPALS in your own project Set up your game mode, pawn and levels, remove demo features, package. Add the systems to your own pawn Wire every system on a pawn of your own.

docs.title: Customize the camera
docs.text:
The camera is data: Gameplay Cameras rigs chosen by chooser tables. Most changes need no Blueprint work. Background: Camera system.

All assets are in /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem/Rigs. Open a rig to edit it in the Camera Rig editor. Save each rig asset after editing.

docs.title: Change distance, field of view or damping for everything
docs.text: Open ThirdPerson/CameraRig_TP_Base. Its exposed parameters (boom arm offset, camera offset, field of view, forward / lateral / vertical damping) are the shared defaults. The variants (CameraRig_TP_Close_Freecam...) override some of them: check a variant before assuming the base value applies.

docs.title: Change one situation
docs.text: Each third-person situation has its own rig: CameraRig_TP_<Close|Medium|Far>_<Freecam|Strafe|Aim>. For example, to bring the camera closer while aiming at the medium distance, edit CameraRig_TP_Medium_Aim.

docs.title: Change the crouch, shoulder and cover offsets
docs.text:
The offsets come from Camera Offset Rigs on each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component:

Entry Default rig Default offset Crouch Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Crouch 50 cm down Right Shoulder Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_Right 100 cm to the side (right shoulder) Cover Low Rig CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverLow 80 cm up behind low cover Cover Edge Left Rig / Right CameraRig_TP_Offset_CoverEdgeLeft / Right 60 cm toward the open side at a wall end
  • To tweak an offset for everyone, edit the offset node's translation in the rig.
  • To give one character different offsets, duplicate the rig, edit the copy and point that pawn's entry at it.
  • To turn an offset off (for example no crouch drop), clear the entry.

docs.title: Change the first-person field of view
docs.text: Open FirstPerson/CameraRig_FP_Base and change its field of view. Keep its First Person node: it keeps the first-person meshes out of the third-person body's shadow. For the Split mode's arm scale, edit CameraRig_FP_Scale (or point Camera Offset Rigs > First Person Scale Rig at your own rig).

docs.title: Add a camera style
docs.text:
1. Add rigs for the new style (duplicate the Medium ones: CameraRig_TP_Medium_Freecam, _Strafe, _Aim).
  2. Add an enumerator to /GASPALS/Systems/CameraSystem/Data/E_CameraStyle.
  3. Open CHT_CameraRigs_ThirdPerson and add three rows for the new style (Free, Strafe and Aim modes) pointing to your rigs. Do the same in CHT_CameraRigs_TopDown and _SideScroller if the style should exist there.
  4. The style input (2) cycles through all enum values, so the new style is included.

docs.title: Change the start perspective or style
docs.text: On the pawn's AC_CameraSystem component: Camera Perspective and Camera Style. The style also follows DDCvar.CameraStyle.

docs.title: Limit the perspectives
docs.text: On each pawn's AC_CameraSystem component, set Allowed Perspectives to the views you want, in the order 1 should cycle them (for example ThirdPerson, FirstPerson). One entry turns the perspective input off. Make sure Camera Perspective (the start view) is in the list; otherwise the camera starts in the first entry and shows a warning. See Choosing the perspectives.

docs.title: Restyle the crosshair
docs.text: Edit W_Crosshair, or make your own User Widget and set it as Crosshair Widget Class on AC_CameraSystem. The camera component only adds the widget to the screen and centers it on the aim point; nothing calls into it. To tint it on cover targets like W_Crosshair does, read the owning pawn's cover system each frame: IsCoverTargeted and CoverTargetCrosshairColor on AC_CoverSystem.

docs.title: Check what is active
docs.text: GameplayCameras.Debug.Enable 1 in the console shows the active rigs and their parameters.

docs.title: Set up cover in a level
Set up cover in a level
docs.text: The cover system needs no special actors: it finds cover with traces against the level geometry. This page lists what the geometry needs so every cover feature works, and how to test a level.

docs.title: Requirements at a glance
docs.text: Feature The level needs Taking cover Walls whose collision blocks the Cover channel (every profile that blocks Visibility does, so the default for static meshes). Low vs. high cover Walls lower than about 1.45 m are low cover (the check is High Cover Height, 148 cm above the feet, minus the trace radius). Cover run A NavMeshBoundsVolume covering the play area, with the navmesh built. Vault from cover The cover must block the Traversable channel (see Make objects traversable). Corner turn At least Corner Turn Min Width (50 cm) of wall around the corner. Aim around an edge Free space past the wall end: capsule radius plus Cover Aim Edge Clearance (20 cm). Pose lowering Walls at least 10 cm thick, so the down trace from the top finds them.

docs.title: 1. Block out the cover
docs.text:
Any static mesh works. The demo levels use LevelBlock and LevelBlock_Traversable from /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping, which you can place and scale directly.

Good cover heights for the sample characters (180 cm tall, capsule center about 86 cm above the floor):

Height Plays as 90 to 110 cm Low cover: the character crouches behind it, can aim over it, can vault it. 110 to 140 cm Low cover, but the character barely clears it when standing to aim. 150 cm and more High cover: the character stands; aiming steps out at the wall ends.

Leave at least a capsule width (about 80 cm) of floor along the cover so the character can move along it.

docs.title: 2. Check the collision
docs.text:
Select a wall and look at Collision Presets in its Details panel. BlockAll, BlockAllDynamic and TraversalObjectPreset all block Cover. InvisibleWall and triggers ignore it, and so do characters. Avoid simple collision that does not match the visible shape: the character hugs the collision, not the mesh.

Exclude or include objects. Set the object's Collision Presets to Custom and change its Cover response:

  • Ignore keeps it from being cover: foliage, see-through fences, props too small to hide behind. The character walks past it, and the crosshair does not mark it.
  • Block makes it cover even if it ignores Visibility, for example an invisible blocking volume along a broken wall.

Shots from cover still trace Visibility (the camera's Aim Trace Channel), so excluding an object from cover does not let shots through it.

Type show collision in the console during Play to see what the traces hit.

docs.title: 3. Add navigation for cover runs
docs.text:
The cover run follows a navmesh path to the target cover.

  1. Place Actors > Volumes > Nav Mesh Bounds Volume, and scale it over the whole play area.
  2. Press P in the viewport to show the navmesh. It must reach the floor in front of the cover.
  3. Keep Project Settings > Navigation System > Allow Client Side Navigation on for multiplayer (the template sets it).

Without a navmesh the character runs to the cover in a straight line, and stops at the first obstacle.

docs.title: 4. Make cover vaultable
docs.text: Pressing jump in cover vaults over it through the traversal system. Traversal only considers geometry that blocks the Traversable trace channel. Use LevelBlock_Traversable, set the wall's collision preset to TraversalObjectPreset, or set its Traversable response to Block in a custom preset. Walls that do not block it make the character jump instead.

docs.title: 5. Test
docs.text:
1. Play and walk into a wall: the character takes soft cover and turns along it.
  2. Aim at a wall a few meters away and tap Q: the cover marker shows on the wall and the character snaps to it.
  3. Aim at a wall farther away and hold Q: the character runs there.
  4. In sticky cover, hold the move input toward a wall end: the character stops at the end, and turns around an outside corner.
  5. Behind low cover, aim (Right Button) over the wall: the character stands up; aim along the wall: it stays down.
  6. Press Space in front of low cover: the character vaults.

For debugging, turn on Enable Debug on the pawn's cover component to draw the cover traces, Cover Aim Debug to print aim pose changes, and use show collision and the navmesh view (P).

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Symptom Cause The character never takes cover The wall ignores the Cover channel, the project has no Cover channel (copy the collision settings, or set Cover Trace Channel to Visibility), or Enable Cover is off on the pawn's cover component. A trigger or volume behaves like a wall It uses Custom collision that blocks Cover (a new channel's default response). Set its Cover response like its Visibility response. Cover drops when moving along a long wall The wall is made of pieces with gaps or uneven faces. Close the gaps, or raise Max Cover Turn Angle for bends. The cover run goes straight into an obstacle No navmesh, or the navmesh does not reach the target. Jump in cover jumps instead of vaulting The cover does not block Traversable, or it is too high to vault. The character sinks into low cover The cover top is lower than the head clearance assumes; lower Cover Lower Max Crouch.

More settings are in Configure cover behavior.

docs.title: Configure cover behavior
docs.text:
All cover settings are on the pawn's cover component. Open the pawn Blueprint (SandboxCharacter_Mover or SandboxCharacter_CMC), select AC_CoverSystem in the Components panel, and use the Details panel under Cover. The full list is in the Cover reference.

Change both pawns

The two sample pawns each have their own cover component. When you change a setting on one, change it on the other, or the Mover and CMC pawns will behave differently. Child Blueprints of a pawn inherit its values except where they override them.

docs.title: Sticky cover only (button to take cover)
docs.text:
Walking into walls no longer takes cover; only the cover button does.

Setting Value Enable Auto Cover off Enable Sticky Cover on

docs.title: Automatic cover only (no button)
docs.text:
Setting Value Enable Auto Cover on Enable Sticky Cover off

The cover button does nothing, the crosshair does not highlight cover, and there are no cover runs or corner turns.

docs.title: Cover only while crouching
docs.text: Setting Value Engage Rule WhileCrouched

docs.title: Keep a gap to the wall
docs.text:
The character rests touching the wall by default. To leave a gap (for bulky characters or poses that clip):

Setting Value Wall Distance Stand Auto / Stand Sticky / Crouch Auto / Crouch Sticky Gap in cm between the capsule and the wall, per case. Cover Hold Distance Keep it larger than the largest gap plus the capsule radius (about 30 cm on the Mover pawn, 40 cm on the CMC pawn), or cover drops.

docs.title: Choose how the character faces
docs.text:
Four settings, one per case, each FaceWall, ShoulderToWall or BackToWall:

Setting Class default Facing Stand Auto ShoulderToWall Facing Stand Sticky BackToWall Facing Crouch Auto FaceWall Facing Crouch Sticky ShoulderToWall

With FaceWall, Character Rotation Right Shoulder and Left Shoulder (25 and -25 degrees) turn the character toward the camera side.

docs.title: Make cover harder or easier to leave
docs.text: Setting Effect Cover Exit Input Dot How directly the input must point away from the wall (0.7 is more than 45 degrees away). Lower leaves more easily. Cover Exit Delay Seconds of pushing away before soft cover is released. Sticky Exit Input Dot / Sticky Exit Delay The same for sticky cover (0.9 and 0.35 s: deliberate). Sticky Tap Time A cover button press shorter than this leaves sticky cover.

docs.title: Snap to cover from farther away
docs.text: Setting Effect Sticky Cover Reach How far along the camera the cover button finds a wall (250 cm). Cover Run Range Up to where the button runs to cover (1500 cm). Cover Enter Distance How far soft cover reaches when walking into a wall (80 cm).

docs.title: Tune the cover run arrival
docs.text: The run slows down before it snaps into cover. If the character overshoots or slides along the wall, lower Cover Run Brake Decel below what the pawn can brake, or raise Cover Run Arrive Distance. Cover Run Arrive Speed is the speed at the snap.

docs.title: Aim from cover
docs.text: Goal Setting Aiming always leaves cover Enable Cover Aim off Step out to edges even when standing over low cover Cover Aim Keep Standing off Fewer pose switches Raise Cover Aim Min Pose Time, Cover Aim Blocked Delay and Cover Aim Return Delay Tall or short characters Cover Aim Muzzle Height Stand (145) and Crouch (95): muzzle height above the capsule bottom Thick walls Cover Aim Cover Depth: hits this deep behind the cover face count as the cover itself See what it does Cover Aim Debug prints every pose change and draws the target; Enable Debug draws the cover traces

docs.title: Pose lowering
docs.text: Setting Effect Cover Lower Max Stand / Max Crouch The most the pelvis is lowered, in cm (10 and 15). 0 turns lowering off. Cover Lower Head Clearance How far under the cover top the head should end up (5 cm).

docs.title: First person
docs.text: Setting Options First Person Sticky Cover SwitchToThirdPerson (default) or Disabled First Person Auto Cover MovementOnly (default) or Disabled

docs.title: Movement speeds in cover
docs.text: On the Mover pawn, cover movement speeds are part of the Cover movement mode (BP_MovementMode_Cover: walk 150, run and sprint 250 cm/s). On the CMC pawn they come from the pawn's speed settings for the walk gait.

docs.title: Turning cover off
docs.text: Turn off Enable Cover on the component. Everything else stays in place, so you can turn it back on per pawn or at runtime.

docs.title: Add an equipment item
docs.text:
This tutorial adds a shotgun. The same steps work for any held item: a weapon, a tool, a carried object. You need the item's mesh (skeletal or static) and, ideally, a few poses of the character holding it.

The result: the shotgun appears in the equipment menu, attaches to the hand, switches the character to your poses in third and first person, and places the support hand with IK.

Background: Equipment system, Overlay system.

docs.title: 1. Add the slot
docs.text:
Open /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Data/Enum_Equipment and click Add Enumerator. Name it Shotgun. Save.

The equipment menu builds its buttons from this enum, so the new slot shows up in the menu by itself.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the mesh sockets
docs.text:
Open the item mesh (for a skeletal mesh, its skeleton) and add:

Socket Where HandIK Where the support hand grips (the shotgun's pump). The hand's palm lines up with the socket. ADS The sight point: on the sight line, at the rear sight. Only for items you aim down sights with.

Copy the transforms from the rifle (/GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Assets/Meshes/M4A1_Skeleton) as a start. If your mesh already has sockets with other names, keep them and set Hand IK Socket / ADS Socket in the data asset (step 6).

docs.title: 3. Create the item actor
docs.text:
Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Actors/BP_Equipment_Rifle and rename it BP_Equipment_Shotgun. Select its mesh component and set your mesh (for a static mesh, delete the skeletal mesh component and add a Static Mesh component instead).

Keep exactly one mesh component and keep the AC_FirstPersonRendering component: it creates the first-person copy of the mesh at runtime, and the equipment system only attaches and updates hand IK for items that have it. Do not add a first-person duplicate mesh or rendering tags.

Tip

Add extra parts (a flashlight, a strap) as more mesh components. Each gets its own first-person copy. Tag a component DoNotAttach if it should stay where it is instead of being attached to the hand socket.

docs.title: 4. Add the attach socket on the character skeletons
docs.text:
The item attaches to a socket on the character's skeleton. Either reuse overlay_rifle (a long gun held in the right hand), or add overlay_shotgun to every skeleton your characters use:

Skeleton Bone for a right-hand item SK_UEFN_Mannequin (the pawns) weapon_r SK_Mannequin (Manny, Quinn) hand_r metahuman_base_skel (Kellan) hand_r

Copy the overlay_rifle socket and adjust it with Add Preview Asset (right-click the socket) showing the shotgun mesh, while the skeleton preview plays a rifle pose.

docs.title: Third person
docs.text:
1. Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Rifle/ABP_Overlay_Rifle into a new folder OverlayPose/Shotgun and name it ABP_Overlay_Shotgun.
  2. Open its Class Defaults. Under Overlay > Poses, each pose is an animation plus a curve map: Stand_Relax_Idle, Stand_Ready_Idle, Stand_Aim_Idle (and the Walk, Run, Sprint and Crouch variants). Set your shotgun poses (single-frame animations are enough). Start with the rifle poses if you have none yet.
  3. Keep the curve maps of the rifle: they decide which body parts the pose takes over and turn the support-hand IK on.
  4. Set Stand Aim Sweep and Crouch Aim Sweep if you have aim sweep animations (arms aiming up and down); otherwise keep the rifle's.
  5. Check Can Aim, and the Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote values (30 / 10).

See Add an overlay state for the full list of poses and curves.

docs.title: First person (optional)
docs.text: Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/FirstPerson/Rifle/ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle into ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Shotgun and set its first-person poses. Without one, first person shows the third-person overlay.

docs.title: 6. Create the data asset
docs.text:
Right-click in Data/ > Miscellaneous > Data Asset > pick PDA_Equipment (or duplicate DA_Equipment_Rifle). Name it DA_Equipment_Shotgun and fill it:

Field Value Spawned Actor BP_Equipment_Shotgun Overlay Pose TP ABP_Overlay_Shotgun Overlay Pose FP ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Shotgun (or empty) Attach Socket TP / FP overlay_shotgun (or overlay_rifle) Attach Offset TP / FP Small corrections; the rifle uses a 5 degree yaw on TP. Is Left Handed Off (on for items held in the left hand, like the bow). Hand IK Socket / ADS Socket HandIK / ADS (the defaults), or your mesh's socket names.

docs.title: 7. Add the chooser row
docs.text: Open Data/CHT_Equipment. Add a row: in the Enum_Equipment column pick Shotgun, and as the result pick DA_Equipment_Shotgun. Save.

docs.title: 8. Test
docs.text:
1. Play, hold T, select Shotgun, release.
  2. Check the grip in third person: idle, walk, run, sprint, crouch, aim (Right Button). If the item is offset, fix the skeleton socket (step 4) or Attach Offset TP. If the support hand misses, move the item's HandIK socket.
  3. Switch to first person (1 until first person) and aim: the sights should line up with the screen center. Fix the ADS socket if not.
  4. Press M to try the retargeted characters, and N for the other pawn.
  5. Run a listen server with a client and equip the shotgun on the client.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• No actor (an overlay without an item, like hands tied): leave Spawned Actor empty and set only the overlay poses.
  • Left-handed item: turn on Is Left Handed and attach to a left-hand socket (overlay_torch style).
  • Start with the item: set Selected Equipment on the pawn's AC_EquipmentSystem component.

docs.title: Tune first-person motion
docs.text: In first person, the hands and the held item react to the player: they lag behind when the view turns, lean into strafes, bob with the steps, breathe at rest and take a jolt on jumps and landings. While aiming down sights the motion fades so the sight stays steady. The camera itself never moves, which keeps the view comfortable. Background: First person system.

docs.title: Where the settings are
docs.text:
All the values live in motion profiles, data assets of the class PDA_FirstPersonMotion in /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Motion. Four ship with the template:

Profile Feel Used by DA_FPMotion_Unarmed Loose Empty hands (the characters' default) DA_FPMotion_Pistol Light Pistol, torch, binoculars DA_FPMotion_Rifle Medium Rifle, bow DA_FPMotion_Heavy Slow and heavy Box, barrel

Which profile is active:

  1. The equipped item's First Person Motion Profile (on its DA_Equipment_* data asset), when set.
  2. Otherwise the character's First Person Motion Profile on its AC_FirstPersonRendering component (FirstPerson > Motion).

Open a profile and change its values while playing in the editor: the change shows at once.

docs.title: Make an item feel heavier or lighter
docs.text:
Setting Heavier Lighter Position Strength / Rotation Strength (Hz) lower (1 to 1.2) higher (2.5 to 3) Look Rotation Per Degree higher lower Look Max Rotation higher lower Position Damping / Rotation Damping higher (0.9 to 1: no wobble) lower (0.6: a little overshoot)

The strengths are how many times per second the hands could swing back; the damping decides whether they overshoot (below 1) or settle smoothly (1).

docs.title: Less or no sway when turning
docs.text: Lower Look Rotation Per Degree and Look Position Per Degree, or turn Look Sway off. To keep slow aiming steady but let fast flicks swing, make the start of Look Response Curve flat.

docs.title: Change the steps
docs.text: Bob Stride Length is the distance of one bob cycle (two steps). Bob Side / Up / Roll Amplitude set the size, Bob Speed Curve how it grows with speed. Bob Shape Side, Bob Shape Up and Bob Shape Roll draw the path over one cycle (X = phase 0 to 1, Y = -1 to 1): the default makes a figure eight with one dip per step. Turn Bob off for no bob.

docs.title: Steadier or looser aiming
docs.text: While aiming, every source is multiplied by its ADS scale: ADS Look Scale, ADS Move Scale, ADS Bob Scale, ADS Breathing Scale, ADS Impulse Scale (0 = none while aiming). ADS Motion Settle Speed makes leftover motion die out faster when you start aiming (2 = twice as fast; higher = less motion). ADS Blend Curve shapes the change as the aim comes up. For a scope with deliberate sway, raise ADS Breathing Scale on that item's profile.

docs.title: Jumps and landings
docs.text: Jump Position / Rotation Impulse and Landing Position / Rotation Impulse are the kicks (cm/s and degrees/s); Landing Curve scales the landing kick by fall speed, so small hops barely show.

docs.title: Players sensitive to motion
docs.text: First Person Motion Intensity on AC_FirstPersonRendering scales all of it: 1 = as the profiles say, 0 = off. Bind it to an options menu to let players choose.

docs.title: Pause the motion during an animation
docs.text: Add a curve named disable_fp_motion to a montage (1 = motion off, 0 = on). The motion fades with the curve, which keeps it from fighting reload or interaction hand animation.

docs.title: Give an item its own feel
docs.text:
1. Duplicate the closest profile (for example DA_FPMotion_Rifle) and tune it.
  2. Set it as First Person Motion Profile on the item's DA_Equipment_* data asset.

docs.title: Setting reference
docs.text:
Every setting has a tooltip in the editor. The groups:

Group Settings Springs Position / Rotation Strength (Hz), Position / Rotation Damping, Pivot Offset (point the hands rotate around, from the eyes; blends to the eyes while aiming) Look Look Sway, Look Rotation Per Degree, Look Roll From Yaw, Look Position Per Degree, Look Max Rate, Look Max Rotation, Look Max Position, Look Response Curve Move Move Sway, Move Roll Per Speed, Move Side Offset Per Speed, Move Back Offset Per Speed, Move Max Rotation, Move Max Position Bob Bob, Bob Stride Length, Bob Side / Up / Roll Amplitude, Bob Speed Curve, Bob Shape Side / Up / Roll Breathing Breathing, Breathing Position, Breathing Rotation, Breathing Rate Impulses Jump Impulse, Jump Position / Rotation Impulse, Landing Impulse, Landing Position / Rotation Impulse, Landing Curve Stance Crouch Scale ADS ADS Look / Move / Bob / Breathing / Impulse Scale, ADS Motion Settle Speed, ADS Blend Curve

Rotations are pitch, yaw, roll in degrees; positions are right, forward, up in cm, as seen from the eyes.

docs.title: Configure first person
docs.text:
First person works out of the box on the sample pawns and the shipped characters. This page covers the choices you make for your own characters and items. Background: First person system.

Where to find the settings:

  • Pawn without a visual override (UEFN mannequin): the pawn Blueprint's AC_FirstPersonRendering component.
  • Retargeted character: the visual override Blueprint's AC_FirstPersonRendering (for example BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny).

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text: You want Mode Classic shooter view with body and shadow FirstPersonOverlay The same, without weapons clipping into walls FirstPersonOverlaySplit (needs arms and body meshes) Immersive view of the real third-person animation TrueFirstPerson A skeleton with non-standard bone names TrueFirstPerson

docs.title: Set the meshes
docs.text:
1. First Person Full Meshes: add the body mesh first, then clothing and accessories. A headless body variant avoids seeing the inside of the head; without one, leave the list empty and the component reuses the third-person mesh with the head bone hidden.
  2. Materials: nothing to do. Material overrides are copied from the third-person component that uses the same mesh, or whose mesh name starts the first-person mesh name (SKM_Hero for SKM_Hero_FP).
  3. Third Person Mesh Name: the name of the body component you copy from.

docs.title: Split meshes
docs.text:
FirstPersonOverlaySplit needs an arms mesh (arms and hands, cut at the clavicles) and a body mesh without arms, neck and head. Author them in your DCC tool (keep a small overlap at the shoulders), or generate a first version:

  1. Duplicate your body mesh twice: SKM_Hero_FP_Arms and SKM_Hero_FP_NoArms.
  2. Open /GASPALS/Systems/FirstPersonSystem/Tools/EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh and set Source Mesh, Arms Target and Body Target in its class defaults.
  3. Right-click the utility in the Content Browser > Run Editor Utility Blueprint.
  4. Put the results in First Person Arms Meshes and First Person Body Meshes.

Warning

The utility overwrites the target meshes. Never point it at meshes you authored by hand.

docs.title: Place the camera at the eyes
docs.text:
The camera sits on the head bone plus First Person Eye Offset. On the UEFN mannequin the head bone is at the eyes (offset 0); on UE5 mannequins and MetaHumans it is at the base of the skull, so the shipped characters use (0, 12, 0): 12 cm forward.

  1. Play, switch to first person, and look straight ahead, then fully down.
  2. If you see the inside of the head or the chest, increase Y (forward). If the view is too high or too low, change Z. X moves the camera sideways.
  3. Equip the rifle and aim. The sights should line up with the screen center. The ADS hand targets use the same offset, so fixing the eye position also fixes the sights.

docs.title: Tune the look-down behavior
docs.text: Setting Effect First Person Arm Pitch Down Limit (45) How far the arms follow the view down before the spine leans. Lower values lean more. First Person Arm Pitch Up Limit (90) The same looking up. First Person Camera Follow Lean (0.75) 1: the camera moves forward with the leaning head. 0: the camera stays, the body moves back.

docs.title: Give an item first-person poses
docs.text:
Items without a first-person overlay show their third-person overlay in first person. To add one:

  1. Duplicate ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_Rifle (/GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/FirstPerson/Rifle), name it ABP_OverlayFirstPerson_<Item>.
  2. In its class defaults, set the pose animations (Stand Relax, Ready, Aim... like the third-person overlay; see Add an overlay state) and their curve maps. Keep the first-person curves: enable_cr_fp_stable_arms, enable_cr_fp_stable_head, enable_cr_fp_ads, enable_cr_fp_aimoffset, and enable_handik_l or enable_handik_r for the support hand.
  3. Set it as Overlay Pose FP in the item's data asset (DA_Equipment_<Item>).
  4. Make sure the item mesh has an ADS socket (the sight point) and a HandIK socket (support hand).

docs.title: Turn first person off
docs.text: Remove FirstPerson from Allowed Perspectives on each pawn's AC_CameraSystem (see Limit the perspectives). The first-person meshes are then never built. To strip it completely, also delete AC_FirstPersonRendering from the pawns and the retargeted characters.

docs.title: First person only
docs.text: Set Allowed Perspectives to FirstPerson only. The game starts in first person and the perspective input does nothing. Cover then never switches to third person: set First Person Sticky Cover to Disabled, or leave it, it acts the same.

docs.title: Add or rebind inputs
docs.text: GASPALS uses Enhanced Input. When a player possesses a pawn, the pawn adds the mapping contexts listed in its Input Mapping Contexts setting (default: IMC_Sandbox at priority 0). The systems listen to input actions (IA_*), not keys, so rebinding is a matter of editing mappings.

docs.title: Rebind a key
docs.text: Open /GASPALS/Input/Mappings/IMC_Sandbox, find the action, and change its key. For example, move the cover button from Q to F. Save; the change applies at the next Play.

docs.title: Add gamepad bindings
docs.text:
A few actions have no gamepad key in IMC_Sandbox: IA_Cover, IA_Equipment, IA_Overlay_Pose, IA_Overlay_Body, IA_Camera_Perspective, IA_Camera_Style, IA_Takedown. Add a mapping for each with the buttons you want, for example the right stick click for cover (then move Switch Shoulder elsewhere).

Note

The Z key is hard-wired to the Mover pawn's debug flying toggle (keyboard only; it does not use a gamepad button). Turn Enable Debug Tools off on the pawn's AC_DebugTools, or remove that node from the Mover pawn's Event Graph (an Input Key node for Z), before shipping. See Debug tools.

docs.title: Use your own mapping context
docs.text:
1. Create your context and map the GASPALS input actions (copy IMC_Sandbox to start).
  2. Open each pawn's Class Defaults and, under GASPALS > Input, replace IMC_Sandbox in Input Mapping Contexts with yours. No graph edit is needed.

Add more contexts as more entries of the map, with a higher priority for contexts that should win on shared keys (for example a gamepad-only context). An empty map leaves the player without controls and shows an on-screen warning.

docs.title: Who handles which action
docs.text:
Handled by Actions The pawn Move, look, sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch, jump, cover PC_Sandbox Next pawn, next character, teleport (through AC_DebugTools on the Mover pawn) AC_CameraSystem Perspective, style, shoulder AC_EquipmentSystem Equipment menu, menu next / previous AC_OverlaySystem Overlay pose and body menus, menu next / previous AC_RagdollSystem Ragdoll (CMC pawn) AC_SmartObjectAnimation Interact (benches) SandboxCharacter_Mover Ragdoll, takedown, interact (shove), jump (get up), debug fly (Z); with aim held, takedown and interact call AC_DebugTools (demo shot, spawn / rotate)

Components bind their own input actions, so they receive input only when their pawn is player controlled and a context maps the action. The full list is in Input actions.

docs.title: Add an input to a system
docs.text:
Example: a button that leaves cover at once.

  1. Create an input action IA_LeaveCover (Digital, bool) in /GASPALS/Input.
  2. Map it in IMC_Sandbox.
  3. In the pawn's Event Graph, add the IA_LeaveCover event and, on Started, call AC_CoverSystem > ExitCover.
  4. On the Mover pawn, remember that movement goes through the input command: changes that affect movement should be read in ProduceInput rather than applied directly.

docs.title: Unused input assets
docs.text: IMC_Sandbox is the only mapping context in /GASPALS/Input/Mappings. Traversal runs from IA_Jump; there is no separate traverse action. IA_TwinStick_AimDirection is read by the Mover pawn's twin-stick mode but not mapped.

docs.title: Add an overlay state
docs.text:
An overlay state is an Anim Blueprint that provides a pose for the overlay layer. This tutorial covers three cases:

  1. Look at the Injured stance (a complete stance overlay that ships with the plugin): the quickest way to learn the pose Anim Blueprint.
  2. Add a new stance to the overlay pose menu (for example Wounded Arm).
  3. Add a body style to the overlay body menu.

For an item pose (something held, spawned by the equipment system), see Add an equipment item; the pose Anim Blueprint part is the same as here.

Background: Overlay system.

docs.title: The pose Anim Blueprint in short
docs.text:
Every pose overlay is a child of ABP_OverlayPose_Base with only class defaults set:

  • Pose variables (Stand_Relax_Idle, Stand_Ready_Walk, Crouch_Aim_Move...): each an animation plus a curve map.
  • Can Aim: whether the Ready and Aiming states are used.
  • Aim sweeps (Stand_Aim_Sweep, Crouch_Aim_Sweep) for items that aim.
  • Aim Sweep Interp Speed Local / Remote: 30 / 10.

Poses are usually single-frame animations of the upper body holding the pose. The curve map says which body parts take the pose (see Curves).

docs.title: 1. Look at the Injured stance
docs.text:
ABP_Overlay_Injured (one hand held to the side) and ABP_Overlay_HandsTied (hands behind the back) are complete stance overlays. Open one to see how a stance is set up:

  1. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Injured/ABP_Overlay_Injured and go to Class Defaults.
  2. Under Overlay > Poses > Stand, Stand Relax Idle has its Overlay Pose set to Pose_Injured_Stand, and so do Stand Relax Walk, Stand Relax Run and Stand Relax Sprint (one pose can serve every speed).
  3. Under Poses > Crouch, Crouch Relax Idle and Crouch Relax Move use Pose_Injured_Crouch.

  4. Each Curve Map uses the same values as the Box poses in ABP_Overlay_Box. For a stance of your own that takes the whole upper body, start with:

    Curve Value layering_spine 1 layering_head 1 layering_arm_l, layering_arm_r 1 layering_hand_l, layering_hand_r 1 layering_arm_l_ls, layering_arm_r_ls 1 layering_pelvis, layering_legs 0 (keep the locomotion legs) or up to 1 for a limp layering_spine_add, layering_head_add, layering_arm_l_add, layering_arm_r_add 0.5 (keep some motion)

    The quickest way: copy the curve map from a Box pose in ABP_Overlay_Box (right-click the field > Copy, then Paste on yours) and adjust. 5. Can Aim is off: the stance never goes to Ready or Aiming. 6. ABP_Overlay_HandsTied is set up the same way with Pose_HandsTied_*. 7. Test: Play, hold V, pick Injured. Walk, run, crouch. To experiment, adjust the curves: lower layering_spine_add to make the torso stiffer, raise layering_legs to bring the pose's legs in.

Starting stance

Set Overlay Pose on the pawn's AC_OverlaySystem to start in a stance. It shows while nothing is held; an equipped item's pose replaces it, and it comes back when the item is put away.

docs.title: 2. Add a new stance
docs.text:
1. Animations. Author the stance poses (standing and crouched) on the UEFN mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Meshes/SK_UEFN_Mannequin), or author them on your own skeleton and retarget them to the UEFN mannequin with an IK Retargeter (Export Animations in the retargeter). Single-frame animations are enough.
  2. Anim Blueprint. Duplicate ABP_Overlay_Injured (a complete example, see step 1) into a new folder, for example OverlayPose/WoundedArm/ABP_Overlay_WoundedArm, and set your poses and curves.
  3. Enum. Open /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayPose/Enum_OverlayPose and add an enumerator, WoundedArm. The menu picks it up automatically.
  4. Link it. Open AC_OverlaySystem (or select the component on each pawn) and add a row to Overlay Pose Layers: WoundedArm > ABP_Overlay_WoundedArm. No graph edit. Compile and save. If the pawn's component already overrides the map, add the row there too.
  5. Test on both pawns (N), with a listen server client.

Stances and items share the layer

A stance from the overlay menu and an item from the equipment menu both link the same overlay pose layer, and the last one wins. If a stance must combine with items (an injured character holding a pistol), make it an item pose instead: an equipment data asset with the stance poses.

docs.title: 3. Add a body style
docs.text:
1. Duplicate /GASPALS/Systems/OverlaySystem/OverlayBody/Feminine/ABP_OverlayBody_Feminine and name it, for example, ABP_OverlayBody_Heavy.
  2. In its class defaults, set Pose Stand Idle, Pose Stand Move, Pose Crouch Idle and Pose Crouch Move.
  3. Add an enumerator to OverlayBody/Enum_OverlayBody.
  4. Add a row to Overlay Body Layers on AC_OverlaySystem: your enumerator > ABP_OverlayBody_Heavy.
  5. Test with B.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Ready and aim poses for items: hold the weapon raised (Ready) and at the eye (Aim). Set Can Aim on. The state machine uses Ready after aiming and drops to Relaxed after a few seconds.
  • Hand IK: set enable_handik_l (or _r) to 1 in the poses where the support hand holds the item, and add a HandIK socket on the item.
  • New settings on the base: if you add a variable to ABP_OverlayPose_Base, existing children keep their own class defaults (empty or 0). Set the value on every child.
  • Authoring curves in animations instead of curve maps: apply the Create_LayeringCurves animation modifier (OverlaySystem/AnimModifiers) to your pose animations and edit the keys.

docs.title: Add the systems to your own pawn
Add the systems to your own pawn
docs.text:
The simplest path is a child Blueprint of a sample pawn (Use GASPALS in your own project). This page is for when you need your own pawn class, for example to add GASPALS to an existing character. It lists every connection the sample pawns make. Open SandboxCharacter_CMC or SandboxCharacter_Mover next to your pawn and copy the graphs as you go.

Background: Architecture.

docs.title: 1. Base class and movement
docs.text:
Character (CMC)Pawn with Mover

Parent class Character. Copy the sample's Character Movement settings (CharMoveComp: max acceleration 500, braking deceleration 500, braking friction factor 0, crouched half height 60, use controller desired rotation, rotation rate yaw -1).

Parent class Pawn, with a CharacterMoverComponent named CharacterMover: copy its Movement Modes, Transitions (BP_MovementTransition_Cover), Shared Settings (legacy movement and stance settings) and Sync Inputs For Sim Proxy. Add a NavMoverComponent for AI. Turn off Replicate Movement on the pawn (Mover replicates itself), and implement MoverInputProducerInterface (see Cover).

Capsule: half height 86. The Mover sample uses the CharacterCapsule collision profile (ignores Visibility and Camera) so camera and visibility traces pass through characters.

docs.title: 2. Components
docs.text: Component Notes Third-person Skeletal Mesh SKM_UEFN_Mannequin with SandboxCharacter_Mover_ABP or SandboxCharacter_CMC_ABP, location (0, 0, -88), yaw -90, component tag ThirdPersonRendering. SkeletalMesh_FP (Skeletal Mesh, child of the mesh) SKM_UEFN_Mannequin_FP_Arms with ABP_FirstPerson_UEFN; Only Owner See, Owner No See, no shadow, First Person Primitive Type FirstPerson. The first-person logic mesh. VisualOverride (Child Actor, child of the mesh) Component tag VisualOverride, Set Owner on. GameplayCamera (Gameplay Camera, child of the mesh, socket root) Camera asset CameraAsset_SandboxCharacter, Auto Activate off, absolute rotation. MotionWarping For traversal. AC_CameraSystem, AC_EquipmentSystem, AC_OverlaySystem, AC_FirstPersonRendering, AC_TraversalLogic, AC_TraversalTracer, AC_VisualOverrideManager The systems. AC_CoverSystem_CMC or AC_CoverSystem_Mover Name it AC_CoverSystem. AC_RagdollSystem, AC_PreCMCTick Character only. AC_SmartObjectAnimation, AC_FoleyEvents Optional: benches, foley sounds. PhysicsControl, AC_PostABPTick Mover only, for the physics ragdoll and takedowns. Copying these means copying the ragdoll logic of SandboxCharacter_Mover too; a child Blueprint of it is simpler. AC_DebugTools Optional, Mover only: demo shot, spawn / rotate, teleport, fly. It works only on SandboxCharacter_Mover and its children (Debug tools).

docs.title: Component settings
docs.text:
Set these on your pawn's components (class defaults do not reach existing component templates):

Component Setting AC_CoverSystem Enable Cover on (the class default, so a new component already has it; the sample pawns also set it). AC_TraversalLogic Is Mover Character on for Mover pawns. AC_FirstPersonRendering Third Person Mesh Name = your mesh component's name; the three first-person mesh lists (copy from the sample). AC_EquipmentSystem, AC_OverlaySystem, AC_VisualOverrideManager, AC_CameraSystem, AC_TraversalLogic Component Replicates on.

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text: Add both interfaces in Class Settings > Implemented Interfaces.

docs.title: BPI_SandboxCharacter_Pawn
docs.text:
Function Return Required by Get_PropertiesForAnimation S_CharacterPropertiesForAnimation Character, overlay and first-person Anim Blueprints, cover Get_PropertiesForCamera S_CharacterPropertiesForCamera Camera director Get_PropertiesForTraversal S_CharacterPropertiesForTraversal Traversal Set_CharacterInputState (sets the input state) AI StateTree tasks Get_PropertiesForRagdoll, Get_MMIResult, Get_MMIAnimContexts ragdoll and interaction data Mover Anim Blueprint (ragdoll and takedowns) AddTarget, RemoveTarget Target dummy (optional)

Copy the implementations from the sample pawn: they read your movement component and the system components.

docs.title: BPI_ModularSystems
docs.text:
Implement the event InitializeModularSystems with the initialization chain, in this order:

  1. UpdateFirstPersonVisuals: pick the active AC_FirstPersonRendering (the visual override's, else yours), call ConnectLogicMesh(SkeletalMesh_FP) and BuildFirstPersonMeshes. Copy the function and GetVisualMeshes from the sample.
  2. AC_OverlaySystem.InitializeSystem(third-person mesh).
  3. AC_EquipmentSystem.InitializeSystem(self, third-person mesh, SkeletalMesh_FP, visual TP mesh, visual FP mesh) with the visual meshes from GetVisualMeshes.
  4. AC_CameraSystem.InitializeSystem(self, visual TP mesh, visual FP mesh, GameplayCamera).
  5. Character only: AC_RagdollSystem.InitializeSystem(self, mesh, capsule).
  6. AC_FirstPersonRendering.InitializePrimitives.
  7. AC_CoverSystem.InitializeSystem(self), then bind AC_CoverSystem.OnCoverVaultReady to your traversal call (see Traversal).

The event runs again when the visible character changes: keep it safe to call more than once.

docs.title: 4. Startup
docs.text: When Do BeginPlay Mover: the mesh ticks after CharacterMover and after the actor. Character: CharacterMovement ticks after AC_PreCMCTick, and bind AC_PreCMCTick's Tick to your pre-movement event. Then call InitializeModularSystems (on self). Possessed (server) Call a Client RPC on the owner that runs SetupCamera and SetupInput. Character: also AC_PreCMCTick.AddTickPrerequisiteActor(Controller). SetupCamera If DDCVar.NewGameplayCameraSystem.Enable: GameplayCamera.ActivateCameraForPlayerController(PC, true). SetupInput For each entry of an Input Mapping Contexts map (context > priority, default IMC_Sandbox at 0): Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem > Add Mapping Context. Copy the sample pawn's function.

docs.title: 5. Input
docs.text: Handle in the pawn: move, look, sprint, walk, strafe, aim, crouch, jump, cover. The other actions are handled by the components and the controller (see Add or rebind inputs). Replicate the input state with a Server RPC that sets a replicated S_PlayerInputState (the CMC sample replicates it skipping the owner).

docs.title: Cover
docs.text:
Character (CMC)Pawn with Mover

In the pre-movement event (from AC_PreCMCTick), first call AC_CoverSystem.UpdateCoverCMC(DeltaSeconds), then your rotation and speed updates. In cover, use the walk gait (sprint during a cover run).

In ProduceInput:

  1. RemapCoverMoveInput(move input) before setting the directional input.
  2. EvaluateCover(move input, delta seconds) after it; add its S_MoverCustomInputs_Cover output to the input collection.
  3. Crouch request = (wants to crouch or the cover's force crouch) and not IsCoverCrouchBlocked.
  4. Gait: walk in cover unless crouched, sprint during a cover run. Rotation offset 0 in cover.
  5. Orientation intent from GetCoverOrientationIntent.

Register BP_MovementMode_Cover as Cover, add BP_MovementTransition_Cover to the global transitions, map Cover to on-ground in your movement mode map, and tick UpdateMoverCoverState and UpdateCoverVault.

Both: IA_Cover Started calls RequestStickyCover; Completed and Canceled call ReleaseStickyCover.

docs.title: Traversal
docs.text:
Implement GetTraversalCheckInputs (copy from the sample) and on jump:

  1. If a traversal is possible (not already traversing; Mover: no montage playing), call AC_CoverSystem.RequestCoverVault.
  2. If it is not deferred, call AC_TraversalLogic.TryTraversalAction(GetTraversalCheckInputs, ...).
  3. If the traversal check or montage selection failed, jump.

OnCoverVaultReady (bound during initialization) calls TryTraversalAction when the character has turned to the wall.

docs.title: 6. Test
docs.text: Run through the Quick start on your pawn: locomotion, traversal, cover (soft, sticky, run, corner, aim, vault), equipment in third and first person, overlays, perspectives, characters (M), and a listen server with a client.

docs.title: Use GASPALS in your own project
Use GASPALS in your own project
docs.text:
There are two ways to start:

Start from When The template project (rename it) A new game. Everything is configured. Your project + the plugin An existing project. Follow Installation, option B first.

Then make GASPALS yours without editing more of the plugin than needed.

docs.title: 1. Create your own game mode
docs.text:
Create a Blueprint child of /GASPALS/Blueprints/GM_Sandbox, for example GM_MyGame, in your project's content.

Setting (class defaults) Value Default Pawn Class Your pawn (step 2), or a sample pawn. Pawn Classes Soft The pawns N cycles through; empty it to disable switching. Visual Overrides Soft The characters M cycles through (and DDCvar.VisualOverride indexes). Player Controller Class PC_Sandbox or a child of it.

Deriving from GM_Sandbox matters: the visual override manager reads its character list from it.

Note

GM_Sandbox picks the pawn from DDCvar.PawnClass (-1 = Default Pawn Class). If your game should always use the Default Pawn Class, keep the variable at -1 and remove the N mapping.

docs.title: 2. Create your pawn
docs.text:
Make a child Blueprint of SandboxCharacter_CMC or SandboxCharacter_Mover (see Mover and CMC pawns to choose). A child keeps every system wired and lets you override what you need:

  • Tune the components (cover, camera, first person) on your child's component templates.
  • Override pawn functions (Get_PropertiesForCamera, GetTraversalCheckInputs...) for different behavior.
  • Add your gameplay: health, abilities, weapons firing.

Your own character mesh goes in as a visual override (see Add a retargeted character); keep the UEFN mannequin on the pawn as the animation source.

To build a pawn from scratch instead, see Add the systems to your own pawn.

docs.title: 3. Set up your levels
docs.text:
For each level, in World Settings > GameMode Override, pick GM_MyGame. Or set it once in Project Settings > Maps & Modes > Default GameMode.

Each level needs:

  • a Player Start;
  • a NavMeshBoundsVolume for cover runs and AI;
  • traversable obstacles on the Traversable channel (Make objects traversable);
  • cover geometry that blocks Visibility (Set up cover in a level).

Set your maps in Project Settings > Maps & Modes (Game Default Map, Editor Startup Map).

docs.title: 4. Remove demo features
docs.text: Demo feature How to remove Pawn switching (N), character switching (M), teleport (J) Remove IA_NextPawn, IA_NextVisualOverride, IA_TeleportToTarget from your mapping context. Equipment and overlay menus (time dilation) Remove the menu actions from the mapping context, and call SelectNewEquipment / overlay selection from your gameplay. Mover debug tools: demo shooting and spawning (aim + Left Button / E), debug flying (Z) Turn off Enable Debug Tools on the Mover pawn's AC_DebugTools component, or remove the component and its calls (the aim branches of IA_Takedown and IA_Interact, the Input Key node for Z). See Debug tools. On-screen debug prints The camera perspective change prints its name; remove the Print String in AC_CameraSystem.

docs.title: 5. Keep upgrades manageable
docs.text:
• Put your assets in your project's content, not in Plugins/GASPALS.
  • Prefer child Blueprints and new data assets over editing the plugin's assets.
  • When you must edit a plugin asset, note it: you will merge it by hand when updating GASPALS.

docs.title: 6. Package
docs.text:
1. Add your maps to Project Settings > Packaging > List of maps to include.
  2. Keep the packaging settings from Installation.
  3. Install a C++ toolchain (Visual Studio 2022 on Windows): the engine plugins GASPALS needs make the packaging tool build a game target.
  4. Platforms > Windows > Package Project.

The demo's Game Animation Widget, Controls and Read Me panels are editor utility widgets: they do not exist in a packaged game.

docs.title: Add a retargeted character
docs.text:
This tutorial puts your own character on the GASPALS pawns. The pawns keep animating the UEFN mannequin; your character copies that animation through an IK Retargeter. Read Characters and visual overrides first if you want the background.

You need: a skeletal mesh with its skeleton and physics asset imported into the project. Time: 30 to 60 minutes, most of it spent on the retarget pose.

Fast path for UE5 mannequin and MetaHuman skeletons

If your character uses the UE5 mannequin skeleton (SK_Mannequin) or a MetaHuman body skeleton, the IK Rig, the retargeter, the VB Camera bone and the equipment sockets already exist. Skip to step 5 and use ABP_Retarget_UE5 or ABP_Retarget_Kellan as they are.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the skeleton
docs.text:
Open your character's Skeleton asset.

  1. Virtual bone. Right-click the root bone > Add Virtual Bone > pick head. Rename the new bone (VB root_head) to VB Camera, exactly. The first-person camera attaches to it.
  2. Check the bone names. The systems need root, pelvis, head, hand_l and hand_r. The first-person overlay modes also need spine_01 to spine_05, clavicle_l, clavicle_r and neck_01. If your skeleton names them differently, plan on the TrueFirstPerson mode (step 6) or rename the bones in your DCC tool.
  3. Equipment sockets. Equipment attaches to sockets on the skeleton. Open SK_Mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UE5_Mannequins/Meshes), select the seven sockets overlay_rifle, overlay_pistol, overlay_bow, overlay_box, overlay_barrel, overlay_binoculars and overlay_torch, right-click > Copy Selected Sockets, then in your skeleton right-click the matching hand bone > Paste Selected Sockets. On SK_Mannequin they hang from hand_r (rifle, pistol, binoculars, box) and hand_l (bow, torch, barrel).
  4. Save the skeleton.

You will fine-tune the socket transforms in step 8, with the items in hand.

docs.title: 2. Create the IK Rig
docs.text:
Content Browser > right-click > Animation > Retargeting > IK Rig, pick your skeletal mesh. Then:

  1. Set the Retarget Root to pelvis.
  2. Click Auto Create Retarget Chains (or add them by hand). Use the standard names: Root, Spine, Neck, Head, LeftClavicle, LeftArm, LeftLeg, finger chains, and the right-side mirrors.
  3. Add IK goals on the hands and feet (LeftHandIK, RightHandIK, LeftFootIK, RightFootIK) and assign them to the arm and leg chains.

Similar skeletons can start from a duplicate of IK_UE5_Mannequin_Retarget (/GASPALS/Characters/UE5_Mannequins/Rigs) or IK_Metahuman_Retarget (/GASPALS/MetaHumans/Common/Rigs).

docs.title: 3. Create the IK Retargeter
docs.text:
Right-click > Animation > Retargeting > IK Retargeter.

  1. Source IK Rig: IK_UEFN_Mannequin (/GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Rigs). Target IK Rig: the rig from step 2.
  2. In the chain mapping, use Auto-Map Chains and check every chain.
  3. Retarget pose: edit the target's retarget pose until the arms, hands and fingers match the UEFN mannequin's pose in the viewport. This is the step that decides the quality of the result.
  4. Op stack: keep the default ops (pelvis motion, FK chains, IK). Make sure there is a Curve Remap op with Copy All Source Curves on: the hand IK weights travel as curves. The shipped retargeters have no Root Motion op.
  5. Preview a few animations from /GASPALS/Characters/UEFN_Mannequin/Animations (idle, walk, a rifle pose) and fix feet, hands and pelvis.

The same retargeter is used twice: for the third-person pose and for the first-person overlays.

docs.title: 4. Create the retarget Anim Blueprint
docs.text:
1. Duplicate ABP_Retarget_UE5 (/GASPALS/Blueprints/RetargetedCharacters) and name it, for example, ABP_Retarget_MyHero.
  2. Open it and change its target skeleton to yours (Asset > Retarget to a different skeleton, or in the Class Settings).
  3. Select the Retarget Pose From Mesh node and set IK Retargeter Asset to your retargeter. Leave Retarget From on Parent Skeletal Mesh Component and the source pose pin unconnected.
  4. Keep the CR_Humanoid_HandIK node after it, and keep the Event Graph, which finds the pawn's equipment component for the hand IK targets.
  5. Compile and save.

docs.title: 5. Create the character Blueprint
docs.text:
Duplicate BP_RetargetedCharacter_Manny (quickest: every setting is already there) or create a child Blueprint of BP_RetargetedCharacter_Base. Name it, for example, BP_RetargetedCharacter_MyHero.

  1. Select the inherited SkeletalMesh component:
    • Skeletal Mesh Asset: your mesh.
    • Anim Class: your retarget Anim Blueprint (ABP_Retarget_UE5 for the UE5 mannequin skeleton, ABP_Retarget_Kellan for MetaHumans).
    • Keep its component tag ThirdPersonRendering and Visibility Based Anim Tick Option = Only Tick Pose When Rendered.
  2. Clothing, hair, accessories: add them as children of SkeletalMesh, each with the component tag ThirdPersonRendering.
    • Same skeleton and no post-process Anim Blueprint: use Leader Pose (Kellan's construction script function EnableMasterPose shows how).
    • Own skeleton with a post-process Anim Blueprint that copies the pose from the parent (typical for MetaHuman clothing): leave the anim class empty.
  3. Keep SkeletalMesh as the first child of Root. The base class makes the first child tick after the pawn mesh, which keeps the pose in sync.

docs.title: 6. Set up first person
docs.text:
Select the inherited AC_FirstPersonRendering component (categories FirstPerson > General for the mode, FirstPerson > Camera for the eye offset, FirstPerson > Setup for the rest):

Setting Value First Person Mode FirstPersonOverlay (default). Use TrueFirstPerson if your skeleton lacks the UE-standard spine names. First Person Full Meshes Your body mesh first (it becomes the lead), then the clothing. Prefer a headless body; leave empty to reuse the third-person mesh with the head bone hidden. First Person Arms Meshes / Body Meshes Only for FirstPersonOverlaySplit. Generate them with EUB_SplitFirstPersonMesh (see Configure first person). Third Person Mesh Name SkeletalMesh (keep it unless you renamed the body component). First Person Retargeter Your IK Retargeter. Required for the overlay modes on any skeleton other than UEFN. First Person Eye Offset Start with (0, 12, 0) (what Manny, Quinn and Kellan use): 12 cm forward of the head bone. Tune it in step 8.

docs.title: 7. Register the character
docs.text:
Open /GASPALS/Blueprints/GM_Sandbox, Class Defaults, and add your Blueprint to Visual Overrides Soft. Its position in the array is its index (0 = first).

If you use your own game mode, derive it from GM_Sandbox so the manager finds the list.

docs.title: 8. Test and tune
docs.text:
1. Play. Press M until your character shows, or open the console (`) and type DDCvar.VisualOverride <index>.
  2. Third person: walk, run, crouch, jump, vault. Watch the feet (sliding means a chain or retarget pose problem) and the hands.
  3. Equipment: press T, pick the rifle, then the pistol and the bow. If an item floats or sits in the wrong place, open your skeleton, select the overlay_* socket, right-click > Add Preview Asset with the item's mesh (/GASPALS/Systems/EquipmentSystem/Assets/Meshes) and adjust the socket.
  4. First person: switch the camera to first person. Look down, aim (Right Button), run. If the camera sits inside the head or in front of the face, adjust First Person Eye Offset (X right, Y forward, Z up, in cm, in the head's reference pose). Aim with the rifle and check that the sights line up.
  5. Warnings: orange messages starting with GASPALS First Person (...) list missing setup (no first-person camera bone, no head bone, missing retargeter...). See Troubleshooting.
  6. Press N to switch to the other pawn and test again. For multiplayer, run a listen server with a client.

docs.title: 9. Make it the default character
docs.text:
Project Settings > Engine > Data Driven CVars: set the default value of DDCvar.VisualOverride to your index. Every pawn then starts with your character, and M toggles back to the UEFN mannequin. To stop players from cycling, remove the M mapping of IA_NextVisualOverride from the input mapping contexts, or keep only your entry in the list. For one pawn only, or with your own game mode, set Default Visual Override on that pawn's AC_VisualOverrideManager and turn Follow Global Visual Override off (see Characters).

Keep the UEFN mannequin on the pawn

Do not replace the pawn's own mesh with your character. The character Anim Blueprints, overlay poses, traversal montages and Control Rigs expect the UEFN skeleton; your character gets all of it through the retargeter.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• Skeleton: VB Camera virtual bone, root/head/hand_l/hand_r, seven overlay_* sockets
  • IK Rig with standard chains and a pelvis retarget root
  • IK Retargeter from IK_UEFN_Mannequin, retarget pose matched, Curve Remap op
  • Retarget Anim Blueprint with your retargeter
  • Character Blueprint: body mesh and anim class, clothing tagged ThirdPersonRendering
  • AC_FirstPersonRendering: meshes, retargeter, eye offset
  • Added to GM_Sandbox > Visual Overrides Soft
  • Tested: locomotion, equipment, first person, both pawns, listen server

docs.title: Make objects traversable
docs.text: Traversal only considers geometry that blocks the Traversable trace channel. Everything else is jumped. Background: Traversal system.

docs.title: Option 1: use the grey-box block
docs.text: Place /GASPALS/Levels/LevelPrototyping/LevelBlock_Traversable and scale it. It is already set up, and is what the demo levels use.

docs.title: Option 2: set the collision preset
docs.text: Select the static mesh actor (or component) and, under Collision, set Collision Presets to TraversalObjectPreset. It blocks everything, including Traversable.

docs.title: Option 3: custom collision
docs.text:
Keep your preset, choose Custom..., and set the Traversable response (under Trace Responses) to Block. Do this in the static mesh asset's default collision to make every placement traversable.

For Blueprint actors, set it on the mesh components in the Blueprint.

docs.title: Shapes that work
docs.text:
Obstacle Typical result Low and thin (a fence, a low wall) Hurdle or vault, depending on speed and what is behind it. Low and deep (a crate, a table) Vault or mantle up onto it. Chest height Mantle. Taller than the character can reach Jump. Narrower than 70 cm Jump (Min Ledge Width on AC_TraversalTracer).

Simple collision that matches the visible top edge gives the best results: the warp targets are placed on the measured ledge.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
1. Type DDCvar.Traversal.DrawDebugLevel 3 in the console during Play, then jump at the obstacle: the traces, ledges and room checks are drawn and the measured data is printed.
  2. Drop a BP_TraversalTester (/GASPALS/Systems/TraversalSystem) in front of the obstacle in the editor: it draws the tracer's result without playing. Its Initial Trace Distance sets how far it looks.
  3. show collision shows whether the obstacle's collision is what you expect.
Symptom Fix The character always jumps The obstacle does not block Traversable, or it is narrower than Min Ledge Width. The hands or feet miss the edge The collision top is not where the visible edge is. A traversal plays into a wall behind the obstacle The room check found space; add collision for the wall, or block Visibility on it.
